News.title: Dad, 56, was killed in ‘violent’ village street brawl sparked by a deadly turf war between rival biker gangs
News.content:
DEADLY BRAWL Dad, 56, was killed in ‘violent’ village street brawl sparked by a deadly turf war between rival biker gangs

A MASS brawl which left a man dead was sparked by a deadly turf war between the Hells Angels and a rival biker gang, The Sun can reveal.

One group was “tooled up” with machetes, axes, knives and hammers for the ambush at the HQ of its bitter rivals.



Witnesses described the “carnage” as more than 20 men attacked each other with weapons in the village of Pontnewynydd, near Pontypool, South Wales.

Anthony “Tony” Jones, 56, was killed, with an eyewitness account claiming he was found face down in an alleyway with a gaping wound in his head.



Two other men were taken to hospital for injuries caused in the running street battle which happened in front of a children’s play park around 6pm last Thursday.

Cops arrested 10 men and are asking another man, Anthony Paul Jones, 40, to hand himself in as they launched a murder investigation.

Locals said one of the gangs had duct-taped machetes to their wrists to prevent losing their grip in the bloodbath.

A driver who stopped to help said: “There were about 20 people with machetes, hammers and axes all beating hell out of each other.



“There was a crash between a car and a van and a group of people got out of the back and joined in.

“A man ran past with a machete Sellotaped to his hand and blood running down his face.”

The passer-by said a woman neighbour came out screaming there was a man badly hurt in the street.

He said: “He was lying face down.

“I pulled him over and his head was just open.



“He wasn’t breathing. I did CPR on him until the ambulance men came. They were trying to zap him but there was nothing.

“It was carnage.”

The violence is believed to be part of a turf war between the Vikings Motorcycle Club and the Hells Angels.

Gwent Police senior investigating officer, detective superintendent Laura Bartley said: “We believe the violent disorder involved members of two rival Outlaw Motorcycle Clubs, the Vikings and the Hells Angels.

“Establishing the extent of involvement of those connected to the incident remains a key focus of the investigation.



“Our thoughts remain with the family of the victim, who continue to be supported by specially trained officers.

Ten men, aged 73, 61, 59, 45, 40, 40, 39, 34, 33, and 31 were arrested in connection with the fracas opposite slides and swings where children had been playing.

Three men have been freed on bail.

Police launched a manhunt for alleged gang member Anthony Paul Jones, 40, from Blaenavon, Gwent, saying he “may be able to assist with inquiries”.

They are also looking for a damaged blue Ford Transit van, registration MA23 FLC, which drove into the riot before armed men burst out the back doors.



Firearms officers, a police helicopter and a fleet of ambulances were called to the scene outside the British Legion Club at 7.15pm last Thursday evening.

A large cordon continued to be in place yesterday(Tues) as forensic officers scoured the scene for evidence.

More than 5,000 people have been “cut off” due to prolonged road closures which are set to be in place until the weekend.

Locals said an innocent cyclist had a lucky escape when he rode into the middle of the riot and was mistaken for a gang member.

A father-of-three who lives 200 yards from the battle ground said: “I was walking my dogs when I heard a woman screaming down the phone calling for help.



“The next minute there were police everywhere and a helicopter was trying to land. It was chaotic, there was blood on the streets and men lying injured.”

Another local, a 41-year-old family man, said: “There’s some sort of rivalry between these two Welsh gangs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It’s pathetic, they are grown men. One of the men arrested is in his seventies, he should know better.

“It’s ended up with a man being murdered right opposite the children’s playground. This violence has to stop.”

News.title: Woman dies at popular festival after being found unconscious in tent as cops probe mystery passing
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FESTIVAL HORROR Woman dies at popular festival after being found unconscious in tent as cops probe mystery passing

A WOMAN has died on the final day of a popular techno music festival.

The death was reported at around 6.10pm on Sunday at the Houghton Festival in Norfolk.



Cops were called to the scene after the woman was found unconscious in her tent.

Despite the best efforts by paramedics, she was sadly pronounced dead.



Police said the death is currently being treated as unexplained but it is not thought to be suspicious.

The woman’s next of kin have been informed as enquiries continue.

A spokesperson for Houghton Festival said: “We are deeply saddened to confirm that a person has passed away at Houghton 2026.

“Our thoughts are entirely with their family and loved ones at this difficult time.

“We are grateful to our onsite medical team, event response team and Norfolk Constabulary, who all responded immediately.

“We continue to work closely with the relevant authorities to support in any way we can with their investigations.”



The yearly festival – which kicked off last Thursday – typically draws in around 10,000 people.

It has been running at the prestigious Houghton Hall estate since 2017.

Founded by dance music legend Craig Richards – who owns the renowned London nightclub Fabric – attendees can enjoy music across its stages all day and night, making it the UK’s only 24-hour festival.

The Princess of Wales is believed to have visited the techno rave back in 2023, while visiting friends the Marquess and Marchioness of Cholmondeley, David and Rose, who own the Norfolk estate.

She reportedly left staff at Houghton Hall a generous £700 after her stay.

News.title: Alligator launches ‘full speed’ attack & drags victim underwater as witnesses see ‘bones poking out & blood everywhere’
News.content:
ANIMAL HORROR Alligator launches ‘full speed’ attack & drags victim underwater as witnesses see ‘bones poking out & blood everywhere’

A QUICK-THINKING boater has been credited with saving a woman’s life after she was dragged underwater by a nearly 10-foot alligator.

The woman, who has not yet been identified, was with her family in Silver River, east of Ocala, Florida, on Saturday when the reptile launched a “full speed” attack, witnesses said.



The Florida woman fought back with a paddle after the 9-foot 8-inch alligator struck, but as she tried to fight it, it bit her arm.

John Gamache was eating lunch with his father on their boat near the scene when they heard the events unfold.



Gamache told Fox affiliate WOFL that he spotted the alligator approaching the group in the clear spring water.

“I looked just upriver from us a couple hundred feet and saw an alligator head way above the water and going full speed towards the swimmers,” he recalled.

By the time Gamache was able to reach the woman, the alligator had let go of her, and the sound of his boat had the reptile fleeing.

Gamache found the woman clinging to a paddleboard as several nearby swimmers appeared in distress.

“I noticed just a cloud of blood, and four or five swimmers panic,” he said.

“It did pull her under for awhile, and looking at the extent of her injury, there was a lot of action going on underwater.”



He rushed to help her after seeing the state of her injuries and used a rope to make a tourniquet on her bleeding and mangled arm.

“It was a terrible injury, bones poking out, blood everywhere,” he said.

“Obviously, the minutes mattered.”

Gamache and his father helped bring the other swimmers and children onto their boat before speeding off to a nearby boat launch.



First responders then rushed the woman to the hospital, and on Sunday, her family confirmed to WOFL that she was discharged.

The woman is now at home recovering after having her right arm amputated.

Her family has since reached out to Gamache to express their gratitude for his quick-thinking efforts.

“They called earlier and we talked for a while and it was heartwarming to hear them explain their emotions,” he said.



“We’re glad that it happened as good as it could have. Like the result is just the sustained injury and nothing more.”

Silver River closed temporarily after the attack as Marion County officials worked to remove the alligator.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The river was back open on Sunday.

Wildlife officials have urged anyone with concerns about an alligator sighting to contact the Nuisance Alligator Hotline at 866-392-4286.

News.title: Drunk driver who killed Brit mum on Turkey anniversary trip jailed for life as widower sobs ‘nothing can bring her back’
News.content:
A HUSBAND who tried to lift a car off his stricken wife when she was killed by a drunk driver in Turkey wept as her killer was sentenced to life with no parole on Tuesday.

Lisa’s Di Palma’s devastated husband cried: “Nothing can bring back the woman I loved more than life itself.”



Heartbroken Keith, 57, was on holiday with Lisa to celebrate their 36th wedding anniversary when she was hit by Turkish national Senay Koparal, 54, who was five times over the drink-drive limit.

The couple were walking on a pedestrian crossing on their way to enjoy a meal on the turquoise coastline in Fethiye, in southwestern Turkey, shortly after 7.30pm on August 6 last year.





After battling for her life in hospital, Lisa passed away.

Poignantly, August 13 will be the one-year anniversary of her death.

Witnesses said that Koparal attempted to flee the scene in the popular holiday resort but in doing so ran her over again as Keith desperately tried to push the car back with his bare hands.

The Sun can also reveal that Koparal had already been jailed for killing a man 17 years earlier—but had been released to kill again.



Speaking from Turkey last night, Keith and the couple’s two daughters, Charlotte, 32, and Danielle, 35, said they were relieved that “justice had been done.”

Keith, a lorry driver from Hornchurch, east London, added: “I am grateful that the truth was heard and that Lisa’s life was valued.

“But no verdict, no sentence will ever fill the empty space that Lisa has left behind. Koparal may have been handed a sentence today—but the true punishment falls on us, the family he destroyed.

“We are the ones who have to live every day without her.”

Keith described Koparal’s actions as “deliberate, cruel and unforgivable”.



He said: “He was drunk, driving at speed, and when he struck Lisa he did not stop.

“He drove over her, reversed, and drove over her again—all to try and escape.

“I saw her body go under the car. I shouted to my wife to tuck her head in because the tyres were going to go over her head.



“The front of the car went over her, the bonnet had gone over her, and I lost sight of her.

“That was not a mistake. That was murder.”

The beloved grandmother-of-four remained conscious and able to talk in the aftermath of the tragedy and was rushed to a local hospital before being transferred to Mugla Teaching and Research Hospital.

She had suffered bleeding in her lungs and brain, fractures to her pelvis, shoulders, and skull, 12 broken ribs, as well as signs of kidney failure and a burn on her leg from the car.

She died on August 13, having been moved to the Letoon Private Hospital for surgery.



Keith told how he and the couple’s daughters were prevented from saying goodbye to Lisa in the ward.

Instead, hospital staff “wheeled her out in a body bag” and unzipped it so they could see her for the last time.

Lisa’s cause of death was given as multiple injuries due to a road traffic collision.

Koparal, who showed no emotion as he was jailed for the rest of his life, was convicted of shooting and killing a 62-year-old farmer in June 2008.

He shot Yusuf Koyuncu in the head and chest in front of his horrified daughter and two daughters-in-law after the farmer stopped Koparal’s teenage sisters from picking thyme in his fields, according to Turkish news reports from the time.



After being jailed for that crime, he escaped in April 2017 and remained on the run for 16 months before he was recaptured.

It was unclear when he left prison, but Turkey released thousands of convicts on parole during the Covid-19 pandemic.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In a tribute to his wife following the sentence, Keith said: “My darling wife, my love, my life.

“I will love you until my last breath. You are and always will be my heart, my soul, and my world. Rest peacefully, my angel. We will never forget you.”

News.title: Why you can’t make your own solar eclipse glasses – the risks explained, and how to watch the eclipse safely
News.content:
WEDNESDAY promises the best solar eclipse the UK has seen so far this century, with up to 96% of the Sun disappearing behind the Moon.

If you haven’t got certified eclipse glasses (and many have struggled to source them), the temptation is to improvise, but don’t – getting it wrong could cause you permanent damage.



Can you make your own solar eclipse glasses?

You should never attempt to fabricate your own solar eclipse glasses.

Watching the eclipse with makeshift glasses made from household materials, or while wearing standard sunglasses, could lead to permanent injury.



Mohamed Elalfy, a consultant ophthalmologist and president of the Royal College of Ophthalmologists, said: “Looking directly at the Sun during a solar eclipse can cause damage to the retina, potentially damaging the cells responsible for sharp central vision.

“Crucially, the retina has no pain receptors, so people will not feel the damage as it happens.”

Solar retinopathy – the condition that occurs when light damages the retina – can leave blurred vision, distorted images, blind spots or permanent loss of central vision.

Symptoms may not appear for hours, Mr Elalfy added, and while some people recover, others will be left with permanent visual impairment.

Safe eye protection isn’t a DIY job – filters on eclipse glasses need to block harmful visible light, ultraviolet and infrared radiation.

And even very dark or expensive sunglasses transmit thousands of times too much sunlight to be safe – even if you wear several pairs at once.



Kyla Black, Boots Opticians director of optical practice, added: “It’s a common myth that wearing multiple pairs of sunglasses can protect you from any harmful UV light.

“This is untrue and should be avoided at all costs as only purpose-built eclipse glasses can allow you to watch an eclipse.”

How can you watch the eclipse safely?

For direct viewing, the only safe option is a a pair of glasses that genuinely meet the ISO 12312-2:2015 safety standard.

However, a printed ISO logo proves nothing on its own, as counterfeiters can copy them – so the Royal Astronomical Society (RAS) advises only buying from authorised sellers and verified manufacturers.



RAS president professor Jim Wild said: “I would encourage everyone to enjoy the spectacle safely.

“Never look directly at the Sun without appropriate solar viewing equipment.

“Certified eclipse glasses, specially designed solar filters for telescopes and binoculars, or indirect methods such as pinhole projectors are all safe ways to observe the event.

“With the right precautions, this eclipse promises to be an inspiring experience for seasoned astronomers and first-time skywatchers alike.”

Cmeras, telescopes and binoculars can be used, but only with a purpose-made solar filter secured over the front of the instrument.



If proper glasses are unavailable, the best alternative is to make an indirect viewer, such as a pinhole viewer.

Just punch a small, clean hole in one piece of card and use a second section of white card as a screen in your other hand or on the ground.

Then stand with your back to the Sun holding up the holed card above the screen, letting sunlight pass through it.

A small image of the Sun will appear clearly on the other white card when the distance between them has been adjusted accordingly, appearing as a crescent during this week’s partial eclipse.

Only watch the projected image – you should never turn around and look at the Sun either directly or through the hole.



There are other even simpler options, with the UK Health Security Agency advising that “you can watch the eclipse indirectly without any specialist equipment at all”.

It lists safe options including “viewing the Sun’s image projected through a colander or the gaps between tree leaves”.

Just like a pinhole projector, the colander method requires a sheet of white card or paper.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Hold it out or lay it on the ground, stand with your back to the Sun and position the colander so sunlight shines through its holes onto the card, and every hole will project a tiny crescent Sun.

The tree method requires nothing else – just stand under a leafy tree and look at the shadows on the ground, where the gaps between leaves act as natural pinholes.

News.title: More than one in four clash with others over what’s for dinner at least once a week, study finds
News.content:
DINNER WARS More than one in four clash with others over what’s for dinner at least once a week, study finds

MORE than one in four adults clash with others over what to have for dinner at least once a week, according to a study.

A poll of 2,000 adults found a quarter find it to be the most stressful decision of the day, with 55 per cent debating face-to-face and 26% using text or WhatsApp.



While nearly one in 10 even resort to social media conversations to decide the evening meal plan.

Of those who converse over text, an average of four messages are sent – with one in 20 sending at least 11 – before settling on what to eat.



The top sticking point was found to be one person ‘craving’ something different to the other (37% ), while 35% bemoaned repeating the same meals.

Others disagreed after one person claimed not to know what they wanted or claiming they ‘don’t mind’ (34%), someone not wanting to cook (30%) or trying to decide between homecooked or a takeaway (21%).

Jeremy Gibson, spokesperson for Napolina, which commissioned the research to launch its first Pasta Stir Ins, said: “By the time dinner comes around, many households have already spent the day making decisions.

“When you then add different tastes, tiredness, and a lack of inspiration, with ‘what’s for dinner’ it can become a difficult question.

“The research shows that people still want to enjoy a satisfying meal at home, but they do not always have the time or energy for a long recipe and lots of preparation.

“Having a quick way to bring flavour to the table is exactly what you need for those nights.”



The study found 37% of all adults find deciding what to have for dinner generally stressful, with a lack of inspiration and ideas the main reason for disliking the task (35%).

A third are put off by the effort required to cook while 31% struggle after a long day at work.

More than one in 10 (12% ) even went as far as to say they feel overwhelmed when it comes to deciding what to eat.

As a result, 48% admit they often default to a go-to, easy meal while 41% have even resorted to eating the same meal they had the night before.

The study, carried out via OnePoll, also revealed just 17% typically map out meals at the weekend, with 28% leaving it until the last-minute to decide their meal plans.



It also emerged only 14% of adults cook from scratch every day.

More than half of those who don’t (54%) are put off if a recipe takes too long, while 39% abandon the idea altogether when it involves too much preparation.

This is leaving 35% falling back on the same meals – with pasta (53%), curries (24%) and jacket potatoes (20%) topping the list.

On the whole, almost half (48%) just want something quick and easy when it comes to cooking during the week.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Jeremy added: “Convenience does not have to mean settling for something uninspiring or compromising on quality.



“Having a few simple options in the cupboard can help households escape the same-meal cycle and spend less time debating dinner and more time enjoying it with friends or family.”

News.title: Mum finds out fertility doctor is her child’s DAD & ‘fathered 9 other kids after using his own sperm instead of donors’
News.content:
'BETRAYAL OF TRUST' Mum finds out fertility doctor is her child’s DAD & ‘fathered 9 other kids after using his own sperm instead of donors’

A MUM was horrified to learn her fertility doctor is the real dad of her son, a bombshell lawsuit claims.

Mary Ellen Lukezick, 71, was promised a “healthy young medical student” would be the father of her child more than 40 years ago.



But she is now suing Dr Federick Dettmann, now 91, amid fears he used his own sperm for insemination of her son, who is now 43.

It comes after Mary’s son, Joseph Laedtka Heider, was shocked to find out he had nine half-siblings through an ancestry DNA result in December 2024.



Joseph said: “Words cannot fully express what it feels like to learn that your entire identity is built on a lie.”

According to NBC News, Mary was a patient of Dettmann in 1982 and after struggling some time with her fertility, he recommended she try artificial insemination.



In December 2024, Joseph submitted his DNA to Ancestry.com and made the shocking revelation that Dettmann was his biological father, the lawsuit alleges.

The suit said: “Upon tracing these DNA connections, Joseph identified a direct genetic link to Dr Dettman’s family; that upon information and belief, this genetic information established that Dr Dettmann is Joseph’s biological father.”



In 1982 after struggling some time struggling with her fertility, Dettmann recommended Mary try artificial insemination.

For over four decades, the family remained unaware of the alleged switch until Joseph received an email from Ancestry.com about his biological connections.

He said: “What he did was incomprehensible and it was such a betrayal of trust that I just wanted to make sure that if I have the opportunity to hold him accountable for the pain that he caused my mom and the things he put her through, that maybe she didn’t even know at the time.”

Mary says she feels “violated”, saying she feels like she has been raped.

She said: “It’s not right. And I want other women to feel ok about coming forward with this.”



The lawsuit was filed on August 6 on behalf of the mother and son by their attorney Al Foeckler, with the Wisconsin Health Care Liability Insurance Plan and ABC Insurance Co also listed as defendants.

At a news conference announcing the suit, Foeckler said: “These families come to fertility doctors at their most hopeful and their most helpless time.

“Trusting completely in the physician who holds their dreams of parenthood in their hands. Dr Frederick Dettmann preyed on that desperation. He exploited that trust.”

Foeckler revealed multiple women have come forward to share with own uncomfortable experiences with the Dr, dating as far back as the 70’s.

He said: “There is no question in my mind that this man was a serial predator of women.”



Dettmann is now retired and denies any wrongdoing in a statement submitted by his legal team on his behalf.

In a statement to NBC News, attorney Sean Gaynor said Dettmann is aware of the allegations but is unable to speak about patient care because of privacy laws.

He said: “The events referenced are alleged to have occurred almost 50 years ago.

“Dr. Dettmann has no independent recollection of the individuals making these allegations and is unaware of any evidence supporting the claims being asserted.”

According to Whitefish Bay police records, Dettmann had previously been accused of assaulting a woman during a gynaecological exam in 1985, TMJ 4 reported.



No charges were issued, citing that proving the assault would be “too difficult”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A spokesperson for the Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services told NBC News it does not have records of closed complaints from that long ago.

Gaynor has since noted that Dettmann was “never sued, disciplined, investigated, had his licensure challenged, nor were any ethical complaints ever made against him.”

News.title: Who really killed Tupac? Suspect Orlando Anderson’s gang shooting death left case cold for years before Keefe D’s arrest
News.content:
THE death of the primary suspect in Tupac Shakur’s drive-by shooting left the rapper’s case cold for decades before the high-profile arrest of a Compton street gang leader.

Duane “Keefe D” Davis, 63, is the only person criminally charged in connection with the infamous shooting of Shakur, 25, near the Las Vegas Strip on September 7, 1996.



Davis has boasted about his involvement in the shooting, including admitting in interviews to being one of the four people inside the white Cadillac that opened fire at the BMW Shakur and Death Row Records founder Suge Knight were driving.

Over the years, retired law enforcement officials have stated that the four individuals inside the Cadillac were Davis, Terrence “Bubble Up” Brown, Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson, and Deandre “Freaky” Smith.



All four were members associated with the Southside Compton Crips, a rival street gang to the Compton Bloods set linked to Knight.

Investigators have long suspected Anderson, Davis’ nephew, as the triggerman who opened fire at Shakur from the back seat.

Read more in The U.S. Sun GRIM FIND Twist in hunt for son, 27, after bodies of missing parents found buried in yard

The drive-by was allegedly a retaliatory gang hit against Shakur and Knight after the two and their entourage jumped Anderson in the hotel lobby of the MGM Grand following Mike Tyson’s heavyweight boxing fight.

Anderson was once named a suspect in Shakur’s murder, however, he was never charged due to lack of evidence.

Two years after Shakur’s death, Anderson also fell victim to gang violence when he was fatally shot at a car wash in Compton in May 1998.

Investigators said Anderson, who was 23 years old at the time of his death, and another man – both members of the Southside Crips, drove up to a car wash where several members of a rival gang had gathered.



An altercation ensued and then quickly escalated into a shootout, according to police.

Four people were injured, while Anderson and another man died from their injuries a short time later.

Michael Dorrough was arrested and convicted of the murders in October 1999.



Now, decades after his nephew’s killing, Davis is finally set to stand trial for the murder of Shakur.

Ahead of his trial, Davis has repeatedly sought to distance himself from the shooting and claimed he was seeking royalties from the interviews he conducted where he bragged about being the shot caller in Shakur’s murder.

“I wasn’t in Las Vegas. They can’t prove it,” Davis told Fox affiliate KVVU.

Davis also detached himself from his memoir, Compton Street Legend, claiming he never wrote the book and only told a ghostwriter aspects of his life.

“I never wrote that book. I just gave him things about my life and I gave him some pictures,” Davis said in a prison interview, referring to the book’s co-author Yusuf Jah.



“He just did research and some stuff like that. He and my lawyer did. My lawyer died, and signed on to it with him. I never read it or nothing.”

Davis was arrested outside his home in Henderson, Nevada, in September 2023 and has maintained his innocence.

The prosecution’s case against Davis will rely heavily on his own self-incriminating remarks, where he portrayed himself as the gang’s ringleader and orchestrated the shooting on the night of September 7, 1996.

Prosecutors have a list of 45 potential witnesses that they plan to call to the stand, including Knight, Reggie Wright Jr., the former head of security of Death Row Records, former Las Vegas Mayor Oscar Goodman, Republican Governor and former Las Vegas Metro officer Joe Lombardo, and several of Shakur’s relatives.



However, Knight, who is serving a 28-year sentence after pleading no contest to voluntary manslaughter in 2018, is refusing to cooperate with prosecutors.

“This trial has nothing to do with me and if somebody brings me there, it’s gonna hurt whoever brings me there. I promise you that,” Knight told ABC News.

“They make me come there against my will, if Keefe D’s lawyers bring me there, it don’t look good for him.

“If the prosecution brings me there, it don’t look good for them. Leave me out of it.”



A defiant Knight, who has long ties with the Compton Bloods street gang, called taking the stand and testifying against someone worse than killing them.

“My loyalty to Tupac can never be compromised,” he told the outlet.

“Me as a man, what I believe in, can’t be compromised. I’m not there to help [Davis], and I’m damn sure not there to hurt him.

“To actually get on the stand, and point somebody out, it’s worse than taking a gun and shooting that man in the head.

“Because if you shoot a person in the head, they die once. If you get on the stand and you snitch on that person, they die a million times.



“I am not going to be responsible for sending another man to prison for the rest of his life. If God’s forgiving, who am I to think I’m bigger than God and don’t forgive? Because I’m not.”

Knight believes his testimony does not matter because Davis already “told on himself” after spending years conducting interviews about his involvement in Shakur’s murder.

“He felt he was untouchable,” Knight told the outlet.

“He wanted to talk bad about ‘Pa, he wanted to just talk, talk, talk, talk. He kept talking until they put handcuffs on him.

“Everything he said and talked about, he already told on himself. So what are you going to do?



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Erase all the recordings of the interviews he did?”

Davis’ trial is expected to last four weeks.

News.title: 'My son, 7, had six teeth removed after inhumane wait for treatment'
News.content:
'My son, 7, had six teeth removed after inhumane wait for treatment'

EXCLUSIVE: Children under 18, or under 19 and in full-time-education, can get free NHS dental appointments and treatment but there is a shortage of NHS practices

View 2 Images Hayley Bramhall, from Macclesfield, said it was "devastating" to see her son Philip in agony (Image: STEVE ALLEN)

A mum whose seven-year-old autistic son had six teeth removed due to a dental abscess has said it was "inhumane" he had to suffer a four-month wait in intense pain.

‌



Hayley Bramhall, from Macclesfield, said it was "devastating" to see her son Philip in agony. During the wait for "urgent" treatment, his abscess grew leading to the need for him to have teeth taken out.

‌



She said her non-verbal son has been holding his mouth and avoiding toothbrushing in a particular area since his surgery in July and she fears they might have to face another long and painful battle if he has another dental problem.

‌



Speaking about him having six teeth removed, Hayley said: "Eating's become more challenging because of that. He's a lot more irate and upset. As a family and for me, it's traumatic. It's frustrating. It makes you feel angry - angry at the lack of services.

Children waiting over a year in agony for tooth extractions READ MORE :

View 2 Images Nearly 10,000 children were admitted to hospital for rotting teeth last year, damning figures show. (Image: Getty Images)

"Frustrated at the fact that, for example, now I need to start the process again because I think he's got toothache. Although I don't know whether it's because he was in pain for four months, which is just inhumane in itself."

‌



Hayley has launched a petition on the Parliament website calling for a maximum 12-week wait for children with special educational needs requiring urgent dental care under sedation or general anaesthetic.

She said her son needs sedation and general anaesthetic just for check up, which can mean long waits that result in the problem getting worse.

"I think the pressure and the wait just for that is exceptional, never mind the wait for someone in extreme pain," she said. "It's devastating as a parent seeing him in pain all the time."

‌



Nearly 10,000 children admitted to hospital for rotting teeth last year, grim study shows

Nearly 10,000 children were admitted to hospital for rotting teeth last year, damning figures show.

In 2025, 8,930 under 18s were admitted for tooth decay, slightly up from 8,925 the year before, analysis by the Liberal Democrats shows.

Children under 18, or under 19 and in full-time-education, can get free NHS dental appointments and treatment but there is a shortage of NHS practices. Around 14 million people – or well over one in four of England’s adult population – were unable to access NHS dental care in 2025.

‌



The study found 470 dental practices have pulled out of the NHS and handed back their contracts since 2020 as ‘dental deserts’ spread across the country.

The research also found particular damage in rural areas, with higher numbers of dentists approaching retirement and a higher proportion leaving the profession.

Elsewhere, researchers found local Education Authorities have shelled out over £2.5million for school-aged pupils since 2020, including on toothbrush kits and on public health initiatives.

‌



Tooth decay remains the number one reason for hospital admissions among young children. The British Dental Association says some kids are waiting years to have teeth extracted because the surgery is competing with other operations on the NHS waiting list for operating theatre time.

Children usually require going under general anaesthetic for tooth extractions so this has to be done in hospital.

Lib Dem primary care spokeswoman Helen Maguire said: “Thousands of young children are being forced into hospital beds just to have their rotting teeth pulled out, millions are trapped in expanding 'dental deserts' unable to get an appointment, and local councils are being forced to shell out millions to patch up a broken system.”

‌



The Liberal Democrats have demanded a £750million Dental Rescue Package to revive access to local NHS appointments and guarantee regular checkups for children. It is also calling for emergency dental A&Es in every community across the country that provide walk-in urgent care seven days a week to ensure that nobody is left in agony.

The British Dental Association welcomed the commitment to new money and criticised a lack of new investment from the Labour Government. The Mirror has launched the Dentists for All campaign with the BDA calling for a return to universal access to NHS dentistry for everyone who needs it.

Eddie Crouch, BDA chair, said: “When millions of people have no options, it’s refreshing to see serious proposals to invest in expanding access to NHS dental care. The real threat to NHS dentistry has always been a poverty of ambition. Rearranging the deckchairs on the Titanic won’t help.”

‌



More than 40,000 people have signed a petition launched by 38 Degrees calling on Andy Burnham to make NHS Dentistry a priority, amid a crisis of people being forced to carry out DIY Dentistry and pull out their own teeth.

Veronica Hawking, Campaigns Director at 38 Degrees, said: "Nobody in modern Britain should be pulling out their own teeth because they can't get an NHS dentist.

"The Government has the public firmly on side - now it needs to properly fund NHS dentistry, so no one else is forced to take matters into their own hands."

Article continues below

A Department of Health and Social Care spokesperson said: "This government is fixing NHS dentistry after a decade of decline. We have improved access to urgent dental treatment by prioritising patients with the greatest need, and millions of additional courses of treatment have been delivered, including a significant amount for children.

“But there is still more to do - especially to increase the dentistry workforce - and that is why we’re rolling out more dentistry school training places in areas which need them, and cutting red tape to allow qualified dentists to practise.”

News.title: UK facing deadly 38C heat blast in just days as Brits urged to drink plenty and check on vulnerable family
News.content:
UK facing deadly 38C heat blast in just days as Brits urged to drink plenty and check on vulnerable family

The Met Office today said the UK is on course to record its hottest summer ever as Brits were warned of 38C temperatures and extreme weather warnings were issued

View 4 Images The record-breaking drought has driven rivers to record lows, with people seen on the cracked mud bed of Hollow Pond, east London (Image: Yui Mok/PA Wire)

Drought-hit Brits were today warned to brace themselves for a blistering 38C heatwave as health alerts kicked in and the UK looked set for its hottest summer on record.

‌



A spike in temperatures is anticipated as the Met Office issued an extreme heat warning, saying the "wider population is likely to experience some adverse health effects". The 15-hour amber warning covering all of England will begin at 9am on Thursday and was scheduled to last until midnight.

‌



Separately, UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) today activated amber heat health alerts for much of England, which will run until Friday, warning of a "rise in deaths". The Government has urged people to stay safe by drinking plenty of water, checking on vulnerable friends and family, and avoiding the sun at the hottest part of the day.

‌



View 4 Images The lost village of Nether Hambleton were exposed today because of the low water levels at Rutland Water reservoir (Image: Joe Giddens/PA Wire)

The scorching weather puts the UK on course for its hottest summer on record. Currently the mean average temperature stands at 16.48C between June 1 and August 10, which is 1.88C above the 1991-2020 average.

Met Office senior scientist Mike Kendon said: "Another record-breaking summer now looks increasingly likely for the UK, following the second-warmest June, and second-warmest July on record and yet another heatwave imminent."

‌



Pointing to repeated occasions in which the UK experienced temperatures of 35C or more, Kendon added: "These statistics are a clear reminder - if one were needed - of the stark changes that we are seeing in the UK's climate."

The record-breaking heatwave - the fifth of the year - has caused chaos across the UK, sparking raging wildfires, creating problems for farmers and driving rivers to record lows. The heat was so severe it exposed the remains of a lost village that was demolished and flooded to create a reservoir.

View 4 Images Scorched fields were seen near Jeremy Clarkson's Diddly Squat Farm as farmers faced more misery during the drought (Image: Jacob King/PA Wire)

‌



Stonework and the outlines of buildings in Nether Hambleton were seen today because of the low water levels at Rutland Water reservoir in the east Midlands. More than 3,000 acres of land were submerged in the 1970s to create what was then Europe's largest man-made lake, with residents rehoused in the surrounding areas. Among the lost buildings were 18th century homes and farmland growing barley to be sold to Germany for brewing lager and wheat which Hovis bought for breadmaking.

It came as the temperature are today thought to have topped 26C in London, 28C in Manchester and 28C in Cardiff, before the mercury is expected to soar in some areas to 34C tomorrow and 38C on Thursday. But meteorologists believe showers could move across the country on Sunday - bringing the first spattering of rain to southern areas in two months.

Searing temperatures have seen almost three quarters of England - affecting 45 million people - experience "flash droughts", with 27million people slapped with hosepipe bans. In Wales almost the entirety of the country was in drought, with hosepipe bans imposed by Wales Water for more than 33,000 people.

‌



View 4 Images The scorching weather has left the UK's grasslands - like those in Hampstead Heath - scorched and dry (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Met Office chief forecaster Chris Bulmer said: "While the peak heat will be more short-lived than recent heatwaves, temperatures widely into the mid-30Cs on Thursday bring the potential for impacts for some, which is why a Met Office warning has been issued.

"High pressure is now becoming dominant and temperatures will build day-by-day. Southerly and south-easterly winds will also tap into the hot conditions over Europe, which helps develop this further notable heat in what has been a hot and dry summer so far."

‌



Met Office Deputy Chief Forecaster David Oliver said: “While Thursday will be the peak of the heat this week, some warmth will remain in the south and south east on Friday, before easing more widely on Saturday as cooler air spreads south from the north west.”

Farmers are struggling to cope with the intense heat and experts warning it would drive up food and drink prices. The Food and Drink Federation (FDF) said "fruit, vegetable and grain supply" are being hit, with crop shortages set to feed into supermarket prices.

Images show dry fields at Jeremy Clarkson's Diddly Squat Farm in Chipping Norton, Oxfordshire. And people were seen walking on the exposed, cracked, and dried mud bed of Hollow Pond, near Wanstead, in east London.

‌



It came as firefighters continued to battle a series of fires across the UK, including one in the New Forest National Park, Hampshire. Emergency crews today began a third day of tackling tackling the blaze - that at one point covered an area equivalent to 140 football pitches - as they say they are "managing to contain" after working "tirelessly" through the night.

The area hit by the blaze, which started after a van caught fire on the nearby A31 near Ringwood on Sunday, is protected heathland and home to a number of rare species, according to the New Forest National Park Authority.

It came as the National Fire Chiefs Council said July was the busiest month on record for wildfires, with serbices responding to 966 wildfires this year, just shy of the 1,017 they attended during a record-breaking year in 2025. In July alone, firefighters attended 458 wildfires, whilst in the first 10 days of August crews have been called out to 185 wildfires.

‌



Phil Garrigan, chairman of the council, said: "The combination of drought conditions and another heatwave means the risk of fires remains high, and these incidents can place huge demands on firefighters and specialist resources. Many wildfires are preventable so we're asking people to be vigilant and take extra care outdoors while these conditions continue."

It came as the Fire Brigades Union said its members were under increased pressure as a result of an "unprecedented summer of dangerous and volatile wildfires". Steve Wright, the FBU general secretary, said the unpredictable environmental challenges the UK was now confronted with meant it was a "national priority" to have enough properly equipped firefighters to "face these threats".

He called for "increased funding, improved access to the best equipment and better national resilience" to combat rising demands. He said: "Our country is facing unpredictable environment.al challenges and it must be a national priority to ensure we have enough properly equipped firefighters to face these threats."

‌



Wright has previously said fire crews were stretched by staffing cuts - with 12,000 fewer firefighters in the UK than in 2010.

William Spencer, climate and first aid expert at the British Red Cross, said: "While periods of hot weather have become more familiar in recent years, they can still pose serious risks to health. In fact, after prolonged dry and warm conditions, it is more important than ever to follow heat safety advice.

"Simple steps such as wearing sunscreen, drinking plenty of fluids, seeking shade during the hottest parts of the day and taking regular breaks from the sun can help protect you and those around you. It's also important to look out for the signs of heat exhaustion and heatstroke, particularly among people who may be more vulnerable to the effects of extreme heat."

Article continues below

There are warnings older people are more at risk from the extreme heat, with Caroline Abrahams, Age UK's charity director, saying that as people age, their bodies find it harder to adapt to extremes of heat and cold.

She said: "Even younger and otherwise healthy people can feel the effects of very hot weather, but with temperatures forecast to reach up to 36C in some areas, the risks can be much greater for older people."

She urged people to check in on older neighbours, friends and relatives to see if they need support such as picking up the shopping or lending them a fan. She said: "The increasing frequency of heatwaves, alongside droughts, wildfires and hosepipe bans, shows how important it is that we do more to protect those most at risk as climate change continues to bring more extreme weather."

News.title: Solar Eclipse 2026: Check your postcode to see when stunning show visible in your area
News.content:
Solar Eclipse 2026: Check your postcode to see when stunning show visible in your area

It will take just 15 minutes for the peak moment to sweep from the very north of Scotland down to Land’s End in Cornwall, so check our interactive tool to see when exactly the eclipse will pass your home

View 2 Images Eclipse glasses have sold out in stores and online (Image: Getty Images/Cavan Images RF)

The biggest solar eclipse visible from the UK since 1999 is now just hours away, with the best time to see the stunning astronomical event in each postcode now revealed.

‌



Most of the UK will come close to a total solar eclipse, with the Isles of Scilly getting the most coverage - more than 96 per cent. The rest of the country will see more than 90 per cent of the Sun obscured, as the Moon will come in between it and the Earth tomorrow evening.

‌



Across the UK, the eclipse will start around 6pm and reach peak obstruction about an hour later, with the event ending just after 8pm in most places. It will take just 15 minutes for the peak moment to sweep from the very north of Scotland down to Land’s End in Cornwall, which means the moon shadow will sweep over the surface of Britain at a speed of nearly 2,500 miles per hour.

‌



But by entering your postcode into our interactive tool, you can be sure that you are looking up at exactly the right moment when it passes your home. Solar eclipse glasses or specialist telescopes are the only safe way to view the eclipse directly, or the eclipse can be projected using a pinhole or household items like a colander which has lots of holes in it.

View 2 Images Most of the UK will witness coverage of more than 90 per cent (Image: Getty Images)

‌



People shouldn't use sunglasses to look at the eclipse as these are not dark enough to block harmful solar radiation, leading to severe damage to your retinas. As tomorrow's event will be the best in the UK for the next 54 years, interest has been so great that some high street stores and online retailers have completely sold out of eclipse glasses.

The latest Met Office forecast shows that most of England and Wales will have clear skies on Wednesday evening, on a day when temperatures are likely to be over 30C in large parts of the country. However, cloud cover is forecast for most of Scotland and Northern Ireland, plus parts of the North East of England and Cumbria. Depending on the thickness of the cloud, the eclipse may still be visible in these areas.

The best locations to view the eclipse are in the far south western areas of Devon and Cornwall, where up to 96 per cent of the sun will be obscured by the moon. The rest of Wales, Northern Ireland, parts of the West Midlands and the South West, and the westernmost parts of Scotland can expect to see 92 per cent to 94 per cent solar coverage.

Article continues below

In Cardiff, the moon is forecast to obscure 93.24 per cent of the sun at 7.13pm while in Belfast it will cover 93.09 per cent of the sun at 7.08pm. Areas in the East of the country, including the coasts of Norfolk, Yorkshire and Aberdeenshire, will witness slightly less of an eclipse effect - but these places will still see just over 90 per cent of the sun obscured.

The next time the moon obscures as much of the sun will be in 2081 and the next total solar eclipse in the UK will be in 2090.

News.title: The Office star Lucy Davis reveals she's been diagnosed with terminal breast cancer aged 53
News.content:
The Office star Lucy Davis reveals she's been diagnosed with terminal breast cancer aged 53

The actress, famous for playing Dawn Tinsley, said: 'I’m not scared of whatever comes next. I’m at peace with it.'

The Office star Lucy Davis reveals she's been diagnosed with terminal breast cancer

The Office star Lucy Davis has revealed she's been diagnosed with "incurable" stage 4 breast cancer and said she "doesn't know how long she has left".

Lucy, 53, shared the sad news with a video that showed her ringing the 'good luck' bell for cancer treatment bell having been told it was "too late" for chemotherapy. The actress told her followers: "I’m not scared of whatever comes next. I’m at peace with it."

The actress, famous for playing Dawn Tinsley alongside Ricky Gervais and Martin Freeman in the BBC version of the Office and as Etta Candy in Wonder Woman, addressed fans in an Instagram post.

She wrote: "A year and a half ago I was diagnosed with Stage 4 Breast Cancer, which has metastasized to my bones. Specifically to my spine, right hip, and my ribs. The cancer is incurable, and too late for chemo.

4 View 4 Images She told fans 'leaving my physical body just means going home' (Image: Getty Images) 4 View 4 Images Lucy Davis shared a video of her ringing the 'good luck bell' alongside her message (Image: Lucy Davis)

"The initial lump that I felt, wasn’t a ‘lump’ as such; rather a kind of hard spot. Really tiny. I almost didn’t bother getting it checked. So I guess I’m saying don’t ignore anything - get everything checked out:)"

Lucy, is the daughter of British comic Jasper Carrott, 81, continued: "As of now, I’m trying to live out whatever might be left of my life in as fun a way as I possibly can.

"I always like to find the teachable moments in anything negative that happens. And cancer has not disappointed in that regard; there’s a lot I have learned from it, and I’m grateful for that.

"As some of you will know, the pain can really be something else. Standing and walking for too long a time can be hard, and I need to use a wheelchair sometimes (so if you see me toddling around in one, feel free to give me a push!)

View 4 Images She appeared as Dawn Tinsley in the groundbreaking BBC sitcom The Office (Image: Lucy Davis/Instagram)

"The thing that has been most vital to me is humour. I asked my friends and family to make fun of me as much as possible (which they’re really good at), and most importantly of all to not treat me like a sick person. There’s nothing that will make you feel more unwell than being treated as if you’re unwell.

"I’m not scared of whatever comes next. I’m at peace with it. I’ll see my Gracie [her dog, who died in 2024] sooner than expected, and for me, leaving my physical body just means going home. Any and all grieving is for my family; it’s far harder for them than for me."

She concluded: "I’m still going to keep up all my work for animal rights. It’s so important to me. And I still would like to keep working. I’m perfectly able to do so, and acting is one of the biggest joys in my life.

"For those of you on a similar journey to mine, I do wish you well. Cancer asks a lot from us, physically and mentally. And we all get to do it however we choose. Much love to you all."

View 4 Images Lucy appearing as Hilda Spellman in The Chilling Adventures Of Sabrina

Her followers reacted in their thousands, with one writing: "Oh Lucy. I’m sending you so much love and wrapping you up so tightly. You will be in my prayers." Another wrote: "Sending all the love. Breaks my heart to see so many affected by cancer."

Earlier this year Lucy revealed that her mum had given her a kidney when she was in her mid-20s as part of a campaign called One's Enough.

Article continues below

She wrote: "My mum gave me a kidney over 28 years ago! Both my kidney, and her remaining one, are still going strong. Please consider donating if you can.

"It’s life changing and life saving. And I understand that the process is simpler than when we had our transplants. We were in hospital for 2 weeks back then, but I believe it’s a few days now."

News.title: Massive fire erupts near Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport as two runways closed
News.content:
Massive fire erupts near Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport as two runways closed

Two runways at Charles de Gaulle Airport in Paris have been closed after the huge fire broke out near the transport hub

Paris: Huge plume of black smoke rises from fire near airport

A massive fire has broken out near Charles de Gaulle Airport near Paris, forcing the closure of two runways.

‌



French media reports the fire broke out near the railway tracks of Louvres train station, close to the airport, with a towering plume of smoke is visible for miles around.

‌



The blaze is believed to have started at around 3pm in a car park near Louvres, a town in Val-d’Oise in the north of the capital. Some 80 firefighters have been mobilised.

‌



View Image Aerial footage showed black smoke pouring into the sky near Paris Charles De Gaulle airport (Image: X/flabrouillere)

There has been no impact on air traffic at this time despite the closure of two runways at the airport, local reports say.

‌



French media, M6info, also reported that the car park where the fire broke out is the one used by passengers flying through Charles De Gaulle. Footage taken from a passing train shows cars ablaze in the parking lot which is on an industrial estate near the train station.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Law enforcement confirmed that the fire involved several dozen vehicles parked in a lot on the avenue. A train station on the RER D commuter rail line was also closed.

Article continues below

Emergency services have warned the public to stay away while they battle the inferno.

Surrounding towns are on high alert as the smoke spreads over several kilometers. On Facebook, the town of Fontenay-en-Parisis urged its residents " to stay indoors, close doors and windows, and turn off ventilation if possible ."

News.title: Aldi to sell £150 'garden baths' from Sunday August 16
News.content:
Aldi to sell £150 'garden baths' from Sunday August 16

The weekend brings a unique item on sale in the middle aisle

View 3 Images Aldi is selling the bath in stores across the UK from Sunday, August 16 (Image: Matt Cardy/Getty Images)

Aldi shoppers are used to all sorts of items being featured in the middle aisles of the supermarket, but the supermarket very rarely sells baths. However, Aldi shoppers won't be getting their hands on the typical tubs that go in the bathroom. The store will start selling a bath you put outside instead, which could help people with certain medical conditions.

‌



The Crane Premium Ice Bath will be arriving in Aldi stores this weekend as part of the newest SpecialBuy refresh. On offer for £149.99, customers can bring home a tub that claims to be big enough for two people to use.

‌



Describing the bath online, Aldi said: "Refresh your body. Refocus your mind. Experience the power of cold water immersion." The discount supermarket claims that the bath is "suitable for two people" and is "perfect for a winter ice bath".

‌



The £150 set, available later this week, includes the bath itself as well as a pump, filter pump with lid, carry bag and repair patch. Previously, Aldi sold a single Ice Bath for £24.99 - so this new option serves as an upgrade for those who take their ice baths seriously.

View 3 Images The Crane Premium Ice Bath

‌



What are the benefits of an ice bath?

Ice baths offer a way for people to practice cold water immersion. According to health experts at Bupa, plunging into water that is colder than 15°C has been linked to easing sore muscles, lowering swelling, speeding up physical recovery after hard exercise, and boosting mental alertness by releasing endorphins.

People should be aware that cold water immersion can trigger some dangerous side effects, such as cold water shock, arrhythmias (heart rhythm disorders) and hypothermia. It is important for anyone wanting to include this in their health and wellness routine to build up sessions gradually to help the body adapt to the cold and lessen the risk.

Cold water therapy won’t be suitable for everybody, despite what the internet may claim. If you’re concerned about how cold water therapy may affect you, discuss it with your GP before trying it.

Article continues below

View 3 Images People practice cold water immersion with these ice baths for various health, fitness and medical reasons (stock image) (Image: Getty)

What else is coming to Aldi this weekend?

The Premium Ice Bath is one of the star products landing in Aldi's middle aisle during the upcoming Sunday refresh on August 16. There will be plenty of options in the fitness collection coming to stores nationwide this weekend, such as:

News.title: Anyone suffering from headaches and tiredness issued disease 'overlap' warning
News.content:
Anyone suffering from headaches and tiredness issued disease 'overlap' warning

GP has shared a health alert for anyone suffering common symptoms this summer to not mistake them as 'normal'

View 3 Images The doc tor says headaches, fatigue, feverishness, and muscle discomfort can occur with both conditions (stock image) (Image: Getty)

With more people spending time outdoors in the ongoing hot weather, a GP is urging them not to automatically put headaches, fatigue or feeling feverish down to the heat. The health expert warns that some of the same symptoms can 'overlap' and occur in the early stages of Lyme disease.

‌



The two conditions can share some early symptoms, making Lyme disease easier to overlook during the summer, particularly when someone has recently spent time outdoors. Dr Rupa Parmar, GP and Medical Director of Midland Health, is sharing her tips on the key differences between heat exhaustion and Lyme disease and when symptoms after time outdoors may need medical attention rather than simply being put down to the heat.

‌



What is the difference between Lyme disease and heat exhaustion?

Dr Rupa Parmar said headaches, fatigue, feverishness, and muscle discomfort can occur with both conditions. However, the circumstances in which symptoms develop can help people decide when to seek medical advice.

‌



"Some early symptoms of Lyme disease overlap with those people may experience after spending too long in the heat," she said. "A headache, tiredness, a raised temperature and aching muscles can occur with both, so it’s important to consider when the symptoms began and what else you are experiencing.

"Heat exhaustion normally develops during or soon after exposure to hot weather or strenuous activity. Excessive sweating, pale or clammy skin, intense thirst, dizziness, nausea, muscle cramps and a fast pulse or breathing rate are all signs that the body may be struggling to cool itself."

View 3 Images Some early symptoms of Lyme disease overlap with those people may experience after spending too long in the heat

‌



The GP added that if someone is experiencing possible heat exhaustion, it’s important to move to a cool place, remove unnecessary clothing, cool the skin, and drink fluids. They should begin to feel better within around 30 minutes.

She also said that if someone remains unwell after 30 minutes, or develops confusion, very hot skin, a very high temperature, a seizure or loss of consciousness, call 999, "as these can be signs of heatstroke". An improvement in symptoms after cooling down and drinking fluids means it’s more likely to be heat exhaustion.

What is the timeline of Lyme disease?

She continued: "Lyme disease follows a different timeline. Symptoms may not appear until days or weeks after a walk, picnic, gardening, or other time spent around vegetation. It’s easy not to connect feeling unwell with where they have been, which can make the infection easier to overlook"

‌



A circular or oval rash that gradually spreads can be an early sign of Lyme disease. It’s commonly called a bullseye rash. The rash may be evenly coloured, and it can be harder to see on brown or black skin.

View 3 Images A circular or oval rash can be an early sign of Lyme disease

The doctor said: "It’s also important to remember that not everyone develops or notices a rash. Ticks can be extremely small, and their bites are not usually painful, so some people with Lyme disease have no memory of being bitten.

‌



"Ticks generally attach in warm, hidden areas, including behind the ears and knees, around the hairline, under the arms, around the waist and groin, and between the legs. So, check skin, but also clothing and belongings after spending time outdoors, particularly after walking through long grass or wooded areas."

How do symptoms of both conditions overlap?

Headaches: Caused by dehydration and strain in heat exhaustion, and by inflammatory immune responses in Lyme disease.

Caused by dehydration and strain in heat exhaustion, and by inflammatory immune responses in Lyme disease. Fatigue: Low electrolytes and fluid in the heat, and from the body fighting a bacterial infection in Lyme disease.

Low electrolytes and fluid in the heat, and from the body fighting a bacterial infection in Lyme disease. Feverishness: Higher body temperature caused by either hot weather or a fever/chills from the immune system.

Higher body temperature caused by either hot weather or a fever/chills from the immune system. Muscle discomfort: Cramps or weakness from heat strain and generalised aches or joint pain from Lyme disease.

What are the distinguishing signs?

Indicators of heat exhaustion include Heavy sweating, pale, clammy skin, extreme thirst, and a direct correlation with hot environments or intense exertion. Indicators of Lyme disease include: History of a tick bite, development of a characteristic expanding circular or "bullseye" rash (erythema migrans), and chills without necessarily being in a hot environment.

‌



What should you do if you find a tick on your skin?

Dr Parmar says that if you find an attached tick, remove it as soon as possible using a tick-removal tool or fine-tipped tweezers. Grasp it as close to the skin as you can and pull slowly and firmly upwards, taking care not to squeeze or crush its body. Clean the bite area afterwards with antiseptic or soap and water.

"Do not try to burn the tick or cover it with petroleum jelly, alcohol or nail varnish," she stressed. "These methods may irritate it and could increase the chance of infected material passing into the skin.

Article continues below

"Finding a tick does not mean you will develop Lyme disease, as not every tick carries the infection. However, you should monitor the area and pay attention to how you feel over the following weeks."

She added: "If you develop a spreading circular or oval rash or experience persistent flu-like symptoms, fatigue, headaches, muscle pain or joint discomfort after possible tick exposure, contact your GP. Tell them where you have recently spent time, even if you didn’t see a tick or notice a bite.

"Most symptoms after a hot day outdoors will not be Lyme disease, but any that persist after cooling and hydration shouldn’t be automatically blamed on the weather. Being aware of the timing and checking for ticks can help people seek the right support sooner."

News.title: Bomb squad and robot scrambled to County Durham town as evacuation ordered
News.content:
Bomb squad and robot scrambled to County Durham town as evacuation ordered

Robert Terrace in Shield Row, Stanley, has been taped off and people have been asked to stay away from the area after a 'suspicious item' was found

View 3 Images A Ministry of Defence Bomb Robot in Stanley (Image: Newcastle Chronicle/Craig Connor)

People are being evacuated following the discovery of a "suspicious item" in the North East, as a bomb squad and a robot have been called in.

‌



Robert Terrace in Shield Row, Stanley, is currently cordoned off as investigations are ongoing. Durham Constabulary confirmed around 60 homes have been evacuated.

‌



A spokesperson for the force said: "We currently have a cordon in place around Robert Terrace in Shield Row, Stanley, while we investigate a suspicious item. Around 60 homes have been evacuated, with residents being directed to The Louisa Centre, in Front Street, for assistance.

‌



"Emergency services, including the Bomb Squad, are currently on scene and working as quickly as they can to assess the item. We are asking people to stay away from the area at this time. Updates will be provided as soon as possible."

View 3 Images The Ministry of Defence's 'Explosive Ordnance Disposal and Search Regiment' are on the scene in Stanley (Image: Newcastle Chronicle/Craig Connor)

Pictures from the scene show a Ministry of Defence (MoD) Bomb Robot being controlled via a remote control, with bomb disposal officers also present.

‌



A spokesperson for County Durham and Darlington Fire and Rescue Service explained that the service was called to the scene just after 1pm today and a 100-metre cordon is in place.

They said: "We were called at 1.02pm today (August 11) to a police incident on Robert Terrace, Shield Row, Stanley. A 100 metre cordon is in place and arrangements have been made to evacuate residents.

View 3 Images A member of the bomb squad on the scene of the incident in Stanley (Image: ChronicleLive)

Article continues below

"One fire engine from High Handenhold is at the scene and the crew is expected to be there for some time." North East Ambulance Service is also present, ChronicleLive reports.

A spokesperson said: "Police requested our support for an incident in Stanley, County Durham shortly before 1pm on Tuesday 11 August.

"We dispatched four HART resources, one duty officer, one tactical commander and one tactical advisor. The incident is ongoing and we remain on scene.""

News.title: Summer 2026 on course to be UK's hottest on record, says Met Office
News.content:
This summer is on course to be the UK's hottest since records began, according to the Met Office.

Only average conditions are needed for the remainder of August to surpass the record set just last year.

Provisional Met Office statistics show that the UK's mean temperature for meteorological summer so far (1 June to 10 August) currently stands at 16.48C (61.66F), which is 1.88C above the 1991-2020 average.

In summer 2025, the mean temperature across the country - which includes overnight lows as well as daytime highs - was 16.10C (60.98F).

It is in line with evidence that summers are getting hotter and are likely to become drier because of climate change.

News.title: Burnham 'confident' early release of PC Harper's killers can be halted
News.content:
Andy Burnham says he is "confident" PC Andrew Harper's killers can be excluded from the government's early release scheme, as outcry over the case grows.

The prime minister has now ordered the justice secretary to find a way to bar Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were jailed for 13 years for manslaughter in 2020, from early release.

It marks a shift from last week, when he said there was "nothing more" he could do without risking the collapse of the prison system.

The move comes after days of pressure to exclude Harper's killers from the scheme, which is aiming to free about 5,000 offenders in England and Wales to make space in overcrowded jails.

Harper's mother, Debbie Adlam, told the BBC she was in "turmoil" following conflicting reports about whether two of her son's killers would be released from prison early, describing the handling of the situation as a "hash".

Conservative shadow home secretary Chris Philp accused Burnham and Labour of "re-traumatising victims and their families with their constant U-turns".

Burnham said a new plan to prevent more prisoners from being freed long before the end of their sentences would be presented to Parliament in September.

It comes after he initially announced some prisoners convicted of rape, serious child sex and other grooming offences would be barred from early release, after a review of the scheme he ordered after he became prime minister.

In an article published last week, external, Burnham said he had "wanted to go even further" but had "pushed to the very limits of what is possible to do".

He added: "I know I can look people in the eye and say to them there is nothing more I could have asked for without risking the prison system reaching capacity and collapsing within months."

But on Tuesday, Burnham insisted he had never accepted "there was nothing more that could be done" to prevent the early release of more offenders, including Harper's killers.

"I came into office and started pushing on this issue, and I have pushed every single day in office," he added.

Burnham said he would seek to hold talks with other political parties to build "consensus" on the approach to early releases.

News.title: Eclipse chasers scramble for glasses as stocks run low
News.content:
At a bakery in central London, stock has been flying off the shelves.

"I've sold, like, 100 this morning," a staff member tells the BBC. But it's not baked goods driving queues out of the door - customers are here to buy eclipse glasses.

They are among those hoping to catch a safe glimpse of Wednesday's solar eclipse - the UK's most significant since 1999 - but struggling to get their hands on the right gear.

Experts have urged eclipse enthusiasts not to look directly at the Sun - with even brief exposure causing lasting damage - and to seek out specialist glasses instead.

But online, pairs that meet safety specifications have all but sold out. Those still available either require a hefty next-day delivery fee or simply cannot arrive on time.

Even the Royal Museums Greenwich - recommended as a reputable retailer by UK health officials - has sold out, citing an "unprecedented volume" of orders.

Meanwhile, eclipse glasses have been turning up for sale in unexpected places as retailers try to capitalise on the demand.

"I Googled 'where can I get eclipse glasses but not through the post', because I realised I was too late," one customer waiting to buy three pairs at the bakery on Monday tells BBC Radio 4's PM programme.

"People have been struggling to find them all over," says another.

News.title: Watch: Was Trump smuggled out of Air Force One in a catering truck?
News.content:
Donald Trump secretly switched planes when he was returning from a Nato meeting last month in order to avoid a threat to his life from Iran, US media has reported.

The president boarded Air Force One in Ankara, Turkey, on 8 July before being transported to another aircraft with the help of a catering truck, the Washington Post said.

He was then seen disembarking Air Force One in the UK, before boarding his newer, Qatari-gifted jet and returning to the US.

Trump spoke to journalists during his flight to the US but did not say whether he had been moved to a different plane.

The BBC's diplomatic correspondent Paul Adams explains.

News.title: Rescuers scramble for survivors with 180 dead in Colombia earthquake
News.content:
Rescue workers in Colombia are working against the clock to free survivors trapped in buildings and under rubble following Monday's powerful earthquake.

More than 180 people have been confirmed dead - most in the cities of Cali and Pereira.

The magnitude 7.4 quake struck at 07:34 (12:34 GMT) on Monday and was felt across an enormous area, stretching for hundreds of miles across western Colombia - with fresh aftershocks still being felt on Tuesday.

While the official death toll remains 181, an aggregated figure gathered from local officials puts it higher - potentially at more than 240. A state of emergency has been declared by President Abelardo de la Espriella.

Giving an update on Tuesday from Pereira, one of the worst hit cities, President Espriella said as well as those killed, almost 2,600 had been injured, and almost 200 people remain missing.

He also reported that more than 1,100 homes had been destroyed, and more than 8,000 had been damaged.

Overnight on Monday into Tuesday, several people several people spent the night outdoors in cities like Pereira and Cali - either due to their homes being destroyed, or fear of further collapses.

Across the country, dozens of larger buildings have also collapsed.

News.title: The Office actress Lucy Davis says she has 'incurable' cancer
News.content:
Lucy Davis, who played Dawn Tinsley in the original UK version of The Office, has revealed she has "incurable" breast cancer.

Davis, the daughter of comedian Jasper Carrott, starred as the office receptionist in the groundbreaking sitcom, which ran from 2001 to 2003.

A post from the 53-year-old actress on Instagram, external on Tuesday said: "I wanted to share something with you all that I've kept to myself for a while but for various reasons would like to share now.

"A year-and-a-half ago I was diagnosed with stage 4 breast cancer, which has metastasized [spread] to my bones. Specifically to my spine, right hip and my ribs. The cancer is incurable, and too late for chemo."

News.title: Luigi Mangione murder trial to have anonymous jury and overflow seating
News.content:
The judge overseeing the state trial of Luigi Mangione, accused of killing UnitedHealthcare chief executive Brian Thompson, has laid down the ground rules for court public and media access to the high-profile case.

Mangione returned to court on Tuesday ahead of his murder trial, which begins next month in New York. Dressed in a charcoal grey suit with his hair clipped short, Mangione sat silently at the defence table while his attorneys conferred with the judge.

In Tuesday's hearing, Judge Gregory Carro decided that the 12-person jury would remain anonymous to the public due to the spotlight on the case, and that there would be an overflow room to meet media demand.

The case has attracted national attention, and has also created an online frenzy, with both his backers - many of whom see Mangione as a symbol of the backlash against US healthcare costs - and his critics analysing everything from his intentions to his appearance.

The spectacle is likely to intensify when jury selection for the trial begins on 8 September.

Mangione, if found guilty, could face decades behind bars. He has pleaded not guilty to all charges, including second-degree murder and weapons-related offences.

He faces a separate federal trial next year, in which he has also pleaded not guilty.

Much of what is expected at the state trial â the prosecutor's case, Mangione's defence, and obstacles both parties face â were previewed in months of court filings and arguments.

Here's what to know about the upcoming trial, and what questions remain.

News.title: Councils to get more powers to stop vape and betting shops, PM announces
News.content:
New vape shops will require planning permission and councils will get more powers to block new betting shops, under government plans aimed at improving high streets.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said town centres had been "hollowed out" by decades of decline and for many people, the high streets they grew up with are "unrecognisable".

He said the plans were "shaped" by a series of BBC News investigations which exposed organised crime on high streets, revealing shops selling illegal cigarettes, vapes, cannabis and cocaine, enabling illegal working and suspected money-laundering.

The Conservatives and Reform said the proposals would lead to "more empty" shops, without tax relief for other small businesses.

Burnham said the measures will give councils more power to control what businesses open in town centres.

The proposals come as the prime minister embarks on a tour of the UK, with Downing Street saying he will be in "listening mode" during his visits as he works on a "10-year plan to bring back hope".

The plans announced by the government include:

Changes to planning law which would mean every new shop selling e-cigarettes, or vapes, would need to apply to their local council for permission to open (England only)

Tightening the definition of a vape shop to prevent businesses avoiding the rules by describing themselves as a general convenience store or retailer (England only)

Scrapping a rule known as "aim to permit", which currently restricts councils' ability to refuse new betting shops and 24-hour slot machine shops (Great Britain-wide)

Requiring planning permission for new adult gaming centres, which offer 24-hour access to gambling machines (England only)

New powers to extend closure orders for mini-marts and vape shops found to be selling illegal tobacco for up to twelve months, something previously proposed by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer (England and Wales)

The National Crime Agency (NCA) estimates that at least Â£1bn of criminal cash is laundered through high street stores in the UK each year through businesses connected to the sale of fake goods, tax evasion, illegal working and illegal drug supply.

Burnham told the BBC that the changes would make it "easier for police to close a vape shop and have it closed for longer".

He said: "At the same time we're changing the planning regime... which should stop the proliferation of vape shops on our high streets."

The prime minister added that Operation Vulcan in Cheetham Hill, Greater Manchester, cleared the area of counterfeits and crime and "proved" what could be achieved.

"When I look at police reform across England, I will be asking for a similar approach to be taken," he said. "I want the strongest possible neighbourhood policing, with all agencies involved, to rip out criminal behaviour that is pulling places down."

Burnham said he did not accept the decline of the high street as "inevitable".

"I don't see why anywhere should have to accept they have empty shops, vape shops and the challenges that come with that."

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner told BBC Breakfast on Tuesday that many people were frustrated at vape and gambling outlets "popping up even near schools and some of them are linked to illegal activity and crime".

News.title: Man guilty of harassing MP Stella Creasy on Tube train
News.content:
A 63-year-old man has been found guilty of harassing the Labour MP for Walthamstow after preventing her from leaving a Tube carriage and behaving in an "abusive and aggressive" manner.

Clifford Wilby, from east London, targeted Stella Creasy on a Victoria line train between Walthamstow Central and Finsbury Park on 15 July last year.

Westminster Magistrates' Court heard how Wilby spoke to Creasy about knife crime and her "failings as a Member of Parliament" before filming her, leading to members of the public intervening.

Deputy Chief Magistrate Tan Ikram found Wilby guilty of using threatening, abusive or insulting words or behaviour with intent to cause harassment, alarm or distress.

Wilby and Creasy first met during a Zoom meeting in 2024 as part of her role as an MP.
