She said he started to make a complaint about a constituent and she reminded him that she could not discuss somebody else's case.

Creasy said he had "made a series of very serious allegations", became abusive and "referred to the fact he had been diagnosed as a psychopath".

The meeting was stopped because of Wilby's behaviour.

News.title: Criticism as thousands of seats empty at Europeans Athletics Championships
News.content:
Nearly 10,000 seats were empty at Birmingham's Alexander Stadium for the European Athletics Championships on Monday evening.

A crowd of 13,623 watched as Britain's 24-year-old sprinter Amy Hunt stormed to her first senior international title, in a stadium that has a capacity of 23,000.

Athletics supporters blamed ticket prices, with some describing them as "extortionate", while BBC commentator Steve Cram commented that spectator numbers were a "little disappointing".

But Birmingham 2026 organisers said they were "delighted" with ticket sales, which have "far surpassed" their targets with "Friday, Saturday and Sunday evening sessions approaching sell-out, with several other sessions close to capacity".

On Monday, Category A tickets for the home straight cost Â£150 with no concessions for juniors.

For the men's 100m final on Tuesday, those same seats cost Â£110, again with no concessions - while a similar ticket for the same final in Rome two years ago was 88 euros (Â£75).

It is Britain's first time hosting the championships in their 92-year history.

News.title: Man dies after punch from security guard in Turkey bar, inquest hears
News.content:
A rugby player was punched in the head by a security guard while on holiday in Turkey and died after he returned home, an inquest has heard.

Scot James, from Maesteg, Bridgend county, had been in hospital since he suffered head and brain injuries in an alleged bar assault on 5 July.

He fell and hit his head during a "verbal exchange", Pontypridd Coroner's Court was told on Tuesday.

The 34-year-old was repatriated to the UK and died on 26 July at the Royal Glamorgan Hospital in Llantrisant, Rhondda Cynon Taf.

A provisional cause of death was given as blunt head injury.

James' family described him as a "loving father, son, grandson and partner" in tributes following his death.

Maesteg Celtic RFC said he was an "outstanding player and a great character".

Coroner Rachel Knight said a full inquest was necessary as there was reason to suspect the death may have been unnatural.

She said that as police in Turkey would potentially be investigating James' death, the next inquest hearing would be scheduled for later this year.

Knight said it may be necessary to pause inquest proceedings pending the outcome of any criminal investigation and confirmed the court would liaise with Turkish authorities.

Police in Turkey are understood to be investigating the death, with assistance from the Foreign Office.

In a statement, James' family said he "had a warm heart, a great sense of humour, and a natural ability to bring people together".

"We are heartbroken by his loss," they said.

"No words can truly express the pain we are experiencing or the void his passing has left in our lives."

Maesteg Celtic RFC said: "Everyone at the club is devastated by this news and our thoughts go out to his family and friends at this difficult time."

News.title: England set to be one of the first countries to eliminate hepatitis C
News.content:
Hepatitis C is spread through contact with blood infected with the virus, such as by sharing needles with someone who has it.

Donor blood is already screened for it.

It is a silent disease, meaning people often have no symptoms until much later.

Untreated, it can cause serious and potentially life-threatening liver damage.

NHS England says that since 2015, more than 100,000 people have been diagnosed and treated for hepatitis C, meaning the country is already meeting that target.

Another goal - a 65% reduction in hepatitis C-related mortality compared with 2015 levels - has yet to be met, but might be before the 2030 target date.

Around 50,200 adults are living with hepatitis C, figures for England in 2024 suggest.

Estimates indicate 84.6% of those living with hepatitis C have been diagnosed - just short of the 90% target.

The Hepatitis C Trust says England is "on the cusp" of one of the most significant public health achievements in our country's history.

Prof Frankie Swords, NHS national medical director, added: "England is now leading the world in the mission to eliminate this disease and on course to beat the WHO's 2030 target, but we are determined to keep up the momentum and finish the job.

"We are committed to finding and treating everyone who needs support and would urge those at greater risk to come forward by ordering a free and confidential home-testing kit online."

Adults born in Ukraine, Romania, Estonia, Latvia, Poland, Albania, Lithuania, Bulgaria, Czechia or Slovakia are particularly urged to test, as some may have been infected through medical or dental procedures before 1991.

People can order a free, confidential NHS home self-testing kit, external without needing to speak to a GP.

News.title: Antisemitism towards Jewish children 'shocking', government expert tells BBC
News.content:
Headteachers of some Jewish schools are spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than on educational matters, a review into antisemitism in schools and colleges has found.

Sir David Bell, speaking for the first time about his ongoing government-commissioned independent review, told the BBC he had been struck by how many leaders of Jewish faith schools had told him security was their main concern - and that "sometimes education takes second place to that".

The extent of antisemitism directed at children and young people was "shocking" he said.

The report, due this autumn, examines experiences of Jewish pupils and staff in faith and secular schools and colleges in England.

Sir David said he found that pupils were "subject to regular harassment and abuse".

He said Jewish children and young people "are facing a pressure - and indeed one might say even a crisis - that is not the experience of other communities in this country".

The review is likely to recommend dedicated training for all teachers and improved education about antisemitism for pupils, the BBC has been told.

The BBC has spoken to several headteachers and staff at Jewish schools. All asked not to be named because of concerns over their security and that of their schools.

One headteacher said: "In recent years [security] has become an overwhelming priority and increased a significant amount. There have been weeks where approximately 90% of my time has been spent on security-related matters.

"Security concerns can become one of the many things that headteachers carry with them beyond the school day and, quite literally, can be among the things that keep me awake at night."

News.title: YouTube couple's donkey sanctuary plans approved
News.content:
A famous YouTube couple have been allowed to build a donkey sanctuary behind their West Sussex home.

Earlier this year, Zoella - real name Zoe Sugg - and her fiancÃ© Alfie Deyes applied for permission to develop a five-acre field they had bought next to their property near Hassocks.

They were warned by Mid Sussex District Council (MSDC) that there could be potential Roman, Anglo-Saxon or even prehistoric remains buried there.

MSDC approved their application at a planning meeting on Friday, having recommended that work cannot begin until archaeologists conduct an investigation.

Zoella, 36, who made her name with make-up videos before moving on to books and her own range of products, applied for planning back in May.

Included were proposals to create an enclosure for the animals, stables, three shepherd huts, parking for tractors and a pond.

However, an earlier excavation across the road had uncovered items from the Roman period, with MSDC's archaeological adviser previously stipulating that no groundwork should take place until a programme of archaeological monitoring was approved.

Locals also voiced concerns about how the development might impact the views of the surrounding area, increase traffic and impede access to nearby bridleways and public footpaths.

They complained that a gate and fences have already gone up at the site.

"We also don't like the gates and would rather they were not there," said one resident, who did not want to be named.

"Once you have gates up, it's not the same.

"There are paths and bridal ways all around here and people use them for walks all the time."

On the gate is a poster from Sugg and Deynes which reads: "We've lived here for nine years with our garden backing onto this field, and we have always worried about it one day being developed into new houses.

"After many years of trying to purchase it, last year we managed to do so.

"This means not only is the view from our house and many others nearby protected, it also helps keep this area the lovely walking spot it is for so many people each day.

"If you live in this area and are also keen to keep as much green space thriving as possible, please head over to the council's planning website and leave a positive comment to help encourage the approval of other projects like ours - thank you."

News.title: Golfer left shaking by 411-yard hole in one
News.content:
An amateur golfer was left "frozen" and "could not stop shaking" after hitting a hole in one from 411 yards (376 metres) - a one-in-six-million chance, according to one estimate.

Matthew Vigurs, from Droitwich in Worcestershire, narrowly missed out on claiming a Guinness World Record when he sank the shot during a league match at Great Barr Golf Club on 25 July in Sandwell near Birmingham.

The record sits with Robert Mitera, external who in 1965 at Miracle Hills Golf Course in Nebraska, USA,, external hit a hole in one from 447 yards (408 metres).

But despite being 36 yards (33 metres) short, 32-year-old Vigurs said: "I got married last year so obviously that's number one but this is definitely up there as a close second best moment of my life."

England Golf, external, the national governing body for amateur golf, believes Vigurs' achievement could be a national record, but that is yet to be confirmed.

But for any golfer a hole in one is a moment to remember and due to its rarity, Vigurs admitted he felt "stupid" even looking for his ball near the hole.

"We all hit good shots but I didn't expect it to go anywhere close to the green and I didn't know it had until we got up there," he said.

"We were looking for the balls but mine was missing.

"Everyone else was about 40 yards short of the green and we even had a look over the back of the green.

"I just double checked the hole and unbelievably I froze for about 10 seconds when I noticed the ball in the bottom.

"I rolled it over and saw my markings and we all went mad. It was surreal."

News.title: Girl, 6, dies and another child hurt in A12 crash
News.content:
A six-year-old girl was killed and another child was injured in a collision that shut part of the A12 on Monday, police have said.

The crash, involving a lorry and a car, happened at about 10:30 BST on the northbound carriageway near the Colchester United football stadium.

The road was shut in both directions and an air ambulance landed, while vehicles caught in the closure were turned around.

Det Insp Mark Fraser, of Essex Police, said the lorry driver had passed all road-side tests and was due to be interviewed in the coming days.

The injured child suffered a leg injury and was recovering in hospital, the force added.

The collision led to parts of Colchester being gridlocked throughout the day, while A12 queues stretched back to Marks Tey.

News.title: Britain’s Andy Green sets a new speed record at Utah’s famous Bonneville Salt Flats

The only driver to ever exceed the speed of sound on land has claimed a new world record in a significant demonstration of hydrogen energy capabilities.

British driver Andy Green achieved 406.320 mph (653.908 kph) behind the wheel of a machine propelled by twin hydrogen internal combustion engines producing a total of 1,600 horsepower. The run established a benchmark for the vehicle class, as confirmed by motorsport's global governing authority, the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile.

Operating across the salt crust at Utah’s Bonneville Salt Flats, the 64-year-old former Royal Air Force pilot piloted a 32-foot (9.75-metre) vehicle developed by British industrial machinery maker JCB. Modified from units deployed in heavy plant equipment, the engines blend compressed hydrogen gas with air before ignition to generate propulsive thrust.

"It’s magic to be able to showcase this technology and to showcase how good the engineering is on the best racing surface in the world, Bonneville Salt Flats," Green said after setting the new record.

open image in gallery Andy Green and the JCB engineering team celebrate setting a new land speed record for a hydrogen-powered vehicle at the Bonneville Salt Flats in Utah, Tuesday, Aug. 11, 2026 ( AP Photo/Hannah Schoenbaum )

The achievement on Tuesday remained well short of the absolute land-speed record, which Green established using jet propulsion in 1997.

Driving Thrust SSC—a slender vehicle positioned between two massive jet engines—he reached 763.035 mph (1,227.985 kph), becoming the first person to go supersonic on land in an unmatched accomplishment. Those runs across Nevada’s Black Rock Desert created sonic shockwaves that rattled the town of Gerlach.

Green previously set a diesel land-speed benchmark of 350.092 mph (563.4 kph) at Bonneville in 2006. He made his return to Utah intent on surpassing that mark through hydrogen, a technology he has previously described as the "fuel of the future."

While pursuing his diesel mark, Green comfortably surpassed the prior hydrogen combustion record of 185.5 mph (298.5 kph). He utilised a 10-mile (16-kilometre) course to accelerate, observed from afar by a small gathering of JCB personnel and journalists using binoculars and cameras.

According to Green, conditions inside the cockpit on Tuesday were "probably a little hotter" than in his 1997 jet vehicle, with internal temperatures regularly exceeding 122 degrees Fahrenheit (50 degrees Celsius).

open image in gallery The JCB Hydromax, developed by British industrial machinery maker JCB ( AP Photo/Hannah Schoenbaum )

open image in gallery Engineers at JCB hope that demonstrating hydrogen capability at this level will influence the clean energy sector ( AP Photo/Hannah Schoenbaum )

"But I have been training four months for that, both training in the gym and actually just getting used to it with hot baths," he added.

Formed from an ancient lake bed, the Bonneville Salt Flats lie roughly 100 miles (160 kilometres) west of Salt Lake City, positioned above a high water table that helps cool tyres. The slick surface and arid climate create optimal conditions for high speeds, attracting racers since competitive driving began there in 1914.

"It looks like snow, and it behaves a bit like packed snow — it is surprisingly slippery," Green remarked.

Prior to entering record-breaking driving, Green was already accustomed to high speeds. He was serving as a supersonic fighter pilot when he answered a 1994  in a British newspaper searching for someone to break the sound barrier on land.

Although Tuesday's attempt was not supersonic, engineers at JCB anticipate that demonstrating hydrogen capability at this level will influence the clean energy sector.

The equipment maker's chairman has maintained that hydrogen technology is better suited to meeting the heavy industry's power demands than battery electrification.

Environmental benefits depend heavily on how hydrogen is generated, with most current supplies derived from fossil fuels. JCB has agreed a contract to procure green hydrogen produced via renewable sources, though this variant accounts for only a minor portion of worldwide production.

What does it mean when brown patches appear on an otherwise healthy lawn? In reality, the issue could stem from drought, dog urine, fungal disease, pests, or excessive fertilizer. Yet many homeowners automatically place the blame on lawn grubs.

The difficulty is that this common assumption is frequently incorrect, and even when grubs are present, minor populations are not actually problematic.

Treatment should only be applied following the confirmation of an actual grub infestation. Fortunately, checking is straightforward, but action must be taken within a specific window of time to prove effective. And that moment is now here.

open image in gallery Fortunately, checking is straightforward, but action must be taken within a specific window of time to prove effective ( Getty Images )

How to know whether grubs are the culprit

Grubs are the early life forms of beetles, including European chafers, and Asiatic, Japanese and Oriental beetles. They live close to the surface under lawns and other plants, where they feed on roots, disconnecting the roots from the plants' top growth.

Confirming their presence is easy: Dig up a 3- to 4-inch-deep (7.6 to 10 centimeters), 12-inch-square (930 square centimeters) section of symptomatic lawn that partially overlaps the border of healthy grass.

If there are grubs in the lawn, the whitish, brown-headed, half-inch to 1-inch-long (1 to 2.5 centimeters) beetle larvae, which resemble shrimp, will be visible either on the underlying soil or on the underside of the sod-like square you removed. They're generally curled into the shape of the letter C.

Fewer than 10 grubs per square foot of soil is normal and does not indicate an infestation, so you should not take any action. Instead, seek out other potential causes.

If grubs are the problem, what's the solution?

Treatment against grubs should only be applied if there are 10 or more of the insects present under the section of turf you removed. Heavily infested lawn sections will easily roll up like a carpet when you attempt to remove them, their roots severed by the feeding insects.

Because grubs are most vulnerable to pest-control measures when they are young, those measures will only be effective if applied in late summer.

Milky spore powder is a natural product that targets only Japanese beetle grubs. Unfortunately, it’s not always easy to discern between the species. If you are certain your grubs are the Japanese variety, you can give it a try, but success rates are mixed, with better outcomes reported in warmer regions.

open image in gallery Because grubs are most vulnerable to pest-control measures when they are young, those measures will only be effective if applied in late summer ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

Beneficial nematodes are microscopic, non-segmented worms that attack soil-dwelling insects, including all types of grubs. They're a more universal approach, with higher success rates. They, too, are natural, as they already exist in the soil; you would just be adding more. The nematodes work by infecting grubs with a bacterium that can kill them in as little as 48 hours.

There are many nematode species available, so read package labels and look for the Heterorhabditis bacteriophora (Hb) strain, which specifically targets grubs.

To optimize effectiveness, water the soil well before applying either treatment.

Avoid using chemical treatments, which can be toxic to earthworms, honeybees and other pollinators, pets and wildlife. Some are even toxic to humans.

Safeway is closing more stores as its parent company, Albertsons, works to reduce and reorganize its grocery store locations, Inc. reports.

The supermarket chain operates more than 900 locations, primarily across the western U.S., with a smaller presence in Maryland, Virginia and Washington, D.C. The chain has already shuttered at least three stores in 2026, in California, D.C. and Oregon.

The closures are reportedly part of a larger shake-up at Albertsons, which operates more than 20 grocery brands across 35 states, including Safeway, Vons, Jewel-Osco, Acme Markets and Shaw’s.

Last year, Albertsons closed at least 30 stores across its various banners, including locations under the Carrs, Albertsons, and United Supermarkets.

The company has been reviewing its store network since its planned $24.6 billion merger with Kroger was blocked by a federal judge in 2024. Albertsons has since focused on managing its existing stores and cutting locations where it sees less long-term potential, though it remains unclear which other stores or brands could be affected this year.

open image in gallery More Safeway grocery store closures are reportedly coming this year as parent company Albertsons continues to restructure its business following its failed merger with Kroger in 2024 ( AP )

“[Our network positioning] includes opening new stores in areas with strong demand and long-term opportunity, while also making the difficult decision to close some locations,” the company told Fast Company. “In these cases, we work to place as many associates as possible in other stores.”

The following Safeway locations have already closed this year, according to Inc.:

231 W Jackson Street, Hayward, CA

1601 Maryland Ave NE, Washington, D.C.

2220 N Coast Highway, Newport, OR

Most of the Safeway closures appear to be tied to expiring leases rather than the company pulling out of entire markets. In Washington, D.C., the Hechinger Mall location closed on May 16 after nearly 40 years because its lease was ending.

“We are coming to the end of our lease at this location, and have made the decision to reinvest our resources into other existing stores,” the company said in a statement.

Similar closures happened in Hayward, California, and Newport, Oregon. The Hayward store closed in late February, becoming the fourth Safeway in the Bay Area to shut down in just over a year, following locations in San Francisco’s Fillmore district, Pinole and Vallejo. The Newport store, which had been open for more than 30 years, was the city’s only Safeway.

"We have been proud to serve the Jackson Triangle neighborhood over the years, and this decision was not made lightly," Safeway said in a statement at the time. "With our lease term ending, we have carefully considered our options and decided to shift our strategy."

The closures have not necessarily meant widespread job losses. In Hayward, all 76 employees were transferred to other Safeway locations under the company’s union agreement. Safeway has followed a similar approach at many of its other store closures, moving employees to nearby locations when possible.

The Independent has contacted Albertsons for comment.

News.title: July was just the hottest month on record in the US. So what does that mean for August?

July was just the hottest month on record in the contiguous U.S., according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration - and shows little signs of slowing down for AUgust.

Fortunately, it appears temperatures will drop for many areas this week - but much of the southern U.S. will see dangerous heat before the end of August.

“Potentially record-breaking heat will grip the Southeast to south-central U.S. into next week, with heat indices reaching 105–115 degrees Fahrenheit and little nighttime relief,” NOAA’s National Weather Service warned.

August is typically not quite as hot as July, but meteorologists say the record sets up August for more extreme events. Some local records have already been broken.

“Wow - Pueblo just set its all-time hottest August temperature on record. 107 degrees at the Pueblo Airport so far,” Colorado meteorologist Chris Bianchi wrote on Bluesky. “That's also just two degrees shy of the all-time hottest temp there.”

open image in gallery Last month was the hottest for the US since record keeping began in 1895, federal officials say. And August is already smashing records ( Getty )

It remains to be seen whether it could be the hottest August on record, too.

July averaged a temperature of 76.9 degrees Fahrenheit, which was the highest average temperature for the region since record keeping began in 1895.

That’s between 0.1-0.2 degrees warmer than the previous records set in July 2012 and July 1936, during the Dust Bowl.

Interestingly, daytime temperatures were only the sixth warmest. That meant America just wasn’t cooling down at night, NOAA explained.

“Daytime maximum temperatures averaged 89.5 degrees Fahrenheit, 2.9 degrees Fahrenheit above average, ranking as the sixth-warmest month on record for average high temperatures, while overnight minimum temperatures averaged 64.2 degrees Fahrenheit, 3.7 degrees Fahrenheit above average,” NOAA explained, “ranking as the warmest month on record for average low temperatures, surpassing July 2022 by 0.7 degrees Fahrenheit.”

open image in gallery This map from the National Weather Service Weather Prediction Center shows heat forecast in the US in the coming week ( NWS Weather Prediction Center )

Experts say human-caused climate change is to blame for record temperatures in July and throughout the year.

The fossil fuel industry’s greenhouse gases are continuing to warm the Earth’s atmosphere and are the largest contributor to global climate change. That is leading to the continued extinction of the world’s species, helping to form more damaging and frequent storms and leading to more extreme heat events.

“Extremely high temperatures across the continental U.S. this summer, along with intense drought and fire conditions, are absolutely consistent with the climate change signal,” Katharine Jacobs, a climate scientist at the University of Arizona, told The Associated Press.

open image in gallery A graph from NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information shows where global temperatures were the warmest, in dark red, during the month of July ( NOAA NCEI )

But it’s not just climate change that is keeping us warm, the natural El Niño climate pattern is also a factor. El Niño is the warm phase of the El Niño Southern Oscillation climate pattern, which helps to regulate weather around the world and typically leads to warmer summers.

Earth just transitioned into this phase over the summer, and the pattern is expected to strengthen to historic levels.

The El Niño helped contribute to the nation’s prolonged heat domes in July that led to dozens of deaths in New Jersey and around the country.

“We expect to set record global temperatures as long as carbon emissions continue to warm the planet, and typically these records are set during major El Niño events,” Michael Mann, a climate scientist at the University of Pennsylvania, told The Guardian.

open image in gallery The days with extreme heat events are expected to increase due to human-caused climate change ( AFP/Getty )

Europe also saw it’s hottest July, according to the European Union’s Copernicus Climate Change Service.

These updates come amid other unfortunate findings about the climate. A “state of the climate” report released by the American Meteorological Society examined last year’s extreme heat, finding that greenhouse gas concentrations, global sea level and ocean heat content reached the highest levels on record in 2025.

News.title: Sharks v New Zealand LIVE: Result and reaction as impressive All Blacks thrash hosts
News.content:
( Reuters )

New Zealand produced a vastly-improved performance as they put the Sharks to the sword in Durban in their second fixture of the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour.

The All Blacks had been scratchy in their opening clash with the Stormers in Cape Town on Friday, but re-found their cutting edge to surge away from their hosts in Durban in the second half. Dave Rennie had shuffled his side and looked to a number of combinations that had served the New Zealand coach well during the Nations Championship, and would have been pleased to see them impress again with Ruben Love and Jordie Barrett forming a potent partnership.

Of concern, though, for the All Blacks boss was an injury to Damian McKenzie. The full-back fell awkwardly and hurt his ankle in the first half, and though he could continue for long enough to score a try and have another chalked off, McKenzie was replaced before the interval. He faces a race to be fit for the four Tests against the world champion Springboks – the first of which takes place on Saturday week in Johannesburg as a landmark series in South Africa continues.

New Zealand ran in an eight-try blitz without conceding as they romped to an emphatic 54-0 win over the Sharks in the second game of their Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour of South Africa.

It ⁠was a ​much ⁠more convincing performance from the tourists after Friday's scratchy opener against the ⁠Stormers in Cape Town, with their forwards, set-piece and kicking game vastly improved to set a platform upon which the backs thrived.

The Sharks started brightly but ultimately had little answer to a rampant All Blacks, with winger Fehi Fineanganofo scoring two of the tourists' tries.

open image in gallery Fehi Fineanganofo scored two of New Zealand’s tries ( Reuters )

The other six came from Damian McKenzie, Caleb Clarke, Jordie Barrett, Kyle Preston, Timoci Tavatavanawai and Sam Darry, with Ruben Love adding seven conversions in an impressive display from the fly half.

There was cause for concern for head coach Dave Rennie, though, as McKenzie was forced off before the interval after landing awkwardly on an ankle.

The Sharks put on 44-year-old former All Black Ma'a Nonu for the last 20 minutes after he recently joined the provincial side in a leadership and mentorship capacity. Nonu, who won 103 caps for the Kiwis, performed a poignant ​solo response to New Zealand's traditional pre-match Haka to the delight of the ‌small crowd, and then delivered some crunching ⁠blows on his compatriots in his cameo performance, one of the highlights for ⁠the 14,759 spectators at King's Park.

The ​All Blacks are next ‌up against the ⁠Bulls in Pretoria on ⁠Saturday before the first of four ‌Tests against the Springboks takes place in Johannesburg a week later.

The landmark series will conclude in Baltimore on Saturday 12 September.

Major retailers across the UK have completely sold out of solar eclipse eyewear as people travel long distances to secure a pair ahead of the most significant celestial event since the previous century.

Local shops, national parks and the Royal Greenwich Society have all run out of stock prior to Wednesday's event, which is set to be the UK’s most complete solar eclipse for the next 54 years.

The Royal Greenwich Observatory informed the Press Association that roughly 15,000 pairs of glasses were bought in the past month, marking a total sellout.

While admission to their on-site viewing event is also fully booked, a free live stream will be broadcast on their website and YouTube channel.

open image in gallery A convenience store in Whitechapel had to turn customers away after selling out ( PA Media )

High demand has left smaller stockists overwhelmed.

Ali Raza, owner of a convenience store in Whitechapel, told the Press Association he had to turn away numerous hopeful buyers, adding that customers were making extensive journeys to locate the specialist glasses.

Mr Raza, who owns the AM2PM store, said: “On Sunday we had people coming from Surrey, Southend-on-Sea, yesterday night a lady came from Southampton, and loads of people have come from Birmingham as well. We’re too busy.

“Today I already sold 6,000 pairs. At 2.30am we had a delivery from Spain and by 9.30am we sold out everything.”

open image in gallery Customers queue outside Am2Pm Convenience shop in Whitechapel for solar eclipse glasses and leave after being told they were temporarily sold out ( PA Media )

More than 90% of the sun will be obscured by the moon between 6.17pm and 8.06pm on August 12 – the most it has been blocked in the UK since the total eclipse in 1999.

In the UK, Devon, Cornwall and the westernmost parts of Pembrokeshire in Wales are set to see the eclipse at its fullest, with a range of 94% to 96% of the sun obscured by the moon.

Officials in Exmoor National Park, in north Devon, told the Press Association they have seen “large numbers” of people coming to see the eclipse there.

The park is an international dark sky reserve and a spokesperson for the park said that they “couldn’t keep up with demand” for eclipse glasses.

They said: “We got to a point where we couldn’t get any more from our supplier in time and we don’t need them again, not until 2081.

open image in gallery In the UK, Devon, Cornwall and the westernmost parts of Pembrokeshire in Wales are set to see the eclipse at its fullest, with a range of 94% to 96% of the sun obscured by the moon ( Getty/iStock )

“As a national park centre, we’ve seen an increase in visitors specifically to our centre looking for those glasses and to ask us where would be the best places to go and look at it.

“We advise people to go up to high moorlands or coastal headlands, or Dunkery Beacon, the highest point on Exmoor, because you get an elevated view across to the west.

“We’ve sold over 300 pairs of glasses but we could’ve sold that twice over.”

Exmoor will also host a now sold-out guided walk from the Hunters Inn pub where participants will watch from Highveer Point.

In South Downs National Park, at least five astronomy groups are holding events, with the eclipse followed by the yearly perseid meteor shower.

The Met Office said weather conditions in most of the country will be “more or less perfect” for eclipse viewing.

A spokesperson told the Press Association: “With clear skies forecast across much of the UK, conditions should be more or less perfect for many to experience the partial solar eclipse.

“The north and west of the country are most likely to struggle with cloud cover when viewing the eclipse on Wednesday evening, particularly across Northern Ireland and western Scotland.

“The rest of Scotland and northern England may also see a good deal of high-level cloud, making skies rather hazy. The best opportunities for viewing the eclipse are likely to be south of a line from Aberystwyth to Lincoln.”

A planetarium astronomer at the observatory told the Press Association that the glasses were important for viewing the eclipse safely and that sunglasses are insufficient.

Imo Bell said solar telescopes – such as the ones available at the observatory’s soldout watch-along event – or holed household objects like colanders were good ways to watch the eclipse, but eclipse glasses are preferable.

She said: “You can use solar eclipse glasses, which are very, very different from sunglasses – they block out so much light that you can’t see anything through them except the sun, because that’s how much light they need to block for the damaging light of the sun to be safe to view.

“And if all else fails, you can project the image of the eclipse using a household item like a colander which has lots of holes in – point the colander towards the Sun with your back facing it, and in the shadow of the colander you’ll be able to see the eclipse in the holes, which is really cool.”

Experts have warned that only special solar eclipse glasses that are ISO 12312-2 certified for the safest eye protection should be used to view the eclipse.

Following the 1999 total solar eclipse, the Royal College of Ophthalmologists reported around 70 cases of people experiencing vision problems after watching the eclipse.

Around 40% had looked at it for less than a minute.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register or login to an existing telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football launched on August 10, 2026. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.

How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.





You can follow the latest Telegraph Fantasy Football news and discussions throughout the year on Facebook, Twitter and Fantasy Football Content Hub.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.



Pick your free Telegraph Fantasy Football team now >

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: troubleshooting
News.content:
Need help logging in? Please read this helpful guide first

You’ll notice the site has a new look and feel this year, but more than the visuals have changed. For the 2026/27 season, your old Fantasy Football username and password will no longer work.

This means you will now need to create a Telegraph.co.uk account in order to access Telegraph Fantasy Football, but rest assured, this is free and you don’t need to subscribe. If you already have a Telegraph account then you should use your existing details. If you are still not sure, please follow the instructions below:

Which option best describes you?



1. I do NOT have a Telegraph account

Select Play Now on the Fantasy Football homepage Select ‘Continue with Telegraph’ Enter your email address For this season, you must confirm you are over the age of 18. If you are, please select continue If you are not over the age of 18, you cannot proceed past this point Check your email address is correct, please also add your first & last name and create a new password Select Continue. You will automatically be returned to the Fantasy Football page, ready to play.



2. I already have a Telegraph account

(For example, if you read Telegraph content online or receive Telegraph newsletters)

Select Play Now on the Fantasy Football homepage Select ‘Continue with Telegraph’ Enter your usual Telegraph email - if you’re logged in to the main Telegraph website, this can be found in your account settings here For this season, you must confirm you are over the age of 18. If you are, please Select continue If you are not over the age of 18, you cannot proceed past this point If you have previously logged in via your social media accounts, please select ‘show more options’ and proceed with the relevant button for you Enter your password and select continue You will be taken straight into the game to set up your team If you have forgotten your password, please refer to section 3

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football points: a complete guide to scoring
News.content:
How many points for a Goal?

A regular source of goals is often the first thing a manager looks for in a fantasy football team. The highly-priced Erling Haaland is a go-to signing for many, but last season saw the continuation of mid-priced forwards getting in on the action too with the likes of Igor Thiago racking up 22 goals in Telegraph Fantasy Football.

Players get five points per goal scored which, added to starting appearance points (two), mean a regularly starting goal scorer can be a huge asset.



How many points for an Assist?

It won’t take a master tactician to work out that players who rank highly in the goalscoring charts often also feature in the upper echelons of the Assists table.

Bruno Fernandes was head and shoulders above the rest with regard to assist points last season with 21 in total (nine clear of his closest rival).

An assist will earn three points.





What counts as an Assist?

An Assist is the final touch (pass, pass-cum-shot or any other touch) leading to the recipient of the ball scoring a goal.

Outside of fantasy football, if the final touch is deflected by an opposition player, the initiator is only given a goal assist if the receiving player was likely to receive the ball without the deflection having taken place. Own goals, directly taken free kicks, direct corner goals and penalties do not get an assist awarded.

In a change to previous years, Fantasy Assists are not being used.



How many points for a Tackle?

A slightly more nuanced aspect of scoring is the points a player earns for a successful tackle. Managers will need to cast their nets wide to capitalise on tackling points as the highest scorers tend to come from mid-table and even lower-table teams.

Everton’s James Garner was a key beneficiary of tackle bonus points last season with 120 tackles in total. His closest rivals have been very popular this summer with Wolves’ Joao Gomes, now at Aston Villa, and Nottingham Forest’s Elliot Anderson, now at Manchester City. It’s clear from this that deeper lying midfielders are more likely to amass points here.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made during a match and only midfielders are eligible.



What counts as a Tackle?

A tackle is defined as a player connecting with the ball in a ground challenge and successfully taking the ball away from the player in possession. The tackled player must have clearly been in possession of the ball before the tackle was made.

The final destination of the ball (to the tackler, to a teammate, to an opposition player or out of play) is not considered. A tackle will only be deemed unsuccessful if the player tackled retains possession of the ball.

A player cutting out a pass does not count as a tackle.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made.



How many points for a Clean Sheet?

Attainable by goalkeepers and defenders, the top-scorers in the clean sheet category last season mostly came from Arsenal.

There are five clean sheet points on offer for a player who has played at least 60 minutes of a match and two points if the player has played less than an hour where the game has finished with their team conceding zero goals.



How many points for a Save?

In addition to clean sheet points, goalkeepers can earn one point for every two saves made in a match. Much like points for tackling, save points introduce a new angle to team selection with keepers from teams further down the table likely to face more shots than those who generally dominate games. Last season Mark Flekken came out on top with 153 saves for Brentford, so it will be interesting to see how Caoimhin Kelleher gets on this season.



What counts as a Save?



A save is a goalkeeper preventing the ball from entering the goal with any part of his body when facing an intentional attempt to score by an opposition player.

Saves have the following attributes:

Body part: Hands/Feet/Body

Save type: Caught/Collected/Parried Safe/Parried Danger area/Fingertip

Goalkeeper position: Diving/Standing/Reaching/Stooping

For an exhaustive list of how to score Telegraph Fantasy Football points, take a look at our Game Guidelines.

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

Sports.title: Hull City close in on big-money Femi Azeez swoop as Acun Ilicali continues ambitious transfer strategy
Sports.content:
PREMIER LEAGUE new boys Hull City are in pole position to complete a swoop for Millwall winger Femi Azeez.

The Tigers have stolen a march on their rivals as they race to lure the South London star to the big time before the transfer window slams shut.



SunSport can reveal Millwall have already knocked back a record transfer bid for the wide man — an offer that eclipsed the £14.5million fee they received when Romain Esse moved to Crystal Palace.

Lions chiefs know it will be extremely difficult to now retain their talisman, despite standing firm so far.



Azeez, 25, established himself as one of the Championship‘s most lethal attacking outlets last season, racking up an impressive 11 goals and 7 assists across all competitions.

His terrifying pace and direct output from the wing made him one of the division’s top performers and triggered intense interest across the top flight.

Azeez’s blistering form has also caught the eye beyond English shores, with a host of European clubs currently sniffing around a potential deal.

Ipswich Town previously launched a formal bid for the winger back in January, but the Tractor Boys have yet to return to the table with a fresh offer.

That leaves ambitious Hull sitting firmly in the driving seat as they prepare to offer Azeez a crack at Premier League football.

Tigers boss Sergej Jakirovic views Azeez as an ideal marquee addition to supercharge their frontline for their top-flight comeback.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Millwall remain desperate to hold out for top dollar after reluctantly sanctioning Esse’s blockbuster departure last year.

But the Yorkshire club will have to be careful not to be gazumped, with European suitors lurking as negotiations ramp up.

Sports.title: England star Kalvin Phillips completes fourth loan transfer since joining Man City after Sheffield United horror season
Sports.content:
KALVIN PHILLIPS has returned to Sheffield United on loan.

The Manchester City midfielder spent the second half of last season at Bramall Lane but only managed three appearances before a knee injury curtailed his stint.



This will be his FOURTH loan at City, with him not featuring in the Premier League for the club since 2023, with two years still left on his deal.

Phillips was sold by his boyhood club Leeds United, who are rivals of the Blades, to City in 2022 for £42.5m but has only started two league games for them.



Blades boss Chris Wilder was keen to bring in Phillips for a second time to give him options in midfield while he faces losing Gustavo Hamer to Coventry City.

Wilder said: “We’ve stayed in contact with Kalvin throughout the summer and in those conversations what was always clear was both sides wanted to make this happen.

“Clearly, there has had to be a degree of patience to get a deal completed. Make no mistake, this is a good deal for the football club, and I have to thank the owners and Stephen Bettis for their diligence and persistence to get this one done.

“Since the first day Kalvin walked through the door here, he instantly ticked the boxes in terms of personality and character, both on the field and behind the scenes and he offers more experience in a crucial area of the pitch.

“Kalvin is a winner; he’s achieved plenty in his career and he’ll set the example to this young squad we have here.”

Meanwhile, Phillips commented: “This was the move I wanted.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“My time was spoiled by my last game and the injury after that so I’m here to put that right.

“The squad is similar to what it was last year, I’m happy to see everyone and I’m looking forward to coming back fighting fit.

“It is a good feeling to walk back through the doors in Shirecliffe, I see that the pre-season has been tough and the lads have come out flying so I’m happy to start training and get involved.”

The midfielder’s last contribution for the Championship side came in a derby win against Sheffield Wednesday – when he was sent off for a knee-high challenge on Svante Ingelsson.



He then missed the remainder of the season with a knee injury.

Phillips prepared for the upcoming campaign by working on his fitness with Jack Grealish last month.

The pair spent 36 minutes on an exercise bike in a 40C chamber before returning to Man City for official pre-season.

Sports.title: Man Utd star Joshua Zirkzee jets in assistant to UK home… just to tidy his WARDROBE & ‘help him look like 90s rapper’
Sports.content:
DUTCH OF CLASS Man Utd star Joshua Zirkzee jets in assistant to UK home… just to tidy his WARDROBE & ‘help him look like 90s rapper’

MAN Utd ace Joshua Zirkzee jets in a personal stylist from Holland just to tidy his wardrobe – and she’s documenting the lot on TikTok.

The Dutch striker enlisted fashion stylist Sydney Luchies to reorganise his wardrobe, clear out the clobber he no longer wears and make space for shiny new pieces.



Sydney jets into Manchester, gets stuck into the rails, then heads straight back.

In a recent TikTok post that racked up over 100,000 views, Sydney said: “Come with me to do a closet clean for Joshua Zirkzee.



“Joshua asked if I could help him reorganise his closet, create a bit more space for new things, and make it all neat and organised.”

The top stylist was drafted in to gut the footballer’s sprawling walk-in, ditching the worn-out clobber to clear a path for new threads that make the United striker look like a slick 90’s rapper.

Sydney reveals that she filters out anything he doesn’t wear or has never worn, plans to sell the decent bits on his behalf and donates the rest to charity.

Footage shows her tackling a mountain of clothes as the clear-out kicked into gear.



The pro wardrobe guru was seen hunting through rows of designer hoodies to decide what stayed and what was benched.

Sydney was tasked with selling off the more high-end clothes or “good items” from Zirzkee’s haul.

In her video, the stylist revealed the remaining gear was packed up and donated to charity.

Sydney was also seen piling and sorting things out in a neat, colour-coded fashion so the footballer’s dressing room was left in immaculate shape.

The freshly cleared rails now sit primed and ready for Zirkzee ahead of the new season.



In another TikTok, Sydney takes fans behind the scenes of a full personal styling job for the Red Devils star.

She starts by asking what he wants, builds a mood board, creates the outfits and once it’s approved, orders everything and delivers them for a fitting.

“Joshua lives in Manchester, so this time we flew to him,” she explains.

Zirkzee wanted to look like a rapper from the 90s – with his own touch.

“I think we did well,” Sydney says.



After the fitting she heads to her hotel for an early night because she’s flying back the next morning.

Sports.title: Unhappy PSG given extra dressing room for Super Cup final vs Aston Villa after complaining to Uefa
Sports.content:
PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN have been given an extra dressing room for the Uefa Super Cup after complaining about the facilities they were initially offered.

The Champions League holders were unhappy with the facilities offered to them ahead of the match against Europa League winners Aston Villa on Wednesday.



They were given the away dressing room at Red Bull Arena in Salzburg, Austria, but told Uefa officials in a meeting on Monday that it was too small.

The French giants allegedly wanted the same size space as Villa – who were allocated the home dressing room – especially considering they are the reigning Super Cup winners.



But instead, Uefa gave them a spare dressing room to make things equal.

That spare dressing room is normally used by the officials.

However, it’s understood that no match officials were moved to accommodate the request.

PSG go into the match as Super Cup holders after beating Tottenham in a penalty shootout last year.

The Ligue 1 side also retained their Champions League crown after beating Arsenal on penalties in May.

Meanwhile, Aston Villa ended their 30-year trophy drought after cruising to a 3-0 win over Freiburg in the Europa League final.

Ahead of the match, boss Unai Emery said: “I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies.

“To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain – the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare with.”

Sports.title: Chelsea have now made over £300MILLION on academy stars in four years as Chalobah and George are latest to be shown door
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’s academy is one of the best in the world.

Not only in terms of the players it has produced for their first team, but in terms of the profit it has produced for the club more recently.



The Blues have made over £300m with the sales of the gems from their academy starlets in the last four seasons alone, with Trevoh Chalobah and Tyrique George being the latest to leave Stamford Bridge after lengthy careers in blue.

Since BlueCo took over the reigns of the club from Roman Abramovich, players have been traded at a rate like never before.



But using Cobham as a money-printing tool is nothing new, with the Russian oligarch also using the academy as a profitable system, selling the likes of Tammy Abraham and Fikayo Tomori for huge fees.

It has always been the case that only the finest to come through Cobham will have long-term futures at Chelsea, while the others will be sold off to make careers elsewhere.



And it is generally a system that is accepted by both the club and its players.

Chelsea need to be careful though, because their academy identity is important to their fans, particularly with the club accused of feeling ‘soulless’ by sections of the support in recent seasons.

Some claim that they feel a lack of connection to the big-money signings who represent their club on the pitch,.

And they miss the days of academy players shining in the first team like they did when Frank Lampard was in charge.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Chalobah was a player who, despite a few shaky moments last season and throughout his career at Chelsea, was utterly ‘proper Chels’ – a commodity that is priceless in modern football.

He joined the Blues as an eight-year-old boy, spending a total of 18 years at the club.

In that time he went from being a promising defender who was sent out on numerous loans, to a first-team regular in the Premier League and the Champions League in recent seasons, and won the Champions League with the club.

But his treatment at Stamford Bridge was not always ideal.

He was exiled from the first team as Chelsea looked for a sale, stripping him of a squad number and leaving him off of their pre-season tour in 2024.



After failing to find a move, they loaned him out to Crystal Palace.

He was having an impressive season in the Premier League before being recalled him due to defensive injuries that meant they needed him once more.

He worked his way back into the first team and never complained, a testament to his professionalism.



Reece James and Levi Colwill now stand as the role models for the abundance of talent in the Blues’ Cobham setup today.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Youngsters like Shim Mheuka, Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, Tayo Suboloye and Jesse Derry will all be optimistic of their chances to make it at Chelsea, despite their continued spending on more and more wonderkids.

But they, and their agents, will also undoubtedly be prepared for the eventuality that only the very best of them will become first-team regulars, at Stamford Bridge at least.

Sports.title: SunRisers beat Super Giants to reach Hundred eliminator
Sports.content:
Reigning champions SunRisers Leeds snatched a spot in the women's Hundred eliminator by beating Manchester Super Giants by 41 runs in a winner-takes-all game at Old Trafford.

In a shoot-out for the final place in the top three, Annabel Sutherland's unbeaten 62 off 36 balls helped Leeds leapfrog their opponents and set up an eliminator clash against Southern Brave.

The Australian all-rounder hit nine boundaries, including three sixes, as the visitors posted 166-4 after being put in to bat.

Visiting spinner Jess Jonassen took 3-21, while Deepti Sharma and Sutherland claimed two wickets apiece, as Manchester were restricted to 125-8 in reply and exited the competition after slipping to fourth place in the standings.

Second-placed Leeds will continue their title defence against Southern Brave on Friday at The Oval, with table-topping Trent Rockets awaiting the winner in Sunday's final at Lord's.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player UNBELIEVABLE athletic fielding from SunRisers' Phoebe Litchfield to prevent a six

Sutherland, the Match Hero, said: "It's the beauty of being an all-rounder, you're in the game all the time, and I love competing, especially in a match we were calling a final. We had to win and it was nice to do a job for the team."

Phoebe Litchfield made her intentions clear after SunRisers were asked to bat, the Aussie opener racing to 27 from 12 deliveries to leapfrog Sophia Dunkley at the top of the competition's run-scoring chart.

An electrifying innings was brought to a halt after Litchfield miscued a drag down from Mady Villiers but Bryony Smith (17 off 16) and Lauren Winfield-Hill (20 off 15) kept the scoreboard ticking.

The Super Giants made a strong start in reply before Jonassen claimed the key scalp of Smriti Mandhana for 28, yorking the Indian with a cleverly-flighted delivery.

Sports.title: Levy goes up against Spurs owners to buy London's NBA Europe team
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham chairman Daniel Levy is vying with a consortium including current Spurs' owners, the Lewis family, to buy NBA Europe's London-based team.

Sky News has revealed that the Lewises are part of a consortium, led by the Checketts family, which has submitted an offer as part of the ongoing auction.

The Checketts have owned or invested in professional sports franchises including Major League Soccer team Real Salt Lake and the NHL's St Louis Blues.

The third leg of the consortium is the Eccles family, who own shares in Burnley FC and Spanish side Espanyol along with the Checketts.

Sky News has previously reported Levy's involvement in a consortium including Liberty Global and MSP Sports Capital, a former backer of McLaren Racing, which is also among the contenders for the NBA London team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kaveh Solhekol examines where Daniel Levy was 'pushed' out of his role as Spurs chairman

London has rapidly become most highly prized of the 12 new NBA Europe outfits, with other teams based in cities such as Berlin, Manchester, Milan, Munich, Paris and Rome.

The NBA wants to generate billions of dollars by selling the rights to the teams, with the first transactions expected in the coming weeks.

Wealthy US families and investors are increasingly buying stakes in sports teams in the UK, especially in football.

Levy left his role as Spurs executive chairman in September 2025 after nearly 25 years in the job.

While the official communication from Spurs and Levy was that he had "stepped down" from the role, it was widely understood that the decision was taken out of his hands.

Sports.title: Floodlights to be on throughout Hundred matches for solar eclipse
Sports.content:
Floodlights will be turned on throughout games in The Hundred on Wednesday due to the solar eclipse.

Up to 90 per cent of the sun will be obscured by the moon during the eclipse, which will occur between 6.17pm and 8.06pm, peaking shortly after 7pm.

It will be the first partial solar eclipse for 27 years and will be visible across Europe, with some places experiencing a total eclipse, where the sun, moon and earth all line up in space.

The light will dim, the temperature will drop and the wind may change direction as the sun disappears behind the moon. After a few minutes the sun will reappear and daylight will return.

There are four games in The Hundred taking place on Wednesday, all of them live on Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at the best moments from this year's Hundred.

Welsh Fire women face London Spirit women at 11.30am in Cardiff, followed by the men's game at 3pm. Birmingham Phoenix women host MI London at Edgbaston from 3pm before the men's teams play each other at 6.30pm.

In anticipation for the solar eclipse, organisers will keep floodlights on throughout all four matches and additional messaging will be issued to fans.

Experts have warned that only special solar eclipse glasses that are certified for the safest eye protection should be used to view the eclipse.

Floodlights will be on 'plenty early' at Kempton

Kempton is all set to stage racing on Wednesday during the solar eclipse.

While the twilight meeting at Ffos Las will begin and end earlier than originally scheduled to ensure all six races take place in daylight, there are no such issues at Kempton due to the floodlights that are in place at the Sunbury circuit.

Image: The floodlights will also be turned on at Kempton race course

The eclipse is expected to occur between 7.02pm and 7.16pm and Kempton has races scheduled to take place at 7pm and 7.30pm.

Kempton's clerk of the course Barney Clifford said: "The last one was nearly 30 years ago so I wasn't quite at Kempton then. I remember it but there were no floodlights in those days!

"I'm going to put the floodlights on early doors. I know they have predicted a time for it but you don't quite know how much of the sun is going to be covered and for what race so we'll have the lights on plenty early enough."
