Sports.title: Liam Paro Insists He Wants Devin Haney Fight, Hears Nothing
Sports.content:
“Haney is ducking me,” Paro told Fox Sports Australia. “I’ve said I’m good to fight by the end of October, and we ain’t heard a thing.”

Paro also rejected the idea that his financial demands caused negotiations to stall.

“I’ll fight him next, no worries. You know I’ll fight anyone. And I’ve proved that my whole career. I’ll fight him in his backyard or mine.”

The former IBF champion may have more to offer Haney commercially than Catterall. Paro brings name recognition and interest from the Australian market. Despite his loss to Richardson Hitchins, he remains a rugged southpaw with enough power and physical strength to make Haney work.

Catterall involves a different type of difficulty. He is a defensive southpaw who moves, potshots, pulls away when opponents close distance, and frequently ties up. That could produce a difficult tactical contest for Haney without necessarily generating the same financial upside as facing Paro.

Catterall’s willingness to step in still gives Haney an important bargaining chip. His manager, Sam Jones, says they have accepted the proposed date and location while accusing Paro of wanting too much money.

Haney also received some unwelcome news from Ryan Garcia this week. Garcia placed Teofimo Lopez, Rolando Romero, and Shakur Stevenson among the opponents he wants after facing Conor Benn on September 12.

“I’m not in a rush to make that fight happen,” Ryan told The Ring about facing Haney again. “They have to sit with that loss.”

That leaves Haney needing someone to fight. Paro may think the silence means Haney is avoiding him, but it may simply be Team Haney waiting to see which welterweight gives them the better deal.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma Talks Like Heavyweight’s Old Guard At 21
Sports.content:
“I like Leo Atang. He’s very decent, and he’s a nice kid as well,” Itauma told DAZN News. “I like Adam Olayinan, the guy who’s just signed with Queensberry. I watched his fight the other day, and that was very good as well. “Obviously that Teremoana, he looks decent. They’re probably the ones I’m looking at for the young guns coming up. They all look decent.”

Teremoana is about to turn 29, competed in the Olympics, and trails Itauma by only three professional bouts. Calling him one of the “young guns coming up” seems odd coming from a fighter eight years his junior.

The difference is that Itauma has been pushed much faster and surrounded by considerably more hype. Wins over Dillian Whyte, Demsey McKean, Jermaine Franklin, and Mariusz Wach have helped move him up the heavyweight rankings and create the impression that he has already graduated beyond prospect status.

Those names look better on a record than the opponents the Australian Olympian has faced, but Teremoana hasn’t been given the same type of matchmaking. He has the size and punching power to potentially run through that same tier of fighters.

Itauma gets his opportunity to show how good he really is when he faces Filip Hrgovic on August 29. Hrgovic is a significant step up from the opposition Itauma has been beating and should give a better indication of where he belongs in the division.

Until then, it’s a bit early for a 21-year-old with only three more professional fights than Teremoana to talk like an established heavyweight watching the up-and-comers work their way toward him.

Sports.title: Jerry Quarry Destroys Earnie Shavers in 141 Seconds
Sports.content:
Both fighters were 28. Quarry weighed 202 pounds, eight lighter than Shavers.

The buildup had almost guaranteed violence. Quarry predicted three rounds and believed he could finish Shavers in one if his opponent came after him. Don King, then part of Shavers’ management team, called it their easiest fight. Madison Square Garden matchmaker Teddy Brenner went further, predicting the shortest 12-round fight in history. He wasn’t far off.

Trainer Gil Clancy wanted Quarry to box, but Quarry abandoned that idea almost immediately. Instead of giving Shavers room to unleash his power, he attacked him.

Quarry drove Shavers toward the ropes and unloaded lefts and rights to the head. Shavers managed to move away, but Quarry followed him across the ring and dropped him with a left-right combination.

Shavers got back up, only to find Quarry waiting for him. Quarry poured on punches as Shavers struggled to defend himself. His eyes looked unfocused, and he was taking clean shots without answering effectively. Referee Arthur Mercante had seen enough and stopped the fight at 2:21 of the opening round. There would be no need for judges Jack Gordon and Bill Recht.

The result was stunning because Quarry had beaten the knockout artist by fighting him at his own game. George Foreman, Joe Frazier, and Muhammad Ali were among the prominent names at ringside. Foreman reportedly expressed surprise that Quarry had chosen to trade with Shavers and came away impressed by his aggression.

Ali and Frazier had another reason to be at the Garden. Their January 28, 1974 rematch was already set for the same arena and was promoted during the Quarry-Shavers telecast. Frazier discussed getting his weight down and preparing for Ali before the main event, while viewers were urged to buy tickets for their second fight.

Their rematch also strengthened Quarry’s position in the heavyweight picture. With Ali and Frazier committed to fighting each other, the broadcast team noted that neither man would likely be available for Foreman until around June. Quarry’s destruction of Shavers suddenly made him an obvious candidate to challenge the champion before then.

Quarry paid a physical price despite the short night. He injured his left wrist after landing a hook high on Shavers’ head, with reports raising concern over a possible fracture.

Shavers later admitted that the first heavy blows had left him unable to recover. He regretted rising so quickly after the knockdown, believing that taking more of the count might have given him enough time to survive the remaining seconds of the round.

Nearly 15,000 spectators had come expecting to see what happened when Shavers’ frightening power collided with Quarry’s durability and experience. They barely had time to settle into their seats.

The official attendance was 14,962, producing a gate of $201,564. Quarry was guaranteed $40,000 against 30 percent of the gate, while Shavers received $30,000 against 27½ percent.

The victory strengthened Quarry’s position near the top of a stacked division ruled by Foreman, but the championship opportunity never followed. Quarry instead met Frazier again the following year and was stopped in five rounds.

Shavers rebuilt his career and eventually challenged both Ali and Larry Holmes for the heavyweight championship.

Neither man’s later career changed what happened that December night. Shavers arrived with the reputation as a devastating slugger, but Quarry never gave him enough time to use it.

For 141 seconds, Quarry simply beat him to the punch.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Wants Haney To Stew In Loss
Sports.content:
“I’m not in a rush to make that fight happen. They have to sit with that loss,” Ryan told The Ring. “Why do I have to beg for it? I’m here. I’m about to beat up Conor Benn. I want Teofimo Lopez, Rolando Romero and Shakur Stevenson. I have a lot of options. I’m not really worried about Haney now. If it happens, it happens.”

What happened in April 2024 remains the source of the hostility. Garcia dropped Haney three times and won a majority decision before the victory was changed to a no-contest following his positive test for ostarine.

Devin and Bill Haney have repeatedly brought up the failed test since then, refusing to treat the original outcome as a legitimate defeat. Drug testing has also been a recurring subject whenever another fight with Garcia has been discussed.

Ryan’s refusal to rush into a rematch sounds personal. He has the WBC welterweight title, a September fight with Benn, and several lucrative opponents he can pursue without giving Haney an opportunity to settle the score.

“All these guys obviously have to come to me,” Ryan said. “I’m definitely the lottery fight. If you want to be a huge name, I’m the guy to do it [against]. You have to get through me.”

That is the position Garcia believes he occupies. After two years of hearing why his performance against Haney shouldn’t count, he doesn’t seem interested in helping Team Haney put it behind them.

They can sit with it.

Sports.title: Archie Moore Rallies To Stop Harold Johnson In 14
Sports.content:
Moore weighed 173 pounds to Johnson’s 172½.

Working behind his jab, movement and counterpunching, Johnson frustrated Moore through much of the early and middle rounds. His advantage grew in the 10th when a right hand behind the ear dropped the champion.

Moore rose quickly, but referee Ruby Goldstein continued counting, overlooking that the automatic eight-count had been waived for the championship fight. Moore recovered and continued pursuing Johnson.

The challenger remained in front as the fight moved into the late rounds. Two officials had Johnson leading after 13, putting Moore in danger of losing his championship on the scorecards.

Then Moore changed the fight. He hurt Johnson late in the 13th and attacked immediately when the 14th began. A barrage of rights and lefts drove Johnson into his own corner before sending him to the canvas.

Johnson regained his feet, but he was badly hurt. Moore followed him along the ropes and continued punching until Goldstein stopped the fight at 56 seconds of the 14th round.

The comeback preserved Moore’s championship and extended his winning streak to 19 fights. Johnson had come within two rounds of taking the title from a rival he had first fought in 1949.

Moore soon resumed his pursuit of heavyweight champion Rocky Marciano. He received the opportunity the following year, dropping Marciano before being stopped in the ninth round.

Johnson never received the sixth Moore fight he wanted. Years later, he became light heavyweight champion himself.

Their August 1954 battle closed a five-fight rivalry with its most dramatic ending. Johnson had the lead, but the Old Mongoose found the punches he needed before time ran out.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Escalates Fury-Joshua Fight Over MSG
Sports.content:
“We signed for this fight in the UK,” Hearn said to Fighthype. “We are desperate to deliver this fight for UK fans. However, everybody else wants the fight in America: Turki Alalshikh, Netflix. I can’t speak on behalf of Tyson Fury; I don’t see him kicking up a fuss. Madison Square Garden. So, they’re telling us this is the place it’s going to do the biggest numbers, this is the place it’ll be the biggest fight.”

Hearn has made his preference for Britain clear for weeks. What changes the discussion is how far he now sounds prepared to push the disagreement.

“I disagree. But at the end we’ll fight, and we’ll fight, and we’ll fight to a point where they’ve breached the contract by doing it in America, or we come to an agreement.”

That is strong language considering Hearn’s business relationship with Alalshikh and the number of major events Matchroom has staged with his involvement.

Hearn also admits the people on the other side of the venue dispute are key allies, making his willingness to discuss a potential breach of agreement more surprising.

His stated reason is loyalty to British boxing fans. But if Madison Square Garden really produces the bigger commercial event, Hearn’s resistance becomes harder to explain purely as a business decision.

There is also no indication that Fury shares Hearn’s resistance to New York. Hearn concedes he doesn’t see Fury “kicking up a fuss” about Madison Square Garden, potentially leaving Matchroom as the strongest opposition to the proposed move.

The dispute has therefore moved beyond a simple choice between Britain and New York. Hearn is now openly discussing how far Matchroom will go to enforce the agreement it signed.

Sports.title: Conor Benn Embraces Underdog Role Against Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Eubank was already in his mid-30s for those fights, yet bookmakers still favored him. That was understandable given how thin Benn’s resume was against top opposition before their rivalry.

The rematch also came with weight conditions affecting the naturally larger Eubank. More importantly, Eubank wasn’t the type of dangerous one-punch counterpuncher Benn will encounter against Garcia.

His previous opponent did much of his damage through combinations and was no longer at his peak. Garcia presents a different threat with a lightning-fast left hook that has produced some of his biggest knockdowns.

Benn’s aggressive style gives Garcia opportunities to land that shot. Charging forward into exchanges worked in earlier bouts, but those attacks can put him directly in range of Garcia’s best weapon.

The September fight will test Benn’s assertion that he performs best when doubted. This isn’t another meeting with an aging veteran. He’s facing a dangerous puncher in his own division with the exact weapon to punish the aggression he relies on.

Sports.title: Osleys Iglesias Faces Oliver Zaren October 8
Sports.content:
The matchup gives Iglesias a challenger who has yet to lose as a professional. Zaren is 19-0 with one draw and seven knockouts and has spent most of his career fighting in Europe.

Iglesias, 15-0 with 14 knockouts, captured the vacant IBF title by stopping Pavel Silyagin in the eighth round in April in Montreal. The Cuban southpaw had already established himself as one of the division’s biggest punchers before winning the belt.

Zaren had been linked to Iglesias several weeks ago after withdrawing from negotiations for a European title fight against Jose Luis Navarro. Those talks never produced a fight, opening the door for his first world title opportunity.

The fight also keeps Iglesias at super middleweight after a possible meeting with WBC middleweight champion Carlos Adames failed to come together earlier this year.

Zaren faces a massive jump in competition. Iglesias has stopped 14 of his 15 professional opponents, including Silyagin, Petro Ivanov and Evgeny Shvedenko.

The Danish challenger has never faced anyone with Iglesias’ combination of power and experience at this level. Zaren will have to prove quickly that his success against European opposition prepared him for a champion who has rarely needed the scorecards.

Ghana News.title: GBA has no business responding to law firms’ petitions – Dafeamekpor
Ghana News.content:
The Majority Chief Whip and President of the Ghana Law Society, Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor, has criticised the Ghana Bar Association (GBA) for responding to concerns raised by law firms over the availability of lawyers during proceedings on the petition against the Chief Justice.

According to him, the Association has no basis to respond to the petitions because they were issued by law firms rather than individual lawyers who are members of the association.

“GBA has no business responding to statements from non-members of the GBA,” Mr Dafeamekpor said on Newsnite on Joy FM.

He explained that lawyers and law firms are separately licensed, with lawyers licensed by the General Legal Council (GLC) to practise while law firms are also separately licensed.

“The petition in question is not coming from lawyers. It's coming from law firms. Check the petitions. It's not the lawyers who are complaining. It's the law firms,” he said on August 11.

Mr Dafeamekpor questioned whether the GBA should be responding to concerns from entities that are not members of the association.

“Are law firms that are complaining that their lawyers are not available, are they members of the GBA?” he asked.

He maintained that if individual lawyers had concerns about their ability to practise during the proceedings, they should have petitioned the Chief Justice in their capacity as lawyers rather than through their firms.

“So if you want to petition the CJ, petition on your terms as a lawyer. Don't petition on your letterhead as a firm. Then it is the firm that is sending the petition,” he said.

Mr Dafeamekpor further challenged the substantive basis of the complaints, arguing that law firms with several lawyers on their rolls should have been able to make alternative arrangements to ensure that cases before the courts were handled.

He cited the firms of Sam Okudzeto and lawyer Akyea as examples, saying they have more than 20 and 15 lawyers respectively listed as members of their firms.

“How is it possible that none of these lawyers are able to work during the petition?” he questioned.

Drawing on his own experience with legal proceedings, Mr Dafeamekpor said senior lawyers could delegate matters to senior associates or other lawyers within their firms when they were required elsewhere.

“I have also participated extensively before, and during the petition, seniors can ask even senior associates on the firm to hold their brief in a matter that may have been listed to be continued during the petition,” he said.

He consequently dismissed suggestions that the lawyers’ participation in the proceedings had created an unusual situation for the affected law firms.

“My suspicion here is that there's nothing untoward in this matter. And so the GBA is just blowing hot air,” Mr Dafeamekpor said.

He further described the GBA’s position "pure politics."

Ghana News.title: NPP accuses Chief Justice of partisan bias over vacation trial warrants
Ghana News.content:
The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has accused Chief Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie of exhibiting a “partisan disposition” and facilitating “selective justice” by issuing special warrants for two High Court judges to conduct substantive criminal trials during the legal vacation.

In a statement dated Tuesday, August 11, and signed by General Secretary Justin Kodua Frimpong, the party said it was “deeply troubled” by the Chief Justice’s defence of the warrants granted to Justices Francis Achibonga and Audrey Kocuvie-Tay.

The NPP questioned why only the two courts had been authorised to conduct full criminal trials when other vacation courts across the country were handling mainly motions and urgent interlocutory applications.

“The Chief Justice has failed to answer one simple question. Why only these two courts, and why only these cases?” the party said.

The party said the affected cases all involve persons associated with the NPP, including former National Signals Bureau Director-General Kwabena Adu-Boahene and former National Food Buffer Stock Company (NAFCO) Chief Executive Officer Hanan Abdul-Wahab.

The two are facing criminal proceedings over allegations including causing financial loss to the state.

The NPP argued that the decision to continue their trials during the vacation amounted to unequal treatment.

“If the vacation can pause the trial of a murder suspect, why can it not pause the trial of political opponents of the Government?” the party asked.

It described what it called “selective urgency” as evidence of an alleged agenda to incarcerate NPP personalities.

The party also compared the development to what it described as the “indecent haste” surrounding the trial and conviction of Ashanti Regional Chairman Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi.

The NPP said defence lawyers in the affected cases, including Zoe, Akyea & Co. and Dame & Partners, wrote to the Chief Justice on August 5 notifying him of their unavailability during the legal vacation and asking that the warrants be withdrawn.

It said the Ghana Bar Association subsequently petitioned the Chief Justice on August 10, reminding him of what it considers the established practice that Vacation Courts do not conduct substantive trials.

Despite the petitions, the warrants remain in force.

The Chief Justice has defended the arrangement, saying decisions on adjournments are matters for the courts and cannot simply be treated as administrative issues arising from the legal vacation.

The party also cited proceedings on Tuesday, August 11, in one of the affected cases, where a vacation judge reportedly adjourned proceedings for less than a week after defence counsel indicated they were unavailable.

According to the NPP, the judge directed the accused to secure new lawyers within the period or personally conduct the cross-examination of a prosecution witness.

The party said the judge indicated that he would continue sitting until the Chief Justice revoked the warrant.

Ghana News.title: Political parties must stop being ‘seasonal electoral machines’ – Asiedu Nketia
Ghana News.content:
Johnson Asiedu Nketia, National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress

National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketia, has called for major reforms within African political parties, arguing that they must move beyond their traditional focus on winning elections and become permanent institutions for democratic governance.

He said political parties could not credibly defend democracy at the national level if they failed to uphold democratic principles within their own structures.

Mr Asiedu Nketia made the call on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation Democracy Dialogue in Bauchi, Nigeria.

The dialogue, held under the theme "Beyond Elections: Can Political Parties and the Judiciary Save African Democracy?", brought together political leaders, members of the judiciary, civil society representatives and other stakeholders to discuss the future of democracy on the continent.

Speaking on a panel on political parties and the judiciary, Mr Asiedu Nketia said political parties had responsibilities that extended beyond organising campaigns and contesting elections.

"Political parties cannot save democracy when they function only as electoral machines, instruments of patronage or vehicles for individual ambition," he said.

He described political parties as important public and constitutional institutions responsible for recruiting leaders, developing alternative policies, organising political participation and connecting citizens to the state.

"A party that demands credible national elections must conduct credible internal elections. A party that condemns authoritarianism in government must tolerate legitimate disagreement within its own structures," he said.

Cost of politics

Mr Asiedu Nketia identified the rising cost of political participation as one of the major threats to internal party democracy.

He cited research by the Westminster Foundation for Democracy and CDD-Ghana which found that the cost of contesting parliamentary office increased by 59 per cent between the 2012 and 2016 electoral cycles, reaching an average of GH¢389,803.

He also cited a later CDD-Ghana study which estimated that a viable parliamentary campaign by 2020, including the cost of maintaining a constituency presence, could cost approximately GH¢4 million.

He warned that the high cost of political participation could result in political parties selecting candidates based more on their financial capacity than their competence.

"When entry into political leadership becomes this expensive, parties risk selecting the wealthiest rather than the most capable, while elected officials may enter office burdened by financiers and expectations of repayment," he said.

He called for reforms to reduce the financial barriers to political participation and ensure that people without wealthy sponsors could compete for political office.

Women and youth

Mr Asiedu Nketia also criticised the limited representation of women and young people in political leadership.

He noted that women occupied only 40 of Ghana's 276 parliamentary seats, representing 14.5 per cent, although women constitute slightly more than half of the country's population.

Young people between the ages of 15 and 35, he said, constituted 38.2 per cent of Ghana's population, yet no member of the current Parliament was aged 30 or younger at the beginning of the legislature.

He urged political parties to create practical pathways for women and young people to progress from campaign mobilisation into policy development, party leadership, Parliament and executive responsibility.

"Political parties must create practical pathways that move women and young people beyond rallies and campaign mobilisation into policy development, party leadership, Parliament and executive responsibility," he said.

Parties need policy institutions

Mr Asiedu Nketia further called on political parties to rebuild their policy, civic education and leadership-development functions.

He said parties should maintain permanent research institutions, train candidates and office holders and develop systems to assess governments formed in their name.

"Democracy suffers when public office becomes the first place at which political leaders begin to learn the responsibilities of government," he said.

He argued that parties should be judged not only by their ability to win elections but also by the quality of leaders they produce and the policies they develop.

'Power is temporary'

Mr Asiedu Nketia said political parties should not be treated as the private property of founders, financiers, office holders or temporary leaders.

He said democratic parties must practise internally the principles they promise to uphold when elected to government.

Concluding his argument, he urged political parties across Africa to abandon the approach of becoming active only during election periods.

"Political parties must cease to be seasonal electoral machines and become permanent democratic institutions," he said.

He added that political parties must remember that political power is temporary and that the state ultimately belongs to the people.

Ghana News.title: Jatikay Centre backs National Security reorganisation, urges focus on emerging threats
Ghana News.content:
The Jatikay Centre for Human Security and Peace Building has welcomed the reorganisation of the National Security Council Secretariat, describing it as an opportunity to strengthen Ghana’s national security architecture and improve the country’s preparedness to deal with emerging threats.

The Centre, in a press release signed by its Executive Director, Adib Saani, congratulated the newly appointed officials, including Maj. Gen. William Ayamdo (Rtd.), who has been appointed Deputy National Security Coordinator responsible for Operations.

It said the restructuring should be used to improve intelligence coordination, operational effectiveness, accountability and preventive security measures.

According to the Centre, one of the immediate priorities for the new leadership should be the growing threat of violent extremism and possible terrorist spillover from the Sahel into Ghana.

It cited developments in Burkina Faso and other parts of the Sahel as requiring Ghana to strengthen intelligence gathering, border surveillance and regional intelligence cooperation.

The Centre also called for greater investment in the resilience of vulnerable communities, particularly in northern Ghana, where proximity to areas affected by violent extremism presents additional security concerns.

Chieftaincy, land conflicts

Beyond external threats, the Jatikay Centre said the new security leadership must pay greater attention to chieftaincy, land and communal disputes, which it described as significant internal security risks.

It noted that Ghana has hundreds of unresolved chieftaincy, land and ethnic disputes, with some classified as high-risk conflicts capable of destabilising communities.

The Centre further identified organised crime, illicit financial flows, money laundering, illegal gold trading and cross-border criminal networks as areas requiring stronger attention.

It said although such activities might appear primarily economic, they have direct national security implications because their proceeds can fuel corruption, organised criminal activities and other destabilising activities.

The Jatikay Centre said the success of the reorganisation should ultimately be measured not simply by changes in personnel, but by the Secretariat’s ability to anticipate threats before they escalate, disrupt criminal networks, improve intelligence coordination and protect citizens while respecting the rule of law and human rights.

It expressed readiness to support the new security leadership with research, expertise and civil society perspectives to strengthen Ghana’s human and national security.

Ghana News.title: ‘Case may not continue without counsel’ – Samson Lardy Anyenini on Adu-Boahene trial
Ghana News.content:
Private legal practitioner Samson Lardy Anyenini has questioned whether the ongoing criminal trial involving former National Signals Bureau Director Kwabena Adu-Boahene can proceed if his defence lawyer is unavailable during the legal vacation.

Speaking on Joy FM's Top Story on Tuesday, August 11, Mr Anyenini said while he does not disagree with the Chief Justice’s position on the need to expedite the determination of cases, he believes the absence of defence counsel could affect the continuation of the trial.

“I think that eventually we may find, and the case may not continue without counsel,” he said.

His comments follow the decision by lead counsel for Mr Adu-Boahene and his wife, Angela Adjei Boateng, Samuel Atta Akyea, to stay away from court on Tuesday, August 11.

Mr Atta Akyea has justified his absence by arguing that the legal vacation is traditionally a period set aside to allow lawyers to rest after extensive courtroom work.

Mr Anyenini, who has practised law for decades, said his own experience has been that lawyers have traditionally been permitted to take a break from court proceedings during the vacation.

“I was called to the Bar 50 years ago. I have been an active practitioner in the courts. I go to court almost on a daily basis,” he said.

“I have done criminal cases, including in the lower courts, which are not on vacation as we speak. But during vacations, judges have indulged me and have indulged my colleagues, even in the lower courts, to stay away during the vacation and then we resume,” he added.

Mr Anyenini therefore suggested that the practical application of the Chief Justice’s directive could depend on whether defence counsel is available to participate in the proceedings.

He also challenged the notion that lawyers should be compelled to conduct substantive trials during the vacation, drawing on his own long experience at the Bar.

“I would respectfully ask you to ask him if he has ever been compelled to conduct a case during the vacation since he was called to the Bar,” he said, referring to the Deputy Attorney General.

Mr Anyenini stressed that his position is based largely on his experience of legal practice and the longstanding approach to court proceedings during vacation periods.

This comes at a time the High Court in Accra has technically given former Director-General of the National Signals Bureau (NSB) and his wife, Angela Adjei Boateng, six days to secure the presence of their lawyers for the continuation of their trial on August 17.

The court warned that if they fail to appear with counsel on the next adjourned date, they will be required to personally continue the cross-examination of the fourth prosecution witness.

Justice Francis Apangabonu Achibonga, a Justice of the Court of Appeal sitting as an additional High Court judge, further directed that if the accused persons fail to conduct the cross-examination themselves, the witness will be discharged.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s democratic progress is not irreversible – Asiedu Nketia
Ghana News.content:
Johnson Asiedu Nketia, National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress

National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketia, has cautioned against complacency over Ghana's democratic record, warning that the country's progress can be reversed if political actors and institutions fail to protect democratic gains.

Mr Asiedu Nketia said Ghana's experience since the beginning of the Fourth Republic demonstrated that peaceful transfers of political power were possible in Africa, but said the country still faced significant threats, particularly election-related violence.

He was speaking at the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation Democracy Dialogue in Bauchi, Nigeria, on Tuesday, August 11, 2026.

The dialogue was held under the theme "Beyond Elections: Can Political Parties and the Judiciary Save African Democracy?"

Mr Asiedu Nketia said Ghana had held nine consecutive general elections since 1992, with four of those elections—in 2000, 2008, 2016 and 2024—resulting in transfers of power between political parties.

He said the record demonstrated that an African governing party could lose power, transfer authority peacefully and subsequently return to government through the ballot box rather than force.

2008 election

He cited Ghana's 2008 presidential election as an important example of how political actors could protect democratic stability even when election results were extremely close.

Professor John Evans Atta Mills won the election with 50.23 per cent of the vote against 49.77 per cent for Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo.

The difference between the two candidates was less than one percentage point.

Mr Asiedu Nketia said the ability of political leaders, institutions and citizens to prevent such a close contest from developing into a national crisis was an important democratic achievement.

Concessions and peaceful transitions

He also cited the 2016 election, when then-President John Dramani Mahama conceded defeat and supervised a peaceful transition to the incoming administration.

He said the 2024 election provided another example of the importance of political concessions, noting that then-Vice-President Mahamudu Bawumia conceded before the formal declaration after his party's collation indicated that the result could not be overturned.

"These concessions were not ceremonial courtesies; they were constitutional contributions," Mr Asiedu Nketia said.

He said peaceful concessions demonstrated a willingness by political actors to place constitutional order above political interests.

Warning from 2020

However, he warned that Ghana's democratic reputation should not create a false sense of security.

He pointed to the 2020 general election, which produced a Parliament comprising 137 members from each of the two major parties and one independent member.

Despite the peaceful outcome at the parliamentary level, Mr Asiedu Nketia said eight lives were reportedly lost through election-related violence.

"This reminds us that democratic progress is never irreversible," he said.

He argued that democracy should therefore not be assessed only by whether elections were held but also by how political parties behave before, during and after elections.

Democracy beyond election day

Mr Asiedu Nketia said elections only determined who received the authority to govern and did not guarantee that power would subsequently be exercised within constitutional limits.

"Elections determine who receives the authority to govern. They do not, by themselves, determine whether that authority will be exercised lawfully, whether constitutional limits will be respected, whether the opposition will remain legitimate or whether government will improve the lives of the people," he said.

He said the true test of democracy occurred between elections, when governments made decisions, institutions exercised their powers and citizens demanded accountability.

"Democracy is therefore tested not only on election day, but in every decision taken between one election and the next," he said.

Protecting democratic gains

Mr Asiedu Nketia called for greater cooperation among political parties, electoral bodies, the judiciary, civil society, the media and academic institutions to address potential political crises before they escalate.

He said dialogue should not begin only when an election dispute threatened national stability.

He also urged political parties to strengthen internal democracy, improve inclusion and reduce the financial barriers to political participation.

"The future of African democracy will not be secured merely by conducting more elections," he said.

According to him, democratic stability would depend on institutions that make elections meaningful, governments accountable, constitutional limits effective and peaceful transfers of power normal.

He said Ghana's experience offered useful lessons for other African countries, but the country itself needed to continue protecting and strengthening its democratic institutions.

Ghana News.title: Traditional faith practitioners appeal for inclusion in national activities
Ghana News.content:
Traditional faith-based practitioners have appealed to the government to formally include their practice in national activities.

They argue that years of exclusion from state programmes and national events have eroded the role of traditional practice in Ghana’s cultural landscape.

The appeal was made during a mass registration, licensing, and sensitisation programme for traditional, indigenous, and faith-based healing practitioners in the Ashanti Region.

The programme was organised by the Trado-Afrikan Faith Healers Association (TAFHA) in collaboration with the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy, and Religious Affairs and the Traditional Medicine Practice Council.

Held at the Kumasi Centre for National Culture under the theme “Building a Recognized and Regulated Traditional Healing Sector in Ghana,” the event brought together hundreds of practitioners to register, receive licences, and be sensitised on regulatory requirements and best practices.

Speaking to the media, the Acting General Secretary of the Trado-Afrikan Faith Healers Association (TAFHA), Jonathan Q. Attoh (Dzogbana), underscored the importance of recognising traditional faith in the country.

He said traditional healing and spirituality form an integral part of Ghanaian identity and must be accorded the same respect and inclusion given to other religious and health practices.

According to him, acknowledging the role of traditional faith in national life will not only preserve Ghana’s cultural heritage but also strengthen unity and promote holistic healthcare delivery.

Mr. Attoh recalled that during the era of Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, traditionalists were given a prominent role in national celebrations and were allowed to pour libations during Independence Day ceremonies. He said that practice reflected the recognition and respect accorded to Ghana’s indigenous spirituality and cultural values at the time.

However, he lamented that in recent years, the country no longer grants that same opportunity to traditionalists.

“We used to honour the ancestors who fought for our independence at the 6th March ceremony. For some years now, the traditional faith has been excluded from national activities, and that approach is not sustainable. Libation is not just a ritual. It is a prayer, a way of connecting with our ancestors and asking for blessings for the nation. When we leave it out of our national events, we are leaving out a part of who we are as Ghanaians,” he stated.

Mr Attoh also expressed concern over the exclusion of traditional faith practitioners from the National Day of Thanksgiving and Prayers activities. He urged the government to grant traditionalists equal recognition and participation as accorded to Christian and Muslim faiths.

“Traditionalists must not be treated as spectators in matters of national prayer and thanksgiving. We are part of this country too, and we deserve the same opportunity to pray for the nation as is given to Christian and Muslim leaders. We are calling on the government through the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy, and Religious Affairs to integrate us into national programmes," he said.

Midao Kadevi, Acting President of the Trado-Afrikan Faith Healers Association (TAFHA), said the association was established in response to the growing need for a strong, credible, and inclusive national institution.

According to him, TAFHA differs from conventional professional associations in both structure and mandate.

He explained that the association operates as a federation of practice groups, a model designed to bring together the diverse indigenous healing traditions in Ghana under one national framework.

This structure, he said will ensure that every recognized indigenous healing tradition retains the autonomy to preserve its unique customs, beliefs, leadership structures, and methods of practice while also benefiting from collective representation.

Midao Kadevi concluded that by working together under this federation, member groups advance shared objectives, including professional development, adherence to ethical standards, compliance with regulatory requirements, and the pursuit of formal national recognition for both the traditional healing sector and national activities.

Officials from the Traditional Medicine Practice Council and the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy, and Religious Affairs used the platform to educate practitioners on licensing requirements, ethical standards, and collaboration with orthodox health institutions.

The registration exercise forms part of broader efforts to build a formal, regulated traditional healing sector that ensures safety, accountability, and public trust.

The Acting Vice President of TAFHA, Nana Abass, said the mass registration will help create a database of credible practitioners and weed out quacks while also positioning traditional healing as a key partner in achieving universal health coverage.

He pledged their commitment to work with government and relevant stakeholders to ensure traditional healing is given its rightful place in Ghana’s health and cultural systems.

He called on law enforcement agencies to intensify efforts to identify, arrest, and prosecute individuals posing as traditional herbalists without proper certification.

He stressed that the rise of fake practitioners undermines public trust, endangers patient safety, and tarnishes the reputation of legitimate traditional medicine in Ghana.

Nana Baffour A.K. Ababio II, Otumfuo Saramanhene, urged traditionalists to align their practices with modern standards. He emphasised the need for them to improve their professional appearance and ensure that shrine premises are well-maintained and hygienic.

According to him, such changes will enhance public perception and promote greater respect for indigenous healing traditions in contemporary society.

In attendance were representatives of the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy, and Religious Affairs; the Ministry of Health; and Dr. (MH) Yakubu T. Yusuf, Registrar/CEO of the Traditional Medicine Practice Council.

Ghana News.title: Major General Ayamdo named Deputy National Security Coordinator for Operations
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has approved a reorganisation of the National Security Council Secretariat, appointing former Chief of Army Staff Major General (Rtd.) William Ayamdo as Deputy National Security Coordinator in charge of Operations.

The changes, announced by Presidential Spokesperson and Minister for Government Communications Felix Kwakye Ofosu, take immediate effect.

Major General Ayamdo, who retired from the Ghana Armed Forces in 2020, brings extensive military and intelligence experience to the new role.

He previously served as Director General of Defence Intelligence and headed the Counter Terrorism Unit under the National Security Council Secretariat.

Yaw Donkor reassigned

As part of the reorganisation, former National Security Coordinator Yaw Donkor has been reassigned to the Office of the National Security Advisor as Director of Intelligence and Research.

Mr Donkor served as National Security Coordinator during President Mahama’s first administration from 2014 to 2017.

Other appointments announced as part of the changes include Adamu Saaka as Director of Logistics and Transport and Faustina Effah-Boadi as Officer in Charge of the Human Security Department.

DCOP (Rtd.) Peter Ndekugri has also been appointed Officer in Charge of the Special Investigations Unit.

Meanwhile, ACP Alhassan Osman has been reassigned to the Ghana Police Service for further deployment, ending his current assignment at the National Security Council Secretariat.

The reorganisation comes as the Mahama administration seeks to realign Ghana’s national security architecture.

President Mahama had earlier appointed former Chief of Staff Prosper Douglas Bani as National Security Advisor, while DCOP Abdul-Osman Razak serves as National Security Coordinator.

Parliament has also passed the Security and Intelligence Agencies Bill, 2025, which introduces reforms to Ghana’s security and intelligence architecture, including the renaming of the National Investigations Bureau as the Bureau of National Intelligence.

The latest changes come against the backdrop of wider discussions about the structure and legal basis of Ghana’s national security institutions.

The National Security Council Secretariat has faced constitutional scrutiny, with some analysts questioning its status and arguing that the 1992 Constitution does not expressly provide for a permanent bureaucratic secretariat separate from the constitutionally recognised security and intelligence agencies.

The latest appointments are expected to strengthen operational coordination, intelligence gathering and specialised security functions within the national security architecture.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
