World.title: Rarara’s attack song normal in politics, Kwankwaso tells Pantami
World.content:
Former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Kwankwaso, has criticised former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Isa Pantami, over a recent song by Dauda Rarara, a prominent political praise singer associated with the All Progressives Congress (APC) and President Bola Tinubu.

Mr Kwankwaso, the presidential running mate in the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), said Mr Pantami should not be surprised by his criticism in the song because, by entering partisan politics, he has exposed himself to the attacks that politicians routinely face.

He spoke in an interview with DCL Hausa on Tuesday.

‘Rarara has attacked me, Shekarau, Ganduje’

Mr Kwankwaso, who has himself been targeted by Rarara’s political songs in the past, described the singer’s attack on Mr Pantami as a form of political retribution.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, Mr Pantami had previously used harsh language against him, but he chose not to respond in kind.

“Rarara has insulted me; he has also insulted Shekarau, Ganduje and many other people here in Kano. Yet, we handled it better because we are politicians,” Mr Kwankwaso said.

He was referring to former Kano governors Ibrahim Shekarau and Abdullahi Ganduje, who, like him, have had political differences with Rarara over the years.

Mr Kwankwaso said the controversy surrounding the song was a consequence of Mr Pantami’s decision to move from religious preaching into active partisan politics.

“That is why we say: once you abandon religious preaching and enter politics, you should not expect politicians to treat you as a religious cleric. What Rarara did to Pantami is only the beginning; it is nothing more than a welcome to politics,” he said.

Kwankwaso recalls past clashes with Pantami

Mr Kwankwaso also recalled an occasion when Mr Pantami allegedly attacked his personality in the presence of his supporters.

“Pantami once hurled all sorts of insults at me in the presence of my supporters. I was the one who asked them to calm down and not react,” he said.

He added that there was another occasion when his supporters attempted to confront Mr Pantami.

“There was even a time when my supporters tried to deal with him in Kano because of the way he attacked my personality,” Mr Kwankwaso said.

He argued that Mr Pantami should now understand that political engagement entails criticism from opponents and other political actors.

Pantami’s move into politics

Mr Pantami, a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy and prominent Islamic scholar, is running for governor in Gombe State.

He initially sought the APC ticket but withdrew from the party’s primary in May, alleging violations of the Electoral Act 2026 and irregularities in the process.

He subsequently joined the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and emerged as the candidate of the Nyesom Wike-led faction.

His entry into partisan politics has also revived scrutiny of his past comments about the PDP, particularly his criticism of the party. At the same time, he was an Islamic preacher and later a minister under the APC administration.

Mr Kwankwaso highlighted this apparent political reversal in his criticism of the former minister.

“Pantami used to call the PDP all kinds of names, including ‘Al-Kafira’ (the Infidel party), yet he has now joined the same party and contested under its platform,” he said.

PREMIUM TIMES had earlier reported that Mr Pantami’s political transition and his emergence as a PDP governorship candidate generated debate, particularly over his past criticism of the party.

Rarara’s song sparks controversy

The latest controversy began after Rarara released a song widely interpreted as a political attack on Mr Pantami.

The song attracted criticism from Nigerians, with some questioning the use of music to attack political opponents, while others argued that political figures who enter partisan politics should expect criticism.

The controversy also drew reactions from Islamic scholars and other public commentators, who criticised what they considered the use of abusive or derogatory language against a prominent religious figure.

However, Mr Pantami previously acknowledged that criticism is part of politics. In May, while suspending a social media aide who described his political opponents as “hypocrites”, he said criticism was an important part of political discourse and that, as a politician seeking to lead a diverse society, he understood its value.

Against this backdrop, Mr Kwankwaso’s comments have added to the debate over whether religious leaders who enter partisan politics should continue to be treated primarily as clerics or be subjected to scrutiny and criticism as other politicians.

World.title: Amnesty International seeks adequate security during Osun election
World.content:
Amnesty International on Tuesday called on security agencies and the Nigerian government at all levels to be neutral and protect the rights of the Osun State people to vote freely in Saturday’s governorship election, amid escalating violence in the lead-up to the poll.

In a statement it shared on its official X page, the group said it made the call “amidst disturbing signs of violence, intimidation and allegations of interference.”

It said it had seen signals of looming danger, calling on the relevant authorities to ensure accountability and investigate the recorded incidents, including deaths, and bring the perpetrators to book.

“The authorities at all levels and security agencies must stand neutral and not engage in any act that may or can be perceived to favour any political party or candidate. The right of the people of Osun State to vote freely and fairly in an atmosphere of respect for human rights must be upheld.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The group, a global movement campaigning against human rights abuses, said “Nigerian authorities must fulfil their obligation to promote, protect, respect, and fulfil human rights…ahead of the Osun State gubernatorial election slated for 15 August 2026.”

A report by Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI), a pro-democracy and electoral reforms advocacy organisation, said on Monday that no fewer than 73 election-related violent incidents resulting in 29 deaths have been recorded in the build-up to the 15 August governorship election in the state.

The report identified 12 high-risk local government areas and called for targeted security operations and political interventions to prevent violence.

It also said the violent incidents appeared to be strategically instigated in politically significant locations to suppress voter turnout.

Amnesty International said in Tuesday’s statement that an investigation by its team “on the ground shows escalating violence and build-up for more clashes in Osogbo, Ede, Ife, Oriade, Ijebu-Ijesha, Ilobu, and Ikire. Fueling the instability and impunity in the state are reports of supporters of some politicians violently targeting political opponents, real or perceived.”

It also urged all political parties to desist from violence and commit to a free and fair election.

Amnesty International also noted that it had received reports of violence, arrests of Osun government officials and alleged plans to “influence the elections.”

For months, Governor Ademola Adeleke, who is seeking a second term in office, and his party, the Accord Party, have questioned the neutrality of federal institutions, particularly the police command in the state, ahead of Saturday’s election.

Among Mr Adeleke’s arch rivals is Bola Oyebamiji, the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), the party in control of the federal government.

Concerns about the neutrality of the police and key federal agencies have intesified in the past weeks following the controversial arrest of the Secretary to the Government of Osun State, Teslim Igbalaye, over unsubstantiated vote buying allegation.

Barely a week after Mr Igbalaye’s arrest, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) froze three bank accounts of the Osun State Government in what it said was necessary to stop a fraudulent diversion of the funds belonging to the state.

President Bola Tinubu, who also belongs to the APC which is fielding a frontline candidate in the forthcoming Osun election, said he was embarrassed by the timing of the steps taken by EFCC and directed the commission to immediately take steps to lift the freeze order on the state’s bank accounts.

World.title: Eno declines disclosing Lagos building project cost despite its N41.05bn budget
World.content:
Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has declined to disclose the contract sum of the 18-storey Ibom Tower building being constructed in Lagos State, despite the project having attracted at least N41.05 billion in budgetary provisions since 2024.

In a series of videos reviewed by PREMIUM TIMES, Mr Eno refused to give the figure when a journalist asked him about the cost of the project during an inspection visit at the weekend.

Rather than disclose the contract sum, the governor said the cost was still being worked out because of changes and additional input from the project consultant.

“A lot of things have happened here that we didn’t envisage. The consultant has made a lot of input. I think we are still working back end,” Mr Eno said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“If you say a figure today, people hold you to it. So, I rather get the work done rightly than to begin to look at the price.

“All these are to help us increase the State IGR.”

Governor Eno’s response has raised questions about the transparency of a project for which the state government has made successive multibillion-naira budgetary provisions since its commencement.

A review of Akwa Ibom State’s budget documents by PREMIUM TIMES shows that N16 billion was provided for the construction of the Lagos building in the 2024 revised budget.

The provision was reduced to N10 billion in the revised 2025 budget, while another N15.05 billion was budgeted for the construction of the 18-storey Ibom Tower in the 2026 approved budget.

The cumulative budgetary provisions amount to N41.05 billion.

It remains unclear how much of the approved funds have actually been released and spent on the project.

The uncertainty is partly due to the failure of the state government to publish detailed budget performance reports since the first quarter of 2025 and capital expenditure in its audited financial statements.

Procurement secrecy

The absence of publicly available information on the project’s contract sum is also notable because Akwa Ibom’s public procurement framework provides for access to procurement information.

The state’s public procurement law requires the Bureau of Public Procurement and procuring entities to publish procurement information through the state’s electronic procurement portal.

PREMIUM TIMES found no procurement records relating to the Ibom Tower project when our reporter searched the portal on Tuesday, 11 August.

The newspaper found that the Eno administration rarely publishes comprehensive details of major public contracts, including contract sums, implementation schedules and procurement documents. This is a violation of Section 21(15) of the state’s 2026 Public Procurement Law which guarantees public access to procurement records.

The provision requires procurement records to contain information including the identity of contractors, contract values, dates of award, procurement proceedings, technical specifications and other information necessary to promote public accountability.

Such information would ordinarily enable residents to determine the actual financial commitment of the government to a major infrastructure project and track its implementation.

The lack of this information has made it difficult to independently establish the actual value of the building project in Lagos, how much has been paid to the contractor and whether subsequent budgetary provisions represent additional commitments, variations or outstanding obligations under the original contract.

Contractor incorporated 15 months before project flag-off

Findings by PREMIUM TIMES show that Messrs WL Construction Limited was selected as the main contractor for the project.

Other consultants associated with the project include D.O Design Build, the architect; Pois Consult Limited; and Alliance Engineering Consult, identified as structural engineers.

WL Construction Limited, according to checks at the Corporate Affairs Commission, was incorporated to carry on business in Nigeria on 11 July 2023, about two months after Mr Eno’s administration commenced.

The company was, therefore, registered 15 months before the state government officially flagged off the Ibom Tower project in November 2024.

The acronym “WL” stands for Western Legacy.

The circumstances surrounding the selection of the contractor and the procurement process leading to the award could not be independently established from publicly available procurement records.

The state government has also not publicly disclosed the bidding documents, number of companies that participated in the procurement process, evaluation reports, award documents or the contract sum.

PREMIUM TIMES previously reported how Mr Eno publicly disclosed that a contractor was awarded a job without bidding.

The newspaper also reported that the governor sought powers in the state’s new procurement law to bypass bidding for multi-billion naira contracts.

N2.934 trillion revenue

The opacity surrounding the Lagos project comes against the backdrop of substantial revenue accruing to the state under Mr Eno.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that Akwa Ibom received more than N2.934 trillion in revenue in the first 38 months of the governor’s administration.

The state’s increased financial resources have enabled the government to embark on multibillion-naira projects across sectors.

PREMIUM TIMES reported how the state budgeted N26.91 billion for the renovation of a hotel in Uyo.

But the availability of funds has also heightened calls for greater transparency over how the money is being spent.

The government has repeatedly presented infrastructure development and investment as central to its economic strategy, including the construction of the Lagos tower, which it says is intended to generate income for the state.

Mr Eno, while responding to the question on the cost of the project, specifically said the investment would boost the state’s internally generated revenue.

“All these are to help us increase the State IGR,” he said.

However, without disclosure of the contract value, expenditure to date, funding structure and projected returns, it is difficult for the public to independently assess the financial implications or the economic viability of the investment.

Why Lagos?

The decision to commit billions of naira to an 18-storey commercial development in Lagos has also generated questions among residents of Akwa Ibom.

Critics have questioned why a government whose state has significant infrastructure and development needs would prioritise a major property investment outside the state.

Akwa Ibom remains one of Nigeria’s states with significant levels of multidimensional poverty, raising questions about the balance between investments designed to generate future revenue and immediate spending on social and economic needs within the state.

The government has argued that the Lagos project is an investment intended to generate income for Akwa Ibom rather than simply a construction project.

But the absence of publicly available procurement and expenditure information has made it difficult to independently scrutinise that justification.

For now, the exact contract value of the Ibom Tower remains undisclosed by the state government, even though budgetary provisions for the project have reached N41.05 billion.

And while the governor says he would rather “get the work done rightly” than disclose a figure that could later change, the procurement law places the responsibility for documenting and making public the financial details of government contracts on the state not on future estimates of what the project may eventually cost.

World.title: NANS urges Senate to extend NELFUND to Nigerian students abroad
World.content:
Senate

By Matthew Johnson

ABUJA — The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS), Turkish Zone, has urged the Senate to expand the Nigeria Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) to cover eligible Nigerian students studying in accredited institutions outside the country.

NANS made the call during an engagement with the Vice Chairman of the Senate Committee on Diaspora and Non-Governmental Organisations, Senator Anthony Siyako Yaro.

The delegation, led by the President of NANS Turkish Zone, Daniel Okpala, discussed the welfare, educational financing and representation of Nigerian students in the diaspora, particularly those studying in Turkey and Northern Cyprus.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Okpala said the increasing number of Nigerians pursuing higher education abroad required corresponding attention from the government in its education financing policies.

He said Nigerian students studying abroad faced financial pressures arising from tuition fees, accommodation, exchange-rate fluctuations and other educational expenses.

According to him, students should not be excluded from government-backed educational support solely because they are studying outside Nigeria.

NANS called for a review of the existing NELFUND framework to accommodate qualified Nigerians enrolled in accredited foreign institutions.

The association also appealed for stronger diplomatic support to address welfare, administrative and other challenges confronting Nigerian students in the Turkish Zone and the wider diaspora.

The students highlighted the impact of the depreciation of the naira on families financing education abroad, saying exchange-rate pressures had significantly increased the cost of tuition, accommodation and other necessities.

NANS said extending the scheme to eligible students abroad would widen access to education and reduce the financial burden on students and their families.

The association also raised concerns about the level of engagement between Nigerian diplomatic missions and student communities in countries with large Nigerian populations.

It argued that Nigerian students abroad remained an important component of the country’s human-capital development and should be considered in policies aimed at expanding access to education.

The association said the realities facing students overseas should be reflected in national education policies, particularly as more Nigerians seek higher education opportunities in foreign universities.

It urged the Senate to consider an appropriate legislative framework that would enable eligible Nigerian students studying in accredited institutions abroad to benefit from NELFUND.

NELFUND was established under the Student Loans (Access to Higher Education) Act, 2024, to provide loans to eligible Nigerians for higher education, vocational training and skills acquisition.

NANS pledged to continue engaging lawmakers and relevant government institutions on policies affecting the education, welfare and representation of Nigerian students abroad.

Yaro, according to the statement, expressed willingness to examine the proposal and explore the appropriate legislative process for broadening the reach of NELFUND.

He also acknowledged the need to ensure adequate representation of Nigerians in the diaspora in national policy and legislative discussions.

World.title: S-West group urges Tinubu to expedite state police bill
World.content:
By Dapo Akinrefon

LAGOS — The Southwest Security Stakeholders Group, SSSG, has urged President Bola Tinubu to expedite action on the establishment of state police following the passage of the proposed constitutional amendment by the National Assembly.

The group made the call on Tuesday after an extraordinary meeting held at Oodua House, Ikeja, Lagos.

The SSSG said the draft executive bill and implementation framework were scheduled for presentation to the President on September 3, 2026, while the constitutional amendment would still require approval by at least 24 of Nigeria’s 36 State Houses of Assembly.

The group, led by the Aare Ona Kakanfo of Yorubaland, Iba Gani Adams, comprises the Oodua People’s Congress, OPC; Agbekoya Society; Vigilante Group of Nigeria, VGN; Professional Hunters Association; Odua Warriors; Vigilante Jahun; Agbekoya Peace Movement; Agbekoya Solidarity Movement; COMSAIC; Isokan Ile Oodua; Egbe Obinrin Oodua Agbaye; Omo Oduduwa United; Yoruba People’s Congress and Yoruba Self-Defence Group.

The stakeholders also urged governors in the South-West and members of the various State Houses of Assembly to prioritise the passage of enabling laws, budgetary provisions and institutional arrangements required for the smooth take-off of state policing.

In a statement by its Publicity Secretary, Ireti Adewole, the group acknowledged that incidents of insecurity had not been alarming in the South-West in recent months but stressed the need for the region to remain prepared by establishing state police structures.

It noted that residents in several states in the North and Middle Belt were still facing insecurity, stressing the need for proactive measures to prevent the spread of criminal activities.

The statement said: “The Southwest, parts of the South-South and South-East, the North and even the Middle Belt, are not yet free from disturbing criminal activities, including armed robbery, kidnapping, cultism and other forms of violence that threaten the peace and development of our communities.

“This situation calls for a united front and proactive measures from all stakeholders — government at all levels, security agencies, traditional institutions and civil society groups.”

The SSSG called on all stakeholders involved in the implementation of the proposed state police framework to expedite action, arguing that delays could undermine efforts to address insecurity at the community level.

It described the proposed state police system as a potentially significant reform of Nigeria’s security architecture, saying decentralisation could enable states to respond more effectively to local security challenges.

The group, however, expressed concern over what it described as the slow pace of implementation despite the passage of the proposal by the National Assembly.

It asked the Federal Government, state governments and State Houses of Assembly to provide clarity on the status of the reform and the steps being taken to actualise it.

“The people of the Southwest deserve clear answers and tangible actions,” it said.

The group also called for greater collaboration among governments, security agencies, traditional institutions and community organisations in developing technology-driven and community-based approaches to tackling insecurity.

According to the SSSG, such collaboration would strengthen intelligence gathering, improve rapid response and enhance community policing tailored to local security challenges.

“The time for rhetoric has passed. The people of the Southwest demand and deserve peace, security and development.

“The SSSG stands ready to collaborate with all stakeholders to achieve these goals. However, this requires commitment, transparency and urgency from our leaders and institutions,” the group said.

World.title: TUC urges urgent action on food imports, demands N1,000 to dollar exchange rate
World.content:
—Says stronger Naira will cut food prices

—-Calls for fast tracking of state police

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — THE Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) on Tuesday, pressed the federal government yto sustain food import policies, fast-track state police, and accelerate a commercial restructuring of refineries, while pledging full support for striking aviation and hotel workers.

TUC also urged the Federal Government and the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to take decisive measures to strengthen the naira for the exchange rate to be between ₦900 and ₦1,000 to the United States dollar.

It argued that a stronger currency would translate into lower food and commodity prices and provide relief to Nigerian workers.

Briefing journalists on the state of the Nigerian economy, insecurity, food prices and other issues affecting workers and the wider population, the TUC President, Comrade Festus Osifo, called on government to sustain this policy and solve the state of insecurity so that farmers could go back to farms.

“We are calling on government to sustain this policy and solve the state of insecurity so that our farmers could go back to farms.”

Osifo reiterated that emergency food importation remains necessary until domestic security allows farmers to return to the fields and restore supply.

“Only when the supply end has been solved can we stop food importation,” he said, warning against a return to the extreme price spikes of past years: “We don’t want a bag of rice to go back again to 100,000 or 120,000 naira.”

On macroeconomic policy, Osifo said national indicators have stabilised but warned that gains have not reached workers.

He pressed the government and the Central Bank to bring the naira closer to its purchasing-power value, arguing the currency remains undervalued and that a fair exchange rate would be in the region of 900–1,000 naira to the dollar.

Osifo noted that said the naira had appreciated from about ₦1,700–₦1,800 to the dollar in early 2024 to around ₦1,380 currently.

“We still believe that our naira is still undervalued,” he said. “CBN has what it takes to manage the exchange rate to about 1,000 naira to a dollar.” He criticised weak consequential salary adjustments after devaluation, noting that workers’ pay has not kept pace with the higher cost of imported inputs and goods.

On security and state police, Osifo urged the administration and National Assembly to fast-track a state police bill despite electoral-year objections.

“How can we, because of less than 0.1% of Nigerian population, allow 99.99% to suffer?” he asked. “The time to implement state police is now.”

Osifo also called on government to invest in technology and equipment to tackle insecurity, insisting security must be treated with the urgency of a nation at war.

On labour disputes, the TUC threw its weight behind aviation workers, including ATSAN members, who are striking over alleged employer resistance to unionisation and non-remittance of a 5% ticket charge reportedly worth about 25 billion naira.

“From the ILO Convention to the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, it is our indelible right to unionise,” Osifo said. “We have endorsed what they are doing 100% and we are giving them total support.”

He warned hotel owners who block union organising — singling out Abuja Continental Hotel — that “the time of talk, talk, talk is almost over” and promised the union would escalate action if employers remained obstinate.

On the energy sector, Osifo backed plans to reduce government equity in refineries without selling them outright, urging a model similar to NLNG’s 49% government, 51% private structure. “Selling it outrightly will not solve energy security,” he said, and urged that private investors with petrochemical experience be allowed to take majority positions to drive commercial efficiency.

The TUC commended the DSS for recent arrests of suspected bandits and terrorists and urged vigorous prosecution. “You send signal to the bad guys when you get some of them arrested, you persecute them and you commit them to either life in prison or, depending on the offence, death sentence,”

Osifo said.

He also welcomed recent military pay rises and called for comparable increases for all workers. “The best way of fighting the war is not just going alone. It’s also taking care of some of the economic needs,” he added.

TUC President commended Health Minister Professor Ali Pate for intervening to reopen factories and secure the release of detained workers in a dispute affecting its affiliate FOBTOB. “We commend him for acting swiftly,” Osifo said.

World.title: Adeleke to IGP: Arrest, prosecute Osun senator over alleged killing threat
World.content:
Gov. Adeleke

By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo

OSOGBO — Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has called on the Inspector-General of Police, Tunji Disu, to order the arrest and prosecution of Senator Francis Fadahunsi, representing Osun East Senatorial District, over an alleged threat to kill members of the Accord Party.

A video circulating on social media purportedly showed Fadahunsi addressing members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) protesting alleged killings of party members in Ilesa.

In the video, the senator was allegedly heard urging APC supporters to attack members of the Accord Party wherever they were found.

However, while addressing journalists at the Government House Banquet Hall in Osogbo on Tuesday, Adeleke raised concerns over what he described as security operations targeting Accord Party leaders and supporters ahead of the August 15 governorship election.

The governor alleged that the viral video showed Fadahunsi calling for the killing of Accord Party leaders, supporters and their family members.

According to Adeleke, the senator allegedly said that where Accord Party leaders could not be found, their wives and children should be targeted.

Adeleke said he had brought the matter to the attention of the Inspector-General of Police and demanded an immediate investigation and arrest of the senator.

He added that Disu had confirmed the existence of the video and assured him that action would be taken.

“This is now beyond politics. This is now a national security threat that requires the attention of Mr President through the Office of the National Security Adviser,” Adeleke said.

The governor also called on the police and the Department of State Services (DSS) to investigate Fadahunsi over what he described as alleged incitement to violence against the people of Ijesaland and Osun State.

Adeleke further demanded an end to what he described as “illegal operations” by the Intelligence Response Team, alleging that its operatives had been arresting Accord Party leaders across local government areas without justification.

He urged the Inspector-General of Police and other security agencies to uphold due process and ensure fair policing before, during and after Saturday’s governorship election.

“We demand that the IGP enforce due process and fair policing by aborting all anti-people plots against democracy in Osun State.

“We finally request that the police and other security agencies should act in line with the rule of law and their oath of office before, during and after these coming elections,” he said.

World.title: Osun Election: Akinfosile urges Tinubu to ensure credible election
World.content:
— Warns against repeat of political violence in old Western Region

By Steve Oko

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has been urged to ensure a level playing field in the August 15 Osun State governorship election, with political analyst, Dr Chris Akinfosile (FNISM), warning that any attempt to manipulate the poll could damage Nigeria’s democratic credibility.

Akinfosile also invoked the history of political violence in the old Western Region, cautioning that electoral manipulation and political impunity could create grievances capable of escalating beyond the immediate contest.

In a commentary titled, “The Osun Tinderbox: As Davido Threatens Trump’s Intervention, President Tinubu Must Shun Election Rigging and Save Nigeria’s Fragile Democracy,” Akinfosile said the President should regard the election as an opportunity to demonstrate that his administration placed national stability above partisan interests.

His comments followed a declaration by music star David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, that he would seek the intervention of United States President Donald Trump if he believed the Osun election was rigged.

Akinfosile said Davido’s position had added an international dimension to an election already generating political tension.

He, however, said the more important issue was whether Nigeria’s electoral institutions would be allowed to conduct a credible election without political interference.

According to him, “there is no patriotic argument for rigging an election in a democracy already precariously balanced on a knife edge.”

He urged Tinubu to direct security agencies to maintain neutrality, protect voters and electoral materials, and ensure that anyone found attempting to use state power or political thugs to influence the outcome was prosecuted.

Akinfosile also challenged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to demonstrate institutional independence and ensure that every legitimate vote counted.

He said the President had shown, through his recent intervention in the controversy surrounding the freezing of the Osun State Government’s account, that he could rise above partisan considerations when national interest demanded it.

Tinubu had directed the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, to take steps to vacate the court order freezing the state government’s account and subsequently spoke with Governor Ademola Adeleke on the matter.

Akinfosile said the gesture should be followed by an equally clear commitment to electoral neutrality.

He warned that a disputed election in Osun could have consequences beyond the state, particularly amid the country’s existing security, economic and political challenges.

“Let the people choose. Let their will stand,” he said, stressing that no political victory was worth the instability that could follow a disputed mandate.

Akinfosile urged Tinubu to publicly assure all contestants that the Federal Government would neither manipulate the election nor tolerate the use of security agencies to intimidate voters.

He also called for effective monitoring of the election by domestic and international observers and urged political parties to commit themselves to peaceful conduct before, during and after the poll.

According to him, a free and credible election in Osun would provide the Tinubu administration with an opportunity to strengthen public confidence in Nigeria’s democratic institutions and send a positive signal to investors and the international community.

He said the President’s handling of the election could ultimately become an important part of his political legacy.

“Tinubu can choose to be remembered as the President who placed nation over party, stability over power and posterity over expediency,” Akinfosile said.

World.title: Oyetola left N15bn for Osun, Adeleke’s empty-treasury claims false – Oyebamiji
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: Governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress APC in Osun State, Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji, has insisted that the administration of Governor Gboyega Oyetola left about N15 billion for his successor, dismissing as misleading the narrative promoted by the Governor Ademola Adeleke administration regarding the finances it inherited.

Oyebamiji made the assertion while fielding questions from journalists at the Arise TV Town Hall Meeting held in Osun State, where he addressed several issues that have dominated the campaign, particularly claims by the incumbent administration about inherited liabilities and the state’s financial position.

He urged Osun residents to resist what he called political narratives designed to create the false impression that the current government inherited an empty treasury, arguing instead that the resources available to the Adeleke administration far exceed what any previous government in the state has had access to.

“As at today in Osun, 97 per cent of resources go to just two local governments. That is an aberration; actually, it is criminal. In 12 years of APC, Aregbesola and Oyetola, Osun got only N450 billion. In three and a half years of Adeleke, they have collected N650 billion. How does N650 billion match what we see in Osun today?” he said.

According to him, the surge in federal allocations to Osun followed major economic reforms introduced by the administration of President Bola Tinubu, yet little on the ground justifies the scale of funding that has accrued to the state government under Adeleke.

The APC candidate commended Tinubu for what he described as bold and courageous decisions to remove the fuel subsidy and reform the nation’s economy, noting that despite the initial hardship the reforms caused, they have substantially boosted resources available to all three tiers of government, Osun inclusive.

He argued that this increase in resources ought to translate into meaningful development, improved infrastructure, better social services and expanded economic opportunities for residents, rather than the disparities he alleged currently exist in how funds are distributed across the state’s local governments.

Oyebamiji pledged that, if elected governor, his administration would deploy Osun’s resources transparently, responsibly and equitably for the benefit of all citizens, with accountability, prudent financial management, economic expansion and inclusive development as guiding priorities.

He said the people of Osun deserved a government that converts public resources into tangible improvements in their daily lives, adding that his administration would work to build an economy where young people have opportunities, businesses can thrive, workers are properly supported, and communities across the state receive equitable attention.

World.title: Jingir’s remarks vindicate Kanu’s warnings, IPOB claims
World.content:
By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — The Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has claimed that recent remarks attributed to Sheikh Sani Yahaya Jingir on Nigeria’s religious identity have vindicated concerns previously raised by its detained leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, over religious freedom and equality in the country.

In a statement issued on Tuesday by its spokesman, Emma Powerful, the group said the reported declaration that Nigeria is a Muslim country and that Christians are “infidels” raised concerns about the country’s constitutional commitment to religious equality.

IPOB argued that such comments should not be dismissed as mere rhetoric, stressing that Nigeria operates a constitutional system in which citizens are entitled to equal rights regardless of religious affiliation.

The group said the remarks had given fresh relevance to what it described as Kanu’s longstanding warnings about alleged attempts to alter Nigeria’s religious and political character.

According to IPOB, “the time for denial is over,” urging the Federal Government to clarify its position on religious equality and the constitutional status of Nigeria.

The organisation also renewed its criticism of the prosecution and continued detention of Kanu, arguing that his case raised questions about due process and the rule of law.

IPOB referred to the October 13, 2022 judgment of the Court of Appeal, which it said discharged Kanu, and questioned subsequent legal developments that led to his continued detention and eventual conviction.

The group further raised questions about the application of criminal laws, fair hearing and the legal provisions under which Kanu was prosecuted.

However, the claims remain IPOB’s position and have been contested in Nigeria’s legal and judicial processes.

IPOB also claimed that lawmakers in the United States and Israel had been briefed on Kanu’s case and what it described as concerns over religious persecution and the treatment of non-Muslim populations in Nigeria.

The group urged the Federal Government to address concerns over religious intolerance and insecurity, rather than allowing them to deepen existing divisions.

It called on the government to clarify whether Nigeria would continue to operate as a secular constitutional state in which Christians, Muslims, adherents of traditional religions and people of other or no faith enjoy equal rights.

IPOB linked its concerns to the broader security challenges facing the country, including attacks attributed to jihadist groups and criminal elements, and warned against the spread of violence and religious intolerance to southern Nigeria.

The group maintained that Kanu’s warnings deserved greater public scrutiny following the remarks attributed to Jingir.

It said its concerns went beyond Kanu’s personal circumstances to issues of constitutionalism, religious freedom, judicial independence, state accountability and the protection of citizens’ rights.

“Imprisoning the man does not erase his words,” IPOB said, insisting that the issues raised by Kanu should be addressed through constitutional and democratic means.

The organisation called on Nigerians and the international community to pay closer attention to developments concerning religious tolerance, security and the rule of law in Nigeria.

It said the controversy surrounding the remarks attributed to Jingir should provide an opportunity for the country to reaffirm its commitment to religious equality and constitutional governance.

World.title: Tinubu tasks Nigerians on unity, peaceful coexistence
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has called for greater unity and community collaboration among Nigerians to address security challenges and promote lasting peace and development.

Tinubu, represented by the Deputy Senate President, Sen. Barau Jibrin, made the call on Tuesday at the International Conference on “Diversity and Social Peace: A Partnership for a Promising Future” in Abuja.

The conference was organised by the Muslim World League (MWL) in collaboration with Jama’atu Izalatil Bid’ah Wa Iqamatus Sunnah (JIBWIS) Nigeria.

Tinubu said the conference came at a critical time when the world is facing multifaceted security challenges.

He called on participants to use the conference to examine emerging security threats and share practical ideas for promoting lasting peace in Nigeria, Africa and the wider world.

“The government is determined to make sure that we remain united in our country; despite our little differences, we should work and remain in this country and allow Nigeria to remain as a united nation.

“The participants in this conference are also expected to take advantage of the internationality of this event to share diverse experiences that will further contribute to the ongoing debate on searching for viable options for restoring sustainable regional, continental and global peace.”

He commended the Muslim World League and JIBWIS Nigeria for choosing Nigeria to host the conference, expressing confidence that its outcomes would contribute to strengthening peace and security.

Also speaking, the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammadu Sa’ad Abubakar III, said Nigeria does not lack solutions to its challenges but needed greater commitment to implement agreed decisions.

“We don’t lack the number of solutions to our problems; what we lack is implementation.

“The more we come together and discuss our issues, our problems, our solutions, the more united we become,” he said.

He urged religious leaders and stakeholders to deepen dialogue, strengthen mutual trust and identify common ground in addressing the country’s challenges.

The Sultan also called for stronger Christian-Muslim relations through the Nigeria Inter-Religious Council (NIREC), stressing that religious differences should not undermine national unity.

Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), said Nigeria’s diversity should be regarded as a strength rather than a source of division.

Yilwatda, who spoke from personal experience of communal conflict and displacement, said religious differences should not undermine Nigerians’ shared humanity.

“Religious differences do not have to produce human distances and separation because of our beliefs; we may worship differently, but we suffer together, we dream together.

“We can build together, and ultimately, we can rise and fall together,” he said.

Yilwatda urged religious leaders to preach without hatred and truth without incitement, while calling on political leaders to resist exploiting religion and ethnicity for temporary political advantage.

“Let us preach faith without hatred, conviction without contempt and truth without incitement.

“To our political leaders, let us resist the temptation to exploit religion for ethnicity, for sentiments and for temporary political advantage.

“No political victory is worth the permanent damage inflicted on a nation,” he said.

He called on Nigerians to reject hate speech and protect vulnerable communities and places of worship regardless of religious or ethnic differences.

Rev. Fr. Cornelius Omonokhua, Executive Secretary of the Nigeria Inter-Religious Council (NIREC), said humanity remained the strongest bond among Nigerians in spite of religious differences.

He said religion should promote mercy, compassion and love rather than division.

“The essence of religion is mercy and compassion and this should be called love, not tolerance, because human life is sacred.

“We should never allow anybody to weaponize religion, ethnicity or poverty to turn us against each other,” Omonokhua said.

He said NIREC would continue to promote human dignity, common good and peaceful coexistence through collaboration between Christian and Muslim leaders.

Earlier, Sheikh Abdullahi Lau, National Chairman of JIBWIS, said government must sustain efforts to address insecurity while investing in education and economic empowerment for young people.

Lau said quality education and economic opportunities would reduce youths’ vulnerability to radicalisation and recruitment by criminal groups.

“Qualitative education for our youths, with emphasis on economic empowerment, will constitute one of the means of engaging our youths, which will remove them from vulnerability to radicalisation and recruitment into criminal groups.

“JIBWIS Nigeria and the World Muslim League will also provide a forum for regular dialogue between adherents of the two major religions in Nigeria to foster peaceful coexistence,” he said.

He also called on Nigerians to pray for peace and for the country’s leaders to be guided toward decisions that would promote development and stability.

The two-day conference, holding from Tuesday to Wednesday, is aimed at promoting tolerance, acceptance of diversity, interfaith dialogue and cooperation among religious, ethnic and civil society groups toward building social peace.

World.title: Tinubu Okays Landmark Deep Offshore Investment Framework To Unlock $50bn In New Investment
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has approved a landmark reform that replaces project-by-project negotiations with a transparent investment framework designed to unlock up to US$50 billion in deep offshore investment and restart Nigeria’s large, capital-intensive offshore developments that have remained stalled for decades.

According to a statement on Tuesday by presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, the reform establishes a transparent, rules-based investment framework capable of supporting the next generation of deep offshore developments, beginning with the approximately US$10 billion Bonga South West project, while strengthening Nigeria’s competitiveness for globally mobile investment capital.

The decision builds on President Tinubu’s engagement with the Chief Executive Officer of Shell Plc, Mr Wael Sawan, during which the president directed the development of the next wave of measures required to unlock Nigeria’s deep offshore investment pipeline.

Rather than pursuing project-specific solutions, the Federal Government transformed that directive into a comprehensive investment framework applicable across multiple categories of qualifying developments.

Given effect through the Deep Offshore Oil and Gas Projects Incentives (Tax Remission) Order, 2026, the framework replaces project-by-project negotiations with transparent eligibility criteria, clear implementation processes and a durable investment architecture that provides greater certainty for investors while safeguarding long-term national value.

The approval also enables NNPC Limited, as the government’s nominated counterparty under the Production Sharing Contracts, to proceed with the necessary amendments to eligible Production Sharing Contracts required to implement the framework.

Tinubu commended the Federal Ministry of Justice, the Federal Ministry of Finance, the Federal Ministry of Petroleum Resources, the Nigeria Revenue Service, NNPC Limited, the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board, investing partners and other industry stakeholders whose collaboration, technical expertise and commitment helped shape the framework.

The president further said: “The countries that attract long-term investment are not necessarily those with the greatest natural resources. They are the ones that provide the greatest certainty. This reform reflects our determination to build an investment environment defined by clear rules, strong institutions and enduring partnerships. We are creating the conditions for capital to flow, for Nigerian businesses to grow, for our people to prosper and for our natural resources to deliver lasting national value.”

On her part, the Special Adviser to the President on Oil and Gas, Olu Arowolo-Verheijen, said a defining feature of the reform is its emphasis on Nigerian industrial capability.

According to her, “Projects qualifying under the framework will maximise execution within Nigeria wherever commercially and technically feasible, strengthening domestic engineering, fabrication, marine logistics, technical services and project management.

“The objective is not only to increase investment and production, but also to create skilled jobs, deepen local supply chains and position Nigeria as Africa’s regional hub for deep offshore project execution.”

World.title: 25 Benin Groups Endorse Paddy Iyamu, Say Misconceptions Over Origin Settled
World.content:
A coalition of 25 prominent Benin socio-cultural and youth groups, on Tuesday endorsed the candidacy of the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Oredo Federal Constituency in the 2027 House of Representatives election, Dr. Paddy Iyamu, declaring that earlier reservations about his origin had been resolved.

The groups, numbering about 25 and comprising Otedo Youth Movement Worldwide, Aiguobasinmwin Movement Worldwide, Eliz United Forum, Girl Child for Social Change and others, threw their weight behind Iyamu at an endorsement ceremony held at Imaguero College, Benin City.

Some of the groups had previously expressed concerns over the politician’s background and origin.

However, they said they had now been adequately clarified and were satisfied that the issues were based on misconceptions, which they declared had been put to rest.

Speaking at the event, Chairman of Aiguobasinmwin Movement Worldwide, Mr. Osaro Culture Iyamu, said the group had listened to explanations surrounding the controversy and was convinced that Paddy Iyamu remained a Benin man deserving of their support.

He said: “We have heard a lot of misconceptions about Hon. Paddy Iyamu, and these misconceptions have been corrected and that is why we are supporting him. We have to support our own.”

Also speaking, Chairman of Otedo Youth Movement Worldwide, Comrade Kari Edosa, said the group had discovered that the issues surrounding Iyamu’s origin were unfounded.

According to him, “We have found out that Hon. Paddy Iyamu is a man of pedigree. We have found out that he is not an Ijaw man. His father’s house is at Sakponba Road. We have been clarified and we are supporting him.”

Edosa added that Iyamu’s record as Commissioner for Education demonstrated his commitment to the people.

Responding, Iyamu said his aspiration to represent Oredo Federal Constituency was driven by a genuine desire to serve the people and build on the interventions he had undertaken before and during his political career.

He recalled that he established the Dr. Paddy Iyamu Foundation in 2014, through which he had provided free medical surgeries, youth empowerment programmes and other interventions across Edo State.

Iyamu said his foundation had annually provided free surgeries for residents suffering from conditions including fibroids, glaucoma and breast lumps, while also empowering hundreds of youths.

He added that the foundation’s free surgery programme would resume in November, while its annual food bank for the elderly would also continue. “Whether I am campaigning or not, it is a covenant with God,” he said.

The former commissioner also cited some of the interventions recorded during his tenure, including the rehabilitation of the six-kilometre road at Edo State Polytechnic, Usen.

He said the project was facilitated after he raised the plight of students and residents with Governor Monday Okpebholo, leading to collaboration with the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC).

World.title: Health Workers Issue Katsina 21-day Ultimatum to Meet Demands
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

The Assembly of Health Care Professionals in Katsina State has threatened to embark on industrial action if the state government fails to address its welfare and professional demands within 21 days.

Addressing journalists in Katsina Tuesday on behalf of the Assembly, the state Chairman of the Association of Hospital and Administrative Pharmacists of Nigeria, Comrade Ibrahim Balange, said the members of the union would embark on strike after the expiration of the ultimatum.

He explained that the ultimatum, which took effect on August 11, 2026, was issued after several engagements, meetings and representations to the state government failed to produce significant progress on the workers’ demands.

He said the health professionals were demanding the immediate implementation of 100 per cent Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS) as applicable in Federal Government-owned health institutions.

He noted that the health workers are also demanding the skipping of CONHESS 10, as contained in previous government circulars and correspondence submitted to relevant committees in the state.

Balange said the assembly was further demanding an upward review of the hazard allowance to 100 per cent, in line with what is obtainable in federal health institutions.

Other demands, he said, included upward review of call duty, shift, clinical and non-clinical, rural and specialist allowances, as well as an increase in nurses’ uniform allowance to N80,000, as applicable in federal health institutions.

He said the demands were not aimed at undermining the government but were necessary to improve the welfare and motivation of health workers and ultimately strengthen healthcare delivery in Katsina State.

Balange expressed concern that the prolonged delay in resolving the issues was affecting the morale and productivity of healthcare professionals whom he said, despite the challenges, remained committed to serving residents of the state.

He warned that failure by the government to meet the demands within the 21-day ultimatum would leave the health professionals with no option but to down tools.

He, however, appealed to the state government to use the period of the ultimatum to resolve the issues and avert a disruption of healthcare services across the state.

He said the Assembly remained hopeful that Governor Dikko Umaru Radda’s administration would respond positively to the demands in the interest of healthcare workers and the people of the state.

Balange revealed that the Assembly, comprising the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria, National Association of Nigeria Nurses and Midwives, Association of Hospital and Administrative Pharmacists of Nigeria and Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists of Nigeria, had been patient with the government over the issues.

World.title: The Man Between Market and the State
World.content:
Kehinde Sowole writes on how Temi Popoola and NGX Group are turning economic reform into capital formation

Every era of economic reform produces two kinds of figures. There are the reformers themselves, the presidents, ministers and governors who take the political risk of change. And there are the interlocutors: the institutional leaders who translate reform into confidence, policy into capital, and government ambition into market reality. Nigeria’s current reform era has no shortage of the first kind. What has become increasingly evident is the emergence of the second, and few embody that role more convincingly today like Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Nigerian Exchange Group.

Last week’s engagement between the NGX Group Board and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at the State House was, on its surface, a courtesy visit. Read properly, it was something rarer: a working session between a government pursuing economic transformation and a capital market leadership that has positioned the market as an increasingly indispensable instrument for delivering that transformation. The numbers presented to the president told one story; market capitalisation rising from under N30 trillion in 2023 to about N160 trillion today, while the All-Share Index climbed from roughly 52,000 to over 244,000 points. The rally reflects the positive response of investors to recent macroeconomic reforms, while also building on decades of institutional development by market operators, listed companies, regulators and investors. But the more consequential story came afterwards was the president’s affirmation that NNPC Limited will be reformed and listed on the capital market, alongside his endorsement of the market’s role in financing Nigeria’s ambition of becoming a one-trillion-dollar economy.

That a sitting Nigerian president now speaks of the stock exchange as an instrument of national economic strategy, in the same breath as fiscal and monetary policy did not happen by accident. It reflects years of deliberate work by institutions across Nigeria’s capital market ecosystem to reposition the market from a spectator of economic policy to an active participant in national development. Throughout that evolution, Popoola has emerged as one of its most influential advocates and architects, helping to articulate a vision of the capital market not merely as a trading venue, but as infrastructure for national growth.

Consider the record. When the banking sector recapitalisation programme was announced, sceptics predicted overwhelming dependence on foreign capital. Instead, roughly three-quarters of the funds were mobilised domestically, supported by NGX Invest, a market infrastructure that NGX Group and the wider ecosystem had modernised for exactly such moments. When Nigeria migrated to T+1 settlement this June, placing it among the more efficient emerging markets in post-trade settlement, it reflected years of coordinated technical work involving exchanges, regulators, clearing institutions and market participants. When international index providers questioned aspects of the market’s structure, NGX Group’s leadership responded with evidence rather than rhetoric. And when Dangote Petroleum Refinery signalled its intention to list, it reinforced a proposition Popoola has consistently advanced: Nigeria’s largest enterprises should increasingly seek long-term capital from Nigerian markets, allowing more Nigerians to participate in the country’s economic growth.

What distinguishes Popoola’s leadership is its refusal of the adversarial posture that has often characterised relations between African markets and African governments. Exchange leaders have traditionally oscillated between supplication and criticism, either asking governments for concessions or lamenting policy shortcomings. Popoola has helped shape a different approach: partnership not with any particular administration, but with credible economic reform itself. The four priorities presented at the State House; the privatisation and listing of viable government assets, dual listings by leading Nigerian companies, clarity around capital gains tax treatment, and greater use of capital markets to finance infrastructure, were less a list of requests than a proposed division of labour. Government provides policy clarity, assets and reform momentum; the capital market provides capital formation, price discovery, transparency and broad-based ownership.

The NNPC commitment is the first major test of that division of labour, and it is difficult to overstate what it could represent. A listed NNPC would mean audited accounts where opacity has often prevailed, market discipline where political discretion has historically dominated, and perhaps most significantly, an opportunity for millions of Nigerians, directly and through their pension funds to own a stake in one of the country’s most strategic commercial enterprises. It is privatisation not as transfer to a connected few, but as broader public participation. If executed successfully, it could become one of the defining institutional reforms of this era. NGX would provide the platform, while years of investment in settlement systems, market infrastructure, retail participation and institutional capacity would help explain why the market is increasingly prepared for transactions of such scale.

None of this eliminates the difficult questions. Nigeria’s cost-of-living pressures remain real, and rising equity indices do not immediately reduce household expenses, a reality acknowledged by both Popoola and Central Bank Governor Yemi Cardoso. The trillion-dollar economy remains an aspiration requiring sustained growth well beyond recent performance. And the distance between a presidential commitment and a completed listing is one on which many reform programmes have faltered. Yet this is precisely why institutional leadership matters. Commitments become transactions only when there are credible institutions capable of executing them and leaders trusted by policymakers, domestic investors and international capital alike. That institutional credibility built patiently over time may prove to be one of the most valuable assets the Nigerian capital market possesses.

The history of successful reforming economies demonstrates that governments alone do not build vibrant capital markets, nor do capital markets reform governments in isolation. Progress emerges through productive collaboration between credible public policy and strong market institutions. That collaboration must outlast any administration because markets ultimately create wealth through rules, not rulers. The strongest testament to NGX Group’s growing institutional maturity is that its case for deeper capital markets would remain the same regardless of who occupies political office. In Nigeria’s reform moment, Popoola has become one of the principal figures helping to occupy that critical space between policy and capital. The president has now said publicly what many market participants have long believed: if the stock market is doing well, Nigeria’s economy is moving in the right direction. The task now is to ensure that confidence continues to translate into investment, reform into opportunity, and market performance into lasting national prosperity.

· Sowole, a financial expert, is based in Lagos

World.title: UBEC Urges States to Fully Utilise Basic Education Funds
World.content:
* Delta reports 90% implementation of 2025 action plan

Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) has called on states to ensure full utilisation of available funds and prompt implementation of approved programmes to improve basic education delivery across Nigeria.

The call was made during a courtesy visit to the Delta State Government, represented by Deputy Governor, Monday Onyeme, in Asaba, as part of the 30th quarterly meeting of UBEC management with executive chairmen of State Universal Basic Education Boards (SUBEBs).

The meeting, themed, ‘Repositioning Basic Education in Nigeria to Optimise Investment and Impact,’ focused on how investments and innovations can translate into better classrooms and learning outcomes.

UBEC commended Delta State for accessing its UBE matching grants up to 2025.

The commission also urged the state to take advantage of the education component of the World Bank-supported HOPE Education Programme, with up to $500 million earmarked for education.

States were told that to qualify, they must access the 2026 matching grant and implement at least 50 per cent of their 2025 Action Plan.

Responding, Onyeme said updated records showed that Delta had about N1 billion in unutilised funds, contrary to the N8 billion earlier reported.

He added that the state had implemented about 90 per cent of its 2025 Action Plan and had already received its 2026 matching grant.

The UBEC team also highlighted Delta’s technology-driven teacher attendance system, Attend360, as a model that could strengthen accountability in basic education nationwide.

“There is no education or quality learning without a good teacher or without a teacher in the classroom,” the executive secretary noted.

During a visit to the Asagba of Asaba, Prof. Epiphany Azinge, UBEC called for stronger collaboration with traditional institutions.

Azinge described basic education as the foundation of Nigeria’s future and urged UBEC and SUBEBs to ensure no child, including those with disabilities and from disadvantaged backgrounds, is left behind.

UBEC assured the Asagba that it will continue working with states to ensure that investments in basic education yield visible impact in classrooms.

World.title: Industrial Action: Sheathe Your Sword, Exercise Restraint, NCAA Tells Unions
World.content:
Kasim Sumaina in Abuja

The Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) has pleaded with aviation unions to sheathe their sword and exercise restraint in the ongoing industrial action which has impacted passengers and other stakeholders.

The authority noted that the matter would have been addressed at the meeting convened by the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development Festus Keyamo last week, but the meeting could not hold as the airline operators failed to honour the invitation.

NCAA, in a statement on Tuesday by its Director General, Capt. Chris Najomo, stated that the appeal became necessary and will be resolved pending the return of the minister, Keyamo, who has been actively working towards resolving the issues.

Najomo assured the travelling public that flight safety remained uncompromised, adding that the authority would continue to exercise its statutory safety oversight responsibilities.

“We appeal to all parties to embrace dialogue and cooperation. We are confident that the matter will be resolved shortly and normal flight operations will resume as soon as practicable.

“The NCAA regrets the inconvenience caused to passengers and appreciates their patience and understanding,” he said.

World.title: Delta Suspends Works Commissioner over Alleged Assault on Gov’s Aide
World.content:
T6Sylvester Idowu in Warri, Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba

The Delta State Government yesterday suspended the state Commissioner for Works (Highway and Urban Roads), Hon. Izeze Rume Yakubu Reuben, with immediate effect.

The suspension, according to a statement signed by the Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Dr. Kingsley Emu, is to allow security agencies to conduct an impartial investigation into allegations linking the commissioner to the recent assault of the Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Protocol, Mr. Simon Mudi, popularly known as ‘Temple’.

The incident reportedly occurred at the Petroleum Training Institute (PTI), Effurun, in Uvwie Local Government Area of the state during the Delta Central meeting of the All Progressives Congress (APC).

The SSG said the suspension was necessary to ensure that the investigation was conducted without interference and to establish the facts surrounding the incident.

The state government, he said, remained committed to maintaining public safety, law and order, and the sanctity of human lives under all circumstances.

Dr. Emu stressed that the government’s commitment to these principles remained unwavering, even when individuals or institutions of the state were involved.

“The suspension is expected to remain in force pending the outcome of the investigation by the relevant security agencies,” he said.

World.title: NHRC Demands Immediate Arrest, Prosecution of Sheikh Jingir Over Hate Speech
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has called for the immediate arrest and prosecution of prominent Islamic cleric, Sheikh Sani Yahaya Jingir, over what it described as hateful and inciting remarks capable of aggravating religious tensions ahead of the 2027 general election.

The Executive Secretary of the commission, Chief Tony Ojukwu, made the demand after the NHRC reviewed a viral video in which the cleric allegedly canvassed religiously exclusive politics and urged his supporters to obtain their permanent voter cards (PVCs) to “show their limit”.

Ojukwu, who condemned the remarks in strong terms, said the cleric’s reference to people of other faiths as “infidels”, coupled with his political exhortations, constituted a dangerous attempt to mobilise citizens along religious lines.

According to him, the statements amounted to hate speech and incitement to religious hatred, with the potential to trigger violence at a time Nigeria is preparing for another politically sensitive electoral cycle.

The NHRC boss said the remarks were inconsistent with the constitutional principles of equality, non-discrimination and peaceful coexistence, as well as Nigeria’s obligations under international human rights instruments.

“The commission finds these remarks to be hate speech and incitement to religious hatred and potential violence. At a time when we are preparing for another general election, such utterances are reckless and dangerous,” he said.

Ojukwu warned that failure by the authorities to respond decisively could encourage other influential religious and political actors to make increasingly provocative statements as the 2027 elections draw closer.

“We cannot afford to look away. If we fail to speak and act now, we embolden both Christian and Muslim clerics and other influential persons to make worse statements in the coming months. That path leads only to crisis,” he said.

Consequently, the commission called on the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS) and other relevant authorities to immediately arrest and prosecute Jingir for alleged hate speech and incitement.

The NHRC insisted that any prosecution should be pursued irrespective of the cleric’s status or political affiliation, arguing that equal application of the law was necessary to deter others from exploiting religious sentiments for political purposes.

The commission’s intervention comes as political actors, religious leaders and civil society groups increasingly turn their attention to the potential impact of identity-based mobilisation on the 2027 electoral process.

Ojukwu further urged religious leaders, traditional rulers and politicians to abandon divisive rhetoric and instead encourage Nigerians to assess political leaders on the basis of competence, service delivery, integrity and respect for fundamental human rights.

He also called on Nigerians to reject identity politics and resist attempts to turn religious affiliation into a tool for political mobilisation.

“The commission will continue to monitor compliance and will engage with security agencies, INEC, and civil society to ensure that the 2027 elections are free from hate and violence,” he said.

The NHRC’s position adds a fresh dimension to the growing debate over the role of religious rhetoric in Nigeria’s electoral politics, particularly as political parties and prospective candidates begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 polls.

Jingir has previously been involved in controversies surrounding politically charged religious messaging.

In the run-up to the 2019 general election, he attracted criticism over a video message to followers concerning voting and religious identity.

The latest NHRC intervention therefore places renewed focus on the responsibility of influential religious figures to ensure that political mobilisation does not cross the line into rhetoric capable of threatening peaceful coexistence or electoral stability.

World.title: WATCH: Cameron Waldeck-Cooks’ ‘movie-like’ US experience
World.content:
St Stithians learner Cameron Waldeck-Cooks during her school years. A video of the 17-year-old speaking about her exchange in the US has resurfaced following her death. Images: Facebook/St Stithians College and Facebook/Derrick Cooks

A video of Cameron Waldeck-Cooks speaking about her school exchange in the United States has resurfaced following her death.

The 17-year-old St Stithians Girls’ College learner and Ethan Coetzee, 19, were found dead at a lodge in Sabie, Mpumalanga, on 3 August.

Police initially opened an inquest into the deaths.



Preliminary post-mortem findings later indicated that Cameron had been strangled. Police then opened a murder case.

The investigation continues.

The resurfaced interview shows Cameron during an exchange at Holy Innocents’ Episcopal School in Atlanta, Georgia.

Cameron spent time in the US

She travelled to the US through the Round Square connection between Holy Innocents and St Stithians College.

In the interview, Cameron introduces herself as being from Johannesburg and speaks enthusiastically about her time at the school.

Archived footage shows Cameron Waldeck-Cooks during an interview from her time on a foreign exchange program. The footage has resurfaced following the recent tragedy involving Cameron and 19-year-old Ethan Coetzee in Mpumalanga. pic.twitter.com/ZqKjyltLPH  August 10, 2026

She describes Holy Innocents as a “safe and welcoming environment”.

“Everyone is just very friendly and conversational,” Cameron said.

During her stay, she attended Upper School classes, explored Atlanta and experienced everyday American school life.

She also attended three American football matches.

One took place at Holy Innocents, while another took her to the Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta.

Cameron also attended a high school football match, which she compared to something out of an American movie.

“It’s kind of similar to how it is in the movies,” she said.

“You wouldn’t expect it because, I guess, the movies, it’s fantasy, but it’s actually kind of very similar.”

‘Feels like I’m in a movie’

One of Cameron’s favourite memories, however, involved something much simpler.

She recalled driving through Atlanta while listening to music.

“In South Africa, the driving age is 18, and here it’s 16,” she said.

“So driving, like, the city with the big buildings, it feels like I’m in a movie.”

Her comments captured her excitement about experiencing life in another country.

Cameron excelled in sport

Back home, Cameron attended St Stithians Girls’ College in Johannesburg.

She also made her mark as a young sportswoman.

Cameron competed in rowing and athletics and earned recognition for her performances.

In 2025, St Stithians awarded her half colours for athletics.

She also secured a place on the South African Schools Rowing Union U16 development tour to the United Kingdom after finishing third in the U16 scull event.

Cameron continued representing St Stithians in 2026 and competed at the Buffalo Regatta.

Her death has since placed the teenager at the centre of a murder investigation.

The resurfaced US interview now captures Cameron during another chapter of her life – exploring a new city, embracing a different culture and speaking excitedly about the experiences she was having abroad.

World.title: Orlando Pirates latest news: Makgopa, Sibisi, Matuludi, Appollis
World.content:
Orlando Pirates have made a strong start to the new season, winning their opening two matches across all competitions.

The Buccaneers began their campaign with a narrow 1-0 victory over Milford before being pushed all the way by Durban City in the MTN8 quarter-finals this past weekend.

Abdeslam Ouaddou’s side eventually secured a 2-1 victory after extra-time to book their place in the semi-finals.



With momentum on their side, Pirates now turn their attention back to the Betway Premiership when they face AmaZulu in midweek.

Orlando Pirates have a few injury concerns

Ouaddou will have to contend with injury concerns within his squad. Striker Evidence Makgopa is set for a spell on the sidelines after suffering an ankle injury in training. The forward could be out for up to six weeks.

There is also uncertainty surrounding defender Thabiso Sesane after the centre-back was substituted during Pirates’ 2-1 win over Durban City.

Ouaddou confirmed after the match that the player had an injury concern, although the full extent of the problem is not yet known.

Meanwhile, Orlando Pirates have been busy in the transfer market and have already completed nine signings ahead of the new season.

One player who has been linked with a move to Mayfair is Polokwane City right-back Thabang Matuludi. The interest would make sense given the departures of two right-backs from the Pirates squad, leaving the club potentially looking to strengthen that position.



For now, however, Matuludi remains a Polokwane City player but there’s no doubt that the Buccaneers are looking at a last-minute deal.

With the transfer window set to close next month, Orlando Pirates still have time to make further additions to Ouaddou’s squad as they look to compete on multiple fronts this season.

On Wednesday, the Buccaneers play AmaZulu away, looking to get their third win in a row. Oswin Appollis, who hasn’t set the season alight, will look to regain his form.
